title: TunePID sampled |S| check misses sharp resonant peaks
body: pidTuningSensitivityPeak steps 1% log + pi/(16 tau); misses narrow peaks. Repro: 1/(s^2+0.05s+1) e^{-s}, PD default -> sampled 3.89, dense |S|=4.11 at w=1.019; PDF dense 4.20. Found reviewing PR #342.

title: TunePID search misses feasible PID designs under |S|<=4
body: Search follows best design ignoring |S| bound. Repro: 1/(s+1)^2 e^{-3s}, PID default -> error; brute force at wc=0.349 finds Kp=1.03 Ki=0.257 Kd=0.85 |S|=3.43. Also errors on f7f60ac. Found reviewing PR #342.

title: TunePID PD/PDF default errors on first-order plants (PM target vs floor)
body: TunePID treats PM as target +-3deg; MATLAB as floor. 1/(s+1) PD and 1/(s+10) PD/PDF default -> ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable; MATLAB returns positive design. Discrete 0.1/(z-0.9) PDF also errors.

title: Slow refusals on mixed-class delay sets in HinfNorm
body: levelBelow retries 16 levels within 2^21 budget then distinctDelays fresh 2^21: some refusals 250-500ms vs ~2ms on f7f60ac. hinfnorm_delay.go peak().

title: HinfNorm reports (lim,+Inf) when finite peak lies beyond scan span
body: peak() scans to R0+max(R0,2P); per-passage maxima can rise above lim later. Repro: feedthroughDifferenceLoop k=[1 2], tau=(0.5411,1.082): returns 4.46591@Inf, true 4.468029@w=95.95. Same on f7f60ac. hinfnorm_delay.go peak().

title: Pidtune has no sign/stability screen
body: Pidtune(-e^{-s}/(s+1), PI) returns positive gains -> unstable loop, L(0)=-1.41. Predates PR #342.

data.title: Pidtune default crossover gives unstable designs; should back off wc as MATLAB
data.body:
After XYTCJ7 (branch fix/pidtune-screen) Pidtune rejects certifiably unstable designs with ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable. Before that it silently returned them. At default wc=0 (no explicit wc), MATLAB pidtune returns a stable design for these stable plants; Pidtune now errors:
- I: 1/(s^2+0.4s+1), 1/(s+1)^4, e^{-s}/(s+1), e^{-2s}/(s+1)^3
- NMP (1-s)/(s^2+3s+2): PD, PDF, PID (ideal, Kd>1 makes char leading coeff 1-Kd<0), PIDF
- discrete 0.1/(z-0.9), (0.01z+0.009)/(z^2-1.7z+0.72) Dt=0.1 (also with 3-sample delay): PD — forward-Euler derivative with Tf=Td/10 < Dt makes the controller filter pole leave the unit circle (|1-Dt/Tf|>1). Consider BackwardEuler for discrete PD/PDF as already done for PID.
Fix idea: when the closed-loop screen fails at the automatic crossover, lower wc (or use TunePID's search) until a stable design meets PM. Files: pidtune.go (findCrossoverFreq, computePD, checkPidtuneStability).

data.title: Pidtune/TunePID gain sign for integrating and unstable plants
data.body: pidTuningDCSign returns 0 for unstable/integrating plants, so Pidtune keeps positive gains. E.g. Pidtune(-1/(s(s+1)), P/PI/PD/PID, 0) and Pidtune(-1/(s-1), P, 0), discrete -0.1/(z-1) now return ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable (closed loop unstable) where MATLAB pidtune returns negative-gain stabilizing designs. Need a sign rule for these plants (e.g. sign of the low-frequency gain after removing integrators / high-frequency gain), shared by Pidtune and TunePID (pid_tuning.go pidTuningDCSign). Found while doing XYTCJ7 (branch fix/pidtune-screen).

data.title: HinfNorm errors when levelBelow cannot separate sup|G∞| from grid peak (k=[1 3])
data.body:
Repro: feedthroughDifferenceLoop (hinfnorm_delay_commensurate_test.go) with d22~U(+-0.8), d12,d21~U(+-1) from rand.NewPCG(i+1000,7) (order d22[4], d12[2], d21[2], then x), h=0.02+0.3x, tau=(k0 h, k1 h). k=[1 3]: ~37 of 200 seeds (e.g. i=8,13,15) stable yet HinfNorm errors 'gain may peak as w -> Inf through a delayed feedthrough' (ErrDelayUnsupported); also k=[1 1] i=97, k=[2 1] i=158.
Source: hinfnorm_delay.go peak(): hf.levelBelow(est, best) fails (budget or torus bound) and est <= best*(1+tol), so default case errors. Same on 493431c (before VFUTSC fix). Likely when sup|G_inf| ~ best grid peak so no level in (est,best) certifies; for dim=1 could take lim=est when est<=best (finite peak dominates) instead of erroring.

data.title: HinfNorm delay: finite-vs-Inf verdict for MIMO and multi-class delays
data.body:
After VFUTSC, hinfnorm_delay.go peakPastLimit decides finite-vs-+Inf via highFrequencyExpansion (hinfnorm_delay_expansion.go) only for vector gains (p=1 or m=1), n>0, one commensurate delay class (hf.dim==1). MIMO gains and several delay classes keep the old heuristic: scan to R0+max(R0,2P) and report (lim,+Inf) if no sample exceeds lim, which misses finite peaks above lim further out (same mechanism as VFUTSC).
Needed: MIMO expansion via top singular pair (sigma' = Re u^H G1 v, second order with gap), and torus version for dim>1.

data.title: TunePID default PI/PID/PIDF unattainable on lightly damped delayed plant
data.body:
Repro: plant 1/(s^2+0.05s+1) with InputDelay 1; TunePID(ctx, p, PidtunePI|PidtunePID|PidtunePIDF, PIDTuningOptions{}) -> ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable. Same at 493431c and on fix/pid-wave2 (974b6c8); PD/PDF succeed.
Cause (likely): default wc is the delay cap (180-PM)/(2tau)=0.995, right at the zeta=0.025 resonance (|G|=20); no I-containing design meets PM 60+-3 with |S|<=4 there, and the moved-crossover ladder only applies to PD/PDF. MATLAB pidtune returns a stable (low-bandwidth) PI/PID for this plant.
Fix idea: when the default-wc search fails |S|<=4 for I-families, back off wc (e.g. below the resonance, |L(j w0)| < 1-1/4) as the PD ladder does. Files: pid_tuning.go (TunePID tuneAt/withFloor, moved crossover ladder).

data.title: hinfnorm delay: close tail of finite peak just above ω→∞ limit via HF expansion (slow/refused)
data.body:
On fix/hinf-delay-wave2 (VFUTSC), when limitVerdict finds finite peaks above lim = sup|G∞|, peak() closes the tail with tailGain(lim, R) <= best(1+tol). best exceeds lim only by ~a/(lim·ω), so R grows huge: long grid scans + certify (1.2 s), or "delay grid exceeds 2097152 points" refusal where base returned a (wrong) +Inf answer.

Repro (feedthroughDifferenceLoop in hinfnorm_delay_commensurate_test.go, tau = [h, k·h], k = [1, k]):
1) slow, k=2: HinfNorm = 7.13752092873 @ w=214.93 in ~1.2 s (base 0.8 ms, wrong 7.137207 @Inf). Values from sweep PCG(2,2) i=18 (regenerate: d22=u(.8)x4, d12=u(3)x2, d21=u(3)x2, h=0.05+0.5r, u(s)=s(2r-1)).
2) refusal, k=10: d22=[-0.3254482799038851 -0.75709048215094 0.3115000957820588 0.13057003133380257] d12=[-1.6500914093149874 2.855751898651099] d21=[1.7403784630902759 2.120490655864659] h=0.1340669528810582. Branch: "delay grid exceeds 2097152 points". Dense oracle: lim=12.0862085728, max over [20,2020] = 12.0862089938 near ω≈2013 (still rising) so the true peak is finite; base returned 12.0862085826@Inf (wrong).

Idea: reuse highFrequencyExpansion (hinfnorm_delay_expansion.go): for t <= T, sup_φ model(t) + remainder <= best certifies ω >= 1/T, same as holds() in limitVerdict with level best; take R = min(tailGain R, 1/T). Also the doubling search for the first sample above lim could start near the predicted peak ω.

data.title: hinfnorm delay: HF expansion for several delay classes and matrix kappa
data.body: VFUTSC follow-up (fix/hinf-delay-wave2). newHighFrequencyExpansion (hinfnorm_delay_expansion.go) returns nil when hf.dim > 1 (several delay classes), so peakPastLimit falls back to the R0+max(R0,2P) scan and may report lim@+Inf while a finite peak above lim lies further out. Also for matrix gains (p>1,m>1) limitVerdict returns undecided when a = 0 at every maximiser of sigma_max(G_inf) (phi* = 0 or pi; kappa not formed for sigma_max) and modelMaxOver/tailBelow are not available (no polynomial in t), so such cases use the old scan and tailGain only. Repro idea: matrix gain U*diag(G,d)*V from limitAtInfCases 'limit' (phi*=pi) -> limitVerdict undecided; incommensurate tau with finite peak past grid end. Fix: kappa via eigen-perturbation of g0^H g0 (or 5-pt FD in t on sigma_max^2); torus version of the expansion for dim>1.

data.title: TunePID failures still ~1.3-3x slower than 493431c: ±3°/ladder |S| incumbent search (76WSAZ)
data.body:
After fix/pid-wave2 af30b0a (floor budget/early stop), failing TunePID calls remain slower than base 493431c, outside the floor.
Repro: 1/(s+10)e^{-0.3s}, PDF, default opts -> ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable. base 1.0 s, branch HEAD 974b6c8 3.7 s, af30b0a 3.0 s.
pprof af30b0a: TunePID 1.40 s CPU, tunePIDFloor only 0.15 s; rest is pidTuningDelayStability -> delayLoop.nyquist in the ±3° attempt and moved-crossover ladder.
Cause: 075978d (76WSAZ) ranks incumbent by |S| excess, so ladder searches whose candidates are stable but |S|>4 run ~120 Nyquist checks each (base rejected via j >= bestScore before the stability check).
Corpus (4032 cases: 13 plants incl. delays 0/.3/1/3 and discrete, 7 families, PM 0/45/75, wc 0/1, MaxEvaluations 0/300): failing-case time base 121 s, 974b6c8 317-356 s, af30b0a 157-165 s.
Idea: cheap |S| pre-screen before the Nyquist check once an incumbent with lower excess exists, or check stability only for candidates that would become incumbent.

data.title: HinfNorm delay: duplicated lightly damped channel declared unstable (+Inf)
data.body: Repro (base 493431c and fix/hinf-delay-wave2 alike): SISO delay loop a=-1.4666973867074775, b1=?, b2*c2=-2.2697439281287144, d22=-0.44819513831474195, h=0.8637187571421795 (generated by math/rand seed 63 in probe: a=-1-3U, b1=0.3N, b2,c2,c1=N, d11,d12,d21=N, d22=(0.2+0.7U)*sign(N), h=0.1+U; NewFromSlices(1,2,2,[a],[b1,b2],[c1,c2],[d11,d12,d21,d22]); SetDelayModel(H,[h])). HinfNorm(SISO) = 707.6342828515 @ 2.8446883 (correct: closed-loop root -0.0027828+2.8446939j by Newton on (s-a)(1-d22 e^{-sh}) - b2c2 e^{-sh}, stable). Block-diagonal 2x2 duplicate of the same channel (A=diag(a,a), delays [h,h], channel 2 identical or scaled by 1-1e-9) gives HinfNorm = (+Inf, +Inf, nil), i.e. declared unstable. Closed-loop roots are the SISO ones doubled; Nyquist/stability count likely mishandles a double root pair near the axis. 1/300 random seeds; others match exactly. Files: hinfnorm_delay.go (stability/nyquist), delay nyquist code.

data.title: delayLoop Nyquist check takes ~600 ms on wide-span PD loops (TunePID floor)
data.body: Repro: plant -31.29(s+0.09685)/(s(s^2+14.84s+367.9)(s^2+7.963s+36.18)) e^-0.5042s, TunePID PD PhaseMargin 36.78 on 0e7ab25 (fix/pid-wave2 before its review fixes): floor bands 78.78 and 84.78 spend 33 s and 17.5 s on ~55 stability checks each (~600 ms per check) vs ~0.1 ms per check in earlier bands. pprof (reviewer): 87.5% in pidTuningDelayStability -> delayLoop.stableClosedLoop -> nyquistGrid/refine (delay_nyquist.go:345, :556). Candidates there are PD with Kp~-1, Kd~8 and a 0 dB crossing near 2e-4 rad/s, so the grid spans many decades. fix/pid-wave2 now stops the floor before those bands, so TunePID no longer hits it, but any caller of the delay Nyquist check on such loops can. Expect: bounded per-check cost (e.g. grid sized by loop features, not span).

data.title: TunePID non-floor crossover scan misses crossover pair at lightly damped resonance (margin < PM-3)
data.body:
Repro: plant 0.05372(s+0.7974)/((s+0.779)(s+0.101)(s^2+0.03714s+10.61)) (makePlant), TunePID PDF, default opts. Moved crossover 3.253 rad/s (robust ladder). Result Kp=5.1135 Kd=1.6582 Tf=0.002603; Evidence.GainCrossovers=[3.2535], PhaseMargins=[59.34].
Independent dense sweep (pidLoopMargins 1e-4..1e4): margins [59.34, 37.18] -> second 0 dB crossing near the 3.257 rad/s resonance (zeta 0.0057) at 37° < PM-3 = 57°, inside [wc/100, 100wc], not reported.
Same at base 493431c (design Kp=5.3539 Kd=1.5935 Tf=0.0010316 via TF StateSpace realisation: margins [57.07, 34.89]) and on fix/pid-wave2 0822145; similar on -0.0503(s-9.178)/((s^2+0.06089s+1.043)(s+0.0589)(s+6.552))e^-0.0301s PD default (dense [61.6, 37.6]).
Cause: pidTuningCrossings outside the floor keeps the 241-point grid scan verbatim (pid_tuning.go, "Outside the floor the scan is kept verbatim"); a crossover pair between samples at a resonance is stepped over. The floor path already uses pidTuningCrossGrid + golden refinement of |L| extrema.
Expect: margin check finds every crossing in the band (apply the floor's mode-refined grid/extremum refinement to all searches), accepting design changes.

data.title: delay Nyquist: rationalTailBound uses unbalanced ||A||, wide grids for companion loops (margin/hinfnorm)
data.body:
rationalTailBound (delay_nyquist.go:140) bounds |L(s)| with ||c|| ||b||/(w-||A||_2) in the given realization, so for a companion-form loop (e.g. TF->StateSpace of -31.29(s+0.09685)/(s(s^2+14.84s+367.9)(s^2+7.963s+36.18)) e^-0.5042s, ||A||_2=1.38e4 vs max|pole|=19.2, balanced ||A||_2=41) the tail is +Inf below ||A|| and the linear pi/(8 tau) delay grid of nyquistLinearTo / grid end R extend past 1.4e4 rad/s: ~18k points per Nyquist pass where |L|<0.3 beyond ~50 rad/s.
Affects delayLoopFromSystem callers: margin.go:680 sensitivityPeaks (DiskMargin/AllMargin delay path), hinfnorm_delay.go nyquist.
C76S2F fixed this only for the TunePID screen (pidMarkovTail takes min over given and balanced realization, pid_tuning.go).
Suggested fix: for nd==0 also bound in newBalancedRealization coordinates (Markov invariant, radix-2 scaling exact) and take the min; for LFT internal delays balance (A,[B B2],[C;C2]) jointly. Grid changes (R, w1 shrink) alter sensitivity-peak grids, so check peak values stay within peakCertTol vs base on a randomized sweep.

data.title: TunePID PI unattainable on 1/(s(s+1)) and 1/(s-1) where Pidtune PI succeeds
data.body: TunePID(ctx, G, PI, {}) returns ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable for G=1/(s(s+1)) and G=1/(s-1) (both signs), while Pidtune PI succeeds (e.g. 1/(s(s+1)): Kp=0.9988 Ki=0.0393; 1/(s-1): Kp=1.4108 Ki=0.0704) and TunePID PID succeeds. Pre-existing at 15ca52c; found during YVAIMU (branch fix/pidtune-wave3). Files: pid_tuning.go (TunePID/tunePIDFloor).

data.title: pidTuningIdealStable accepts ideal-D loops with 1+L(inf)<0 (near ill-posed)
data.body: pidTuningIdealStable (pid_tuning.go) accepts continuous ideal-derivative (Tf=0) designs whose closed-loop characteristic leading coefficient flips sign, i.e. 1+L(inf) = 1 + k*Kd < 0 with |1+k*Kd| tiny. Repro at 15ca52c: Pidtune(-2.03/s, PID, 0, nil) returned Kp=0.04998 Ki=0.02029 Kd=0.49706 Tf=0: char = (1-2.03*0.497)s^2 - 0.101s - 0.041 = -0.009 s^2 - ..., polynomially Hurwitz but near ill-posed (|S(inf)| ~ 100, positive feedback at HF). Same for -1.83/s, -0.18/s, and -0.732(s+.108)(s+.617)/((s-.284)((s-.73)^2+8.35^2)) PID. YVAIMU's sign fix replaces these Pidtune designs incidentally, but the screen (also used by TunePID) should reject or flag designs with 1+D_L(inf) near/below 0 for ideal D on relative-degree-1 plants. Found during YVAIMU (branch fix/pidtune-wave3).

data.title: Pidtune PDF errors when needed phase is lag (no phase clamp like PD)
data.body:
Pidtune(G, PDF, wc, nil) returns ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable ("requested phase is unattainable by a same-sign PDF") whenever the controller phase phiC = -180+PM-argG is outside the PDF range, e.g. lag plants where phiC ~ -120 deg. computePD clamps phiC into (0, 90 deg); the PDF branch in computePIDGainsPositive (pidtune.go, pidtuneFamily case PidtunePDF) does not, so no wc works and the Q7GUKL back-off cannot help.
Repro (fix/pidtune-wave3): discrete 0.1/(z-0.9) Dt=0.1, and (0.01z+0.009)/(z^2-1.7z+0.72) Dt=0.1, Pidtune(...,PDF,0,nil) -> unattainable at every wc. Same at wc=2 for many random discrete plants.
MATLAB pidtune returns a PDF (small Kd) for such plants. Fix idea: clamp phiC to PDF's reachable range at wc as computePD does (best-effort when PM not explicit).

data.title: Pidtune backed-off designs can have poor gain margin (Ms 7-12)
data.body:
After Q7GUKL (fix/pidtune-wave3) Pidtune at wc=0 lowers the crossover until the closed loop is stable and PM >= target at every gain crossover. Gain margin / sensitivity peak is not gated, so some accepted designs are fragile:
- I on 1/(s^2+0.4s+1): Ki=0.358, PM 78 deg, Ms ~10 (|L(j1)|~0.89 at -180 deg)
- (1-s)/(s^2+3s+2): PD Ms 3.7, PDF Ms 7.2, PID (ideal, Kd~0.86 -> HF |L|->Kd) Ms 7.0, PIDF Ms 11.7
Measured by pidtuneLoopMargin in pidtune_backoff_test.go (TestPidtuneAutoCrossoverBacksOffToStable logs PM/Ms).
MATLAB pidtune balances robustness too (would likely pick lower wc / smaller Kd). Consider adding a GM or Ms bound to the back-off acceptance (pidtune.go pidtuneLoopGrid) and comparing against MATLAB outputs.

data.title: TunePID I family: infeasible PM reported as ErrOverflow
data.body:
TunePID returns ErrOverflow ("objective overflows; rescale plant units") instead of ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable for I-family designs whose phase target is geometrically infeasible.
Repro (continuous, no delay, MaxEvaluations 0 or 300): TunePID(1/s, PidtuneI, {PhaseMargin:45}) and PM 75, wc 0 or 1; 1/(s^2+.2s+1) I PM 45/75 wc 1; -1/(s+1)^2 I PM 45 wc 1.
Count on 7392-case grid: 10 at 493431c, 14 at 15ca52c/fix/tunepid-wave3 (pre-existing; QZIL4R change leaves it identical).
Likely: seed controller for I at wc is degenerate/normalized gain non-finite so components() overflows before any search; should be a PIDTuningError (target unattainable) not overflow.
Files: pid_tuning.go tunePID (norms check after pidTuningSolveWeights).

data.title: HinfNorm: torus limit for near-commensurate float delays (fl(k*h) != k*h) unsupported; decide semantics / orbit-density certificate
data.body:
From OUWA5P investigation (track hinf, branch fix/hinf-wave3).
OUWA5P repro failures occur only when fl(k1*h) != k1*h exactly (k=[1 3],[3 1],[2 3]): commensurateMultiples rejects, dim=2 torus, error from torusPastLimit (exits: !risesPast 36, below fails 4, span exhausted 45 over k=[1 3],[3 1],[2 3] x 200 seeds), not peak() default.
Every failing seed: dense 2-D torus sup of G_inf > finite dense oracle peak (e.g. i=8 k=[1 3]: torus 2.720 vs finite 1.583; i=153: 2.3283 vs 2.3278). Literal-float norm is the torus sup, approached at omega ~ 1/|fl(3h)-3h| ~ 1e15; intended-commensurate norm is the finite peak. Dyadic h (exact multiples): 0 failures, values match oracle (finite peaks beyond oracle wmax verified attained).
Possible design: tau ratio is an exact rational p/q; orbit of phases is pi*K/q-dense on the 2-torus, so limsup = torus sup within lip*pi*K/q when q huge -> report at w=+Inf, with a tail certificate along the near-commensurate line for w up to ~gap^-1(tol*lim). dim=2 only; reverses the documented torusPastLimit stance. Needs owner decision on semantics (literal floats vs intended commensurate).

data.title: TunePID PD: ladder rungs never try the floor; resonant plant fails though a sound design exists
data.body:
Plant -0.0503(s-9.178)/((s^2+0.06089s+1.043)(s+0.0589)(s+6.552))e^-0.0301s, TunePID PD default opts.
After PXJTBU (fix/tunepid-wave3 84787f0) TunePID returns ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable; base 15ca52c returned Kp=0.4687 Kd=0.7836 at the 1.0137 rad/s ladder rung whose dense margins are [60.0, 36.25] (hidden 36 deg crossing), so the error is a corrected unsound value.
Default wc0=0.0332 fails PD 60+-3; ladder rungs 0.973/0.992/1.004/1.0137 (lead 15..60) all sit on the rising flank of the zeta=0.03 resonance at 1.021, where any crossover's partner crossing just above the peak has PM < 57; floor runs only at wc0 (withFloor(wc0,...)), never at ladder rungs.
Independent brute force (Kp,Kd in [0,4] step 0.02, dense margins + winding): sound PD designs exist, e.g. Kp=0.10 Kd=0.90: crossings 1.0146 (82.6 deg) and 1.0264 (60.5 deg), |S|max 2.2; all lie in a ~1% pocket at the resonance.
Options: run the floor at the last feasible ladder rung, or move the ladder to the falling flank / below the resonance. Files: pid_tuning.go TunePID ladder (pidTuningPhaseCrossing loop), withFloor.

data.title: delay Nyquist refine: certified phase-variation bound per span (replace sampling heuristic)
data.body:
delayLoop.refine (delay_nyquist.go) accepts a span on endpoint phase step <= pi/4 plus, since YA5BBE (fix/hinf-wave3 54aad90), a near-origin (|1+L| < 0.5) modulus-ratio/midpoint rule. Both are sampling heuristics: a near-axis zero of even multiplicity (or several close zeros) with |1+L| >= 0.5 at the samples, or a fast-varying L, can still alias a 2*pi phase turn and miscount the winding (stable declared unstable or vice versa).
Certified route: bound |d/dw (1+L(jw))| per span (resolvent bound on (jwI-A)^-1, |d/dw e^{-jw tau}| = tau, LFT/det derivative bound) and accept only when min |1+L| over the span is provably > 0 with phase variation <= pi/4.
Evidence: YA5BBE repro (hinfnorm_delay_duplicate_test.go) fixed by heuristic only. Cost of heuristic: HinfNorm_DelaySharpLimit +6-8% vs bc8850c.

data.title: delay nyquist: high-multiplicity near-axis root trips absolute 1e-12 floor -> stable model reported unstable (+Inf)
data.body:
Found reviewing fix/hinf-wave3 (YA5BBE follow-up). Pre-existing on base 15ca52c and on 54aad90.

Repro: SISO delay loop p (a=-0.2-3U, b1=0.3N, b2=N*exp(g*U), c1,c2,d11,d12,d21=N, d22=(0.2+0.7U)*sign, h=0.1+2U; math/rand/v2 PCG(seed,4242), draw order as listed; NewFromSlices(1,2,2,...), SetDelayModel(H,[h])). Build r-fold block-diagonal replica (A=a*I_r, delays [h]*r, same channel per block, as hinfnorm_delay_duplicate_test.go duplicate() generalised). HinfNorm(SISO) finite & correct; r=6 replica gives (+Inf,+Inf,nil).
Failing (g,seed): (0,1916) (0,530) (3,274) (3,1423) (3,1530) (3,545) (3,1012); 7/4000 at r=6; r=2,4 all pass on 54aad90; r=3 base fails 1530,545.
Mechanism: e.stability() returns axisRoot=true (roots=0) at the near-axis root, e.g. seed 1916 closed-loop root -0.00324 (real), seed 530 -0.00163+2.1045j. 1+L = (1+L1)^6, so |1+L| near the root ~ (delta*|L1'|)^6 ~ 1e-18 < 1e-12 absolute floor of resolvedNonzero (delay_nyquist.go) -> refineAxisRoot -> declared unstable. Absolute floor on a quantity scaling as power of multiplicity; also nearOriginLevel=0.5 is absolute.
Files: delay_nyquist.go refine/resolvedNonzero/nearOrigin; hinfnorm_delay.go stability.

data.title: Pidtune auto wc too high for integrator + slow double pole; P/PI fail at wc=0
data.body: Repro (branch fix/pidtune-wave3, after YVAIMU fix 728798b): G=(0.1z+0.05)/((z-1)(z-0.999)^2), Dt=0.1 (TransferFunc.StateSpace). Pidtune(G,P,0) and Pidtune(G,PI,0) return ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable for both G and -G (symmetric, not a sign bug); PID works. findCrossoverFreq picks wc=5.32 rad/s, but the double pole at z=0.999 (~0.01 rad/s) needs wc<=~1e-3: explicit wc=1e-3 gives stable P/PI designs. Back-off only lowers 3 decades (floor 5.3e-3), not enough. MATLAB pidtune returns a design. Likely fix: crossover choice should account for slow poles/integrators (phase-based wc), or extend back-off floor relative to plant dynamics. Files: pidtune.go findCrossoverFreq/plantCrossoverFreq, pidtuneBackoffSteps. Test: pidtune_sign_test.go TestPidtuneNearIntegratorMirrors uses this plant at wc=1e-3.

data.title: Pidtune back-off: cut cost of screen-bound failing steps (closedLoopPoles allocs / certified pre-screen)
data.body: After Q7GUKL wave3 (250ce9d) gate-bound failing auto-wc calls are 2.7x faster (BenchmarkPidtune_BackoffFail/GateP 8.4->3.1 ms), but screen-bound failures (every back-off step closed-loop unstable, e.g. BenchmarkPidtune_BackoffFail/ScreenI: I on 1/((s-2)(s+1)), ~0.6 ms vs ~15 us for one design) still cost ~61 designs. Per step: computePIDGains (evalPlantAt->FreqResponse allocs), PID.System + Feedback + eig in pidStabilityScreen.closedLoopPoles (~130 allocs/step), doubled by the mirror for forced/guessed signs. Coarse-then-refine and U-run early stop are NOT exact: randomized corpus (150 plants x 7 families) has success windows of width 1-2 after long unstable runs (e.g. U46 then OK@59), so they would turn successes into failures. Options: (a) allocation cuts in closedLoopPoles (reuse buffers, build closed-loop A directly) keeping eigenvalues bit-identical; (b) certified-instability pre-screen from characteristic polynomial (cached rational TF) used only when it agrees with IsStable tolerance; (c) evaluate plant at wc via sisoEval in computePIDGains if bit-identical. Verify with byte-identical design dump over a randomized corpus.

data.title: pidtune: delay Nyquist screen accepts PI integrator cancelling plant zero at s=0
data.body:
Repro (base 15ca52c and fix/pidtune-wave3): G = s e^{-0.5s}/((s+1e-8)(s+1)) (TransferFunc num [1 0], den [1 1.00000001 1e-8], SetInputDelay 0.5). Pidtune(G, PI, 1, nil) returns Kp=0.976 Ki=1.023. C's integrator cancels G's zero at s=0, so r->u has an uncancelled pole at s=0 (not asymptotically stable).
The delay-free plant (same num/den, no delay) is rejected: 'PI design at wc=1 gives an unstable closed loop'. With delay, eps>=1e-6 is rejected too, but eps<=1e-7 is accepted, so the continuous-delay Nyquist screen (pidTuningDelayStabilityBudget, pid_tuning.go: l.addAxisPole(0,1) when Ki!=0) misses a controller pole cancelled by a plant zero at the origin.
fix/pidtune-wave3 (728798b, near-integrator rule) also mirrors this to -G (num [-1 0]): base errors there, the branch returns Kp=-0.976 Ki=-1.023.
Also affects ideal PID (Tf=0), e.g. wc=3. Files: pid_tuning.go (delay screen), pidtune.go.

data.title: TunePID back-off: isolated deep-depth floor failure (PI, RHP zero) while neighbours succeed
data.body: TunePID PI back-off: on num=[-184.15361912744427 35.680543192821474] den=[1 4.558547394863393 3.2717623475043296 14.23672605433042] tau=1.0816929318008033 (input delay), default opts, PI, the back-off depth j=20 (wc0*2^-10 ~ 9.45e-4 rad/s) fails with 'gain of sign opposite to DC gain' while j=19 and j=21..24 all succeed; independent of floorRungs (1,2,3,30 same). TunePID PI back-off: on num=[-184.15361912744427 35.680543192821474] den=[1 4.558547394863393 3.2717623475043296 14.23672605433042] tau=1.0816929318008033 (input delay), default opts, PI: back-off depth j=20 (wc0*2^-10 ~ 9.45e-4 rad/s) fails with 'gain of sign opposite to the stable plant's DC gain' while j=19 and j=21..24 all succeed; independent of floorRungs (1,2,3,30 same). data.title: hinfnorm torus: certify exhausts 2M-sample budget (~5 s) on ridge 2x2 τ=(h,√2h) models where base gave up in 1 ms
data.body:
Found while fixing the torusPastLimit give-up cost on fix/hinf-wave3 (commit 03f0d91). Out of scope there (certify path, not torusPastLimit).

Repro (2x2 lftCase, hinfnorm_delay_matrix_test.go lftCase.system, τ = (h, √2·h)):
  rng := rand.New(rand.NewPCG(uint64(i+5000), 11)) // math/rand/v2, i = 115 or 153
  u := func(a float64) float64 { return a * (2*rng.Float64() - 1) }
  v(n, a) = n draws of u(a)
  a := v(4,1); a[0] -= 2; a[3] -= 2
  h := 0.05 + 0.4*rng.Float64()
  c := lftCase{n:2, a:a, b1:v(4,1), b2:v(4,1), c1:v(4,1), c2:v(4,0.3), d11:v(4,1), d12:v(4,2), d21:v(4,2), d22:v(4,0.6)}
  c.h, c.k = h, math.Sqrt2
  c.d12 = {d12[0], 0, d12[2], 0}; c.d22 = {d22[0], 0, d22[2], d22[3]}   // G∞ independent of phase 2: ridge
Evidence: HinfNorm on base 15ca52c -> "gain may peak as ω → ∞ through a delayed feedthrough" in ~1 ms;

data.title: hinfnorm torus: tail closing fails after finite peak just above torus limit (grid exceeds budget)
data.body:
Found on fix/torus-wave4 (M2FKRH). After torusPastLimit/torusRisesPast finds a finite sample barely above the torus limit (excess ~1e-5..1e-4 rel), peak() tail-closing loop needs tailGain(lim,R) <= best*(1+tol); dim>1 has no highFrequencyExpansion (newHighFrequencyExpansion nil), so hfx.tailBelow is unavailable and R runs past span -> 'delay grid exceeds 2097152 points'.

data.title: hinfNormDelayed peak grid/tailGain use given-realization ||A||_2 (companion forms)
data.body:
Follow-up of CGE3HF (branch fix/nyquist-wave4, 5c90bf7). That fix bounds the delay tail in balanced coordinates for delayLoopFromSystem and the delayLFT *stability* loop (delayLFT.balancedTail, hinfnorm_delay.go). The H-inf peak path still uses e.normA of the given realization: delayLFT.resolvent / h / tailGain and R0 := max(hi, 2*e.normA+1) (hinfnorm_delay.go ~1263, ~1337), and the axisOnly loop of linfNormDelayed.

Repro 1: q := companionDelayQuasiLoop(-0.3) (delay_nyquist_tail_test.go); cl := Feedback(q.system(t), 1, -1); stability grid now 627 pts (base 32037) but HinfNorm(cl) regrows the grid toward ||A||_2 = 1.38e4 (balanced 41); HinfNorm time unchanged ~40ms.
Repro 2 (error): companion realization (quasiLoop.system) of num=0.05*[4.35518229454678e+06 7.216831436462314e+06], den=[1 155.944003732878 9955.032050307716 303390.20384392294 3.7420871694087246e+06], tau=0.1821465736750913; cl = Feedback(sys, 1, -1). internalDelayStable(cl)=true (oracle RHP roots 0), HinfNorm(cl) -> "delay grid exceeds 2097152 points: peak gain outside the certified delay scope". data.title: pidStabilityScreen false-unstable for PI with tiny Ki on clustered near-integrator poles
data.body: Plant G=(0.1z+0.05)/((z-1)(z-0.999)^2), Dt=0.1 (TransferFunc.StateSpace). Explicit Pidtune(G,PI,wc,nil) at wc=5.32e-5, 2.99e-5, 1.68e-5, 5.32e-6 returns ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable 'gives an unstable closed loop' (pidStabilityScreen / checkPidtuneStability in pid_tuning.go), yet the same pidtuneGains designs (Kp~3e-11..3e-12, Ki~1e-15..1e-17) are stable by an exact big.Rat Schur-Cohn test of den*denC+num*numC (helper pidtuneExactSchurStable in pidtune_backoff_test.go on branch fix/pidtune-wave4, commit 4bcc8ef). wc=3e-4,1.68e-4,9.46e-5 pass both. Likely float closed-loop pole computation on 4 clustered roots near z=1 (error ~eps^(1/4)). Impact: spurious ErrUnattainable at explicit low wc; auto back-off could skip valid designs. Found while fixing X5LHXA; not fixed (pid_tuning.go out of track scope).

data.title: TunePID free I errors on lightly damped 2nd-order plants (needs slow-integrator wc)
data.body:
Found while fixing WDBBJB (branch fix/tunepid-wave4, 450542e). Pre-existing at base; not a regression.
Repro: TunePID(plant num {-1.054599885306892}, den {1, 0.00299557580140128, 1.0733714787112956}, PidtuneI, PIDTuningOptions{}) -> ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable.
Cause: under I the Nyquist circle of k/(s^2+as+b) rotates -90 deg, so the peak |L| sits at -180 deg; the -120 deg unit-loop point just below wn has |L|>1 through -180 -> unstable/|S| huge. tuneOneGain's move to the lowest 60-deg phase point therefore fails. Only robust I design is a very slow integrator (|L| peak < 1, roughly wc0/60 on this plant), which MATLAB returns.
Fix idea: for free I, after the 60-deg move fails, lower wc (backOff-like) until sampled |S|<=4; backOff currently excludes fam==PidtuneI.
Files: pid_tuning.go TunePID tuneOneGain/backOff.

data.title: nyquist: det certifier lacks model near multiple axis poles of H22
data.body:
Follow-up of XSMUDK (branch fix/nyquist-wave4, commit 502f3a6+).
detCertifier (delay_nyquist_cert.go) certifies det(I-H22 Delta) from the descriptor Taylor model of H22 only; it has no reciprocal (S-like) model as the SISO descriptorCertifier has.
Near a multiple imaginary-axis pole of H22 (Jordan block, e.g. a double integrator inside the delay channels) ||(jwI-A)^-1|| ~ 1/w^2 so the Neumann reach falls below the 1e-13 bisection tolerance next to the axis indentation; refine then returns refineUncertified -> ErrDelayUnsupported (IsStable/HinfNorm) where base returned a heuristic verdict.
Not a wrong value, a value->error regression in that regime; untested either way.
Fix idea: second model kind for the LFT loop from the full delay descriptor M (det M = chi*e^{jw sum tau}), or a frequency-adaptive diagonal scaling of the state block.
Files: delay_nyquist_cert.go (detCertifier), hinfnorm_delay.go loop().

data.title: perf: cut per-node cost of certified delay Nyquist refine
data.body:
Follow-up of XSMUDK. Certified refine costs one descriptor sample (O(size^3) inverse + norms) per grid node, ~4-6x a Hessenberg evaluation.
benchcmp -base c3d1364 (arm64): DiskMargin_PIDExactDelay +80..104%, Pidtune_Delayed +84..116% (PD_wc10 +588%, unstable-design error path, 1619 vs 1224 nodes), HinfNorm_InternalDelay siso/dde +70..78%, HinfNorm_Delay* +6..12%.
Levers: skip secondDerivativeNorm for certifier samples (only tightens small-h remainder), use the model g as f when l.at is the stock sisoEval (drops one evaluation per node), cache pidLoopCertifier descriptor build across PID candidates, cheaper resolvent norm bound.
Files: delay_nyquist.go refine/halfSpanPhase, delay_nyquist_cert.go, delay_peak_bound.go sampleInto.

data.title: nyquist: multi-channel det loops with double integrator error (phase of 1+L not certified)
data.body:
Branch fix/nyquist-wave4 (after 3e9e4b2). Value->error regression vs base c3d1364.

Repro: L=(s+0.5)/s^2 realized via quasiLoop.system with tau=0, then SetInputDelay(0.05) and SetOutputDelay(0.05) (total 0.1); IsStable(Feedback(sys,nil,-1)).
Branch: error "phase of 1+L not certified near ω=1.00000029e-07"; base: true (oracleRHPRoots 0).
Same for L=2.19702/(s^2(s+0.39245)), split tau 0.00813: branch errors, base false (oracle 2).
DiskMargin is fine (descriptor path).

Cause: closed loop has nd=2 internal delays, so delayLFT.loop uses detCertifier (kind 0 only). 3e9e4b2 gives nd==1 det loops a descriptorCertifier (S model); nd>1 still has none. detCertifier's reach near a multiple axis pole of H22 is tiny: h22.remainder Inf (zeta ~ 1/ω^2 for the Jordan block), and relRemainder's nu·‖ΔG‖ bound ignores that N^{-1} shrinks the rank-1 huge part of G, so even with a per-sample diagonal rescaling of the descriptor the det model needs h << ω^3.
Files: hinfnorm_delay.go (loop), delay_nyquist_cert.go (detCertifier), delay_peak_bound.go (descriptorResponse.remainder).
Possible fix: S-like model for det loops (1/det with a remainder from a closed-loop descriptor of the LFT), or scale-aware det remainder.

data.title: hinf torus: finite peak past span after in-span find -> grid exceeds
data.body:
Repro: torusRiseSeed("mixed", 155) (hinfnorm_delay_torus_rise_test.go), HinfNorm -> "delay grid exceeds 2097152 points".

data.title: TunePID default PID on stable delayed plant: Kd=137 design, 0.35deg crossing at 17.8 rad/s outside band

data.title: TunePID: sticky sisoEval singular error near integrator poles (discrete multi-integrator plants)
data.body:
Repro (fix/margins-wave5 d5c4f8d, after DSRJ7M lets AllMargin succeed; base 8015ead failed earlier in AllMargin):
TunePID(ctx, tf2ss(-0.015511622455509733/(z-1)^3, Dt=0.19047714028975662), PidtunePI, {}) -> 'TunePID: loop response at ω=3.8458e-06: singular complex matrix'.
TunePID(num=[-2.3897487927970316 -1.1649076634460165 1.1571601778487086], den=[1 -3.7187190663923624 5.156157199177088 -3.156157199177087 0.7187190663923623] (double pole at z=1), Dt=0.016181320226854916, PidtunePID) -> 'loop response at ω=1.2535e-04: singular'.
TunePID(num=[-86.58188789608674 -86.54930732135502], den=[1 -1.418487078684577 -0.7445387639462693 0.7445387639462693 1.418487078684577 -1], Dt=0.020779089557500845, PidtunePID) -> 'loop response at ω=2.03e-05: singular'.
41/600 seeded discrete/continuous integrator plants hit this. Cause: pid_tuning.go uses the sticky sisoEval (eval.err checks at pid_tuning.go:470/532/706/742) at frequencies so low that z≈1 / s≈0 integrator poles make the point solve singular; one failed evaluation aborts tuning instead of skipping (cf. sisoEval.try added in DSRJ7M). MATLAB pidtune returns a design or a target-unattainable result, never a solver error.

data.title: AllMargin drops phase crossovers at multiples of another when L(0) real negative (zeroRoot probe)
data.body:
Repro (base 8015ead and fix/margins-wave5 a4aa6a2, identical): AllMargin of tf(-2, [1 0 0 0 0 0], Dt=1) (= -2 z^-5, also with InputDelay=5 on tf(-2,1,1)) returns PhaseCrossFreqs [1.2566] only.
Oracle: -2 e^{-5jθ} is real negative at θ = 2πm/5, so phase crossovers at 1.2566 and 2.5133 (GM -6.02 dB each); MATLAB allmargin lists both.
Also -2 z^-4 misses π (Nyquist), -2 z^-6 misses 2π/3, -2 z^-8 misses π/2 and π. Seeded sweep: -116.75 z^-5, Dt=0.79 misses 3.182.
Cause: margin.go rationalLoop.polish zeroRoot path — L(0) real negative gives |f(0)|<=tol, and a crossover at twice another has f(best/2)=0 at the lower crossover, so within(best/2) drops it as a rounding-shifted root at 0. Same mechanism fixed for the pole-at-0 case in a4aa6a2; the no-pole case remains.

data.title: AllMargin misses low-frequency gain crossover of small-gain discrete multiple integrators k/(z-1)^n
data.body:
Repro: AllMargin(tf(3.1623e-8, [1 -2 1], Dt=1)) returns no gain crossover on base 8015ead and fix/margins-wave5. Oracle: |k/(2 sin(θ/2))^2| = 1 at θ ≈ √k = 1.778e-4. k=1e-7 is found (3.162e-4).
On fix/margins-wave5 (base errored), tf(3.1623e-8, [1 -3 3 -1], Dt=1 or 0.1) returns no gain crossover; oracle θ ≈ k^{1/3} = 3.162e-3 (/Dt). k=1e-7 found.
Cause: rationalLoop gainCandidates pencil roots near the multiplicity-2n cluster at z=1 lose accuracy once k^2 is below eps relative to D·D~ coefficients: for k=3.16e-8/(z-1)^3 candidates are [0.0023024 0.0023026 0.0026296] vs true 0.003162; polish only brackets ±1e-2 relative, so the root is never reached and the crossover silently vanishes. Continuous k/s^n is fine to k=1e-20.
Files: margin.go gainCandidates/boundaryRoots/polish.

data.title: delay nyquist: Inf/NaN 1+L at axis indentation (multi-integrator) -> false unstable via hiddenAxisRoot, or singular-matrix error
data.body:
Found reviewing fix/nyquist-wave5 (QZWVN4/BRT7G3/ZF4ESN). Pre-existing: identical on base 8015ead and branch 845547e (not caused by wave5).

Wrong value: stable closed loop reported unstable (IsStable=false, HinfNorm=+Inf).
Repro 1 (SISO, nd=1): P=num/den via TransferFunc.StateSpace,
  num=[5.910980332296372 27.806410726825444 37.431038620035174 11.565340194450041]
  den=[1 0.20389057161026952 -0.07104652183880648 0 0], SetInputDelay(0.022715415198538882), Feedback(P,nil,-1).
  Oracle: chi=den+num*e^{-tau s} has 0 RHP roots (argument principle box 50+, Newton sweep: rightmost root -0.4389); dense sweep |T| peak 1.777.
  delayLFT.loop(false).at: |L(1e-6)|=1.63e14, |L(1e-5)|=1.63e12 (correct ~163/w^2), but |L(1e-7)|=+Inf.
  hiddenAxisRoot (delay_nyquist.go) treats Inf/NaN at a.w+axisGap as a hidden axis root -> nyquist returns axisRoot -> stable=false.
Repro 2 (nd=3): P=[0.46603599034106363 1.1507662521895636 0.8492300943505945 0.24647378460270886 0.024431190753480315]/[1 1.0954836376994372 0 0 0] (StateSpace), P.SetOutputDelay(0.02290693554361851),
  K = Parallel(0.9575000297606748 e^{-0.019511878680882565 s}, -0.022781002697111294 e^{-0.26994534441905227 s}) (NewGain + SetInputDelay), Feedback(P,K,-1). Oracle 0 RHP roots; |L| NaN at 1e-7 and 1e-6 -> false unstable.
Repro 3: P=[10.747742314693493 11.151438054546672 2.1696272808395105]/[1 4.665255397111082 0 0 0], out 0.04028063817878855, K=1.0443033033837892 e^-0.1306289578483865 + 0.4884653272897968 e^-0.20653192846415452: NaN up to 1e-5, false unstable.

Sibling (value->error, same cause): ~200/2500 random triple-integrator loops error "IsStable: response at ω=1e-07: singular complex matrix" (e.g. num=[1.3878930086477943 5.22648972355323] den=[1 0 0 0] tin=0.1033441077900939 tout=0.4856267246070171, canonical/TF realization, Feedback(sys,nil,-1)).

Cause: state-space evaluation of H22/L at w=1e-7 with a triple (or ill-scaled double) integrator overflows/singular in the frequency evaluator; hiddenAxisRoot's !(near>0)||IsInf check converts the evaluation failure into a closed-loop axis root claim. Fix idea: evaluate at the indentation via the descriptor/certifier models or a balanced/scaled realization; never infer an axis root from a non-finite sample.
Files: delay_nyquist.go hiddenAxisRoot/refine, hinfnorm_delay.go charMinusOne/h22 evaluator.

data.title: pid stability screen false-stable for PI with negative Ki on clustered near-integrator poles
data.body:
Repro (pre-existing on base 8015ead and on fix/tunepid-wave5): plant G=(0.1z+0.05)/((z-1)(z-0.999)^2), Dt=0.1 (TransferFunc.StateSpace). Take P0 = computePIDGains(G, PI, wc, 60, 1, true) for wc in {3e-4, 5.32e-5, 5.32e-6}; scale Kp by f in {0.35..2.05} and Ki by -1 or -0.01. 30 of these points are unstable by the exact big.Rat Schur-Cohn oracle (pidtuneExactSchurStable, pidtune_backoff_test.go) but pidStabilityScreen.closedLoopPoles and pidtuneLoop.stable (float eig + poleStabilityTolerance) call them stable; e.g. wc=5.32e-5, Kp=0.75*Kp0, Ki=-Ki0. Cause: the 4-pole cluster near z=1 gives float eigenvalue errors ~3e-6 vs a true real root ~4e-7 outside |z|=1.
Files: pid_tuning.go (pidTuningPolesStable / pidTuningExactStable, added for 4FAOGG on fix/tunepid-wave5), pidtune.go pidtuneLoop.stable.
Why not fixed with 4FAOGG: escalating float-stable verdicts with a pole within 1e-3 of the boundary to the exact test fires on every design of fast-sampled plants (e.g. c2d(1/((s+1)(s+2)),1e-3)): Pidtune PI 3-11x slower. Candidate cheap refutation: exact sign of c(1)=det(I-A_cl) and (-1)^n c(-1) on the dyadic integer build (one Bareiss det each) catches real-root crossings like these; complex pairs just outside the circle need more. Impact: only designs with wrong-sign gains, which Pidtune's sign rule normally avoids; mirrored/unknown-sign searches could accept one.

data.title: TunePID default PIDF on integrating plant: 1.2deg crossing below wc/100 band (|S| 49)
data.body:
Pre-existing: identical gains at 8015ead and fix/tunepid-wave5 (bcd97f4). Found by wave5 reviewer sweep.
Repro (continuous, no delay): num {-3.8562437633148288}, den {1, 2.38218255046348, 0.43053693845881924, 0}.
TunePID(ctx, plant, PidtunePIDF, PIDTuningOptions{}) -> Kp -5.294e-05, Ki -6.797e-05, Kd -0.83193, Tf 0.18240; AchievedCrossover 1.232, AchievedPhaseMargin 57.0 (warnings: initial seed infeasible; margins describe finite band).
Independent dense sweep of L=G*C (1e-4..1e2): extra 0 dB crossings at 0.008488 rad/s (PM 1.17 deg) and 0.009714 (PM 173); |S| peak 48.96 at 0.00849. Closed loop is stable (exact Routh on den*denC+num*numC), so the design is nearly unstable but evidence reports 57 deg.
Second case: num {6.021719327000207}, den {1, 3.3266544288844027, 0.13253243642255236, 0}, PIDF -> Kp 5.56e-05, Ki 6.09e-05, Kd 0.787, Tf 0.1785; crossing at ~0.0087 rad/s PM 7.6, |S| 7.92.
Cause guess: tiny Kp/Ki vs Kd lets the integrator-on-integrator low-frequency loop cross 0 dB below the wc/100 sampled band; delay-free default design does not run the sampled |S| check (robust mode is for delayed plants / moved crossovers), and the band starts at wc/100.
Files: pid_tuning.go (TunePID default path, pidTuningPlant low/high band, robust flag).

data.title: plantCrossoverFreq: Bandwidth infinite-DC error aborts TunePID/Pidtune on integrators with |G|>1 everywhere
data.body:
Repro (branch fix/tunepid-wave6 after KMOSVP; same on 86ae800): plants with |G| > 1 at every frequency have no gain crossover, so plantCrossoverFreq (pidtune.go) falls to Bandwidth(plant,-3), which errors on an integrator's infinite DC gain instead of falling through to the pole-based fallback below it.
- TunePID/Pidtune(tf2ss(2.834699423337496/(z-1), Dt=0.02298944503089565), PID) -> 'Bandwidth: DC gain is +Inf, bandwidth undefined: invalid argument'.
- TunePID/Pidtune(tf2ss((5.340957844707375 s + 23.09187463052385)/s), PID) -> same error (continuous).
Explicit CrossoverFrequency anywhere in 1e-3..1e2 rad/s gives TunePID designs (discrete ones Schur-stable by pidtuneExactSchurStable). MATLAB pidtune returns a design. ~33/600 seeded integrator plants (discrete+continuous, P..PIDF) hit this. Fix: treat a Bandwidth infinite-DC error as no bandwidth and continue to the pole fallback (or choose wc from phase), files pidtune.go plantCrossoverFreq.

data.title: AllMargin: singular sticky eval in polish near rounded z=1 poles (TunePID/Pidtune PIDF)
data.body: Repro (branch fix/tunepid-wave6 after KMOSVP, also 86ae800): G=tf2ss((0.5296264797589852 z - 0.49398687205654906)/(z^4 - 3.927287723431127 z^3 + 5.782240810121571 z^2 - 3.7826184499497617 z + 0.9276653632593171), Dt=0.0422252269048428) (rounded poles near z=1). TunePID(ctx,G,PidtunePIDF,{}) and Pidtune(G,PIDF,0,nil) -> 'AllMargin: loop response at ω=0.00015974604677042932: singular complex matrix'. Path: findCrossoverFreq -> plantCrossoverFreq -> AllMargin -> rationalLoop.polish (margin.go ~987/1028) calls the sticky eval.at on a candidate next to the cluster, not eval.try (DSRJ7M covered other polish paths). Explicit wc 0.0187..0.0469 rad/s gives TunePID PIDF designs, Schur-stable by pidtuneExactSchurStable. MATLAB allmargin/pidtune return results. Files: margin.go polish/gainCrossings.

data.title: TunePID auto PID unattainable on discrete double integrator+lag; designs exist 2 decades below wc0
data.body: Repro (branch fix/tunepid-wave6 after KMOSVP): G=tf2ss(-0.14994524256120972/((z-1)^2 (z-0.98722)), den=[1 -2.9872237308563525 2.974447461712705 -0.9872237308563525], Dt=0.018062614213725733). TunePID(ctx,G,PidtunePID,{}) -> ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable at wc0=29.8 rad/s; Pidtune(G,PID,0,nil) returns a design (its back-off). TunePID with explicit CrossoverFrequency 0.0035..0.35 rad/s returns designs, all Schur-stable by pidtuneExactSchurStable. TunePID never backs off an undelayed PID/PD (backOff is gated on tau>0), so findCrossoverFreq's high wc0 decides. Seeded sweep: 6/20 probed discrete multi-integrator PID plants (formerly KMOSVP solver errors) have explicit-wc designs 1-3 decades below wc0 while auto says unattainable. MATLAB pidtune returns a design. Related: X5LHXA (Pidtune wc too high). Files: pid_tuning.go TunePID (back-off gate), pidtune.go findCrossoverFreq.

data.title: AllMargin: singular complex matrix error for k<0 over (z+1)^4 near Nyquist
data.body:
Repro (86ae800 and fix/margins-wave6 98bd058, identical): AllMargin(tf(-1e-6, [1 4 6 4 1], Dt=1)) -> 'AllMargin: loop response at ω=3.1413647317487747: singular complex matrix: controlsys: singular matrix in transformation'. tf(+1e-6, same den) succeeds (wgc 3.10997, wpc 1.5708).
Also: -5.32259e-11/(z+1)^4 Dt=1 (ω=3.14127), 2.33286e-6(z-0.49718)/(z+1)^4 Dt=1 (ω=3.14123); seeded sweep of k/(z+1)^4 (+extra stable real factors, Dt in {1,0.1,0.79,0.01}) gave 32/2400 such errors, all with the 4-fold z=-1 cluster.
Oracle: L=k/(2cos(θ/2))^4·e^{-j2θ}; for k=-1e-6: |L|=1 at cos(θ/2)=k^{1/4}/2 -> θ≈3.10997; L real negative at θ=π/2 -> wpc [1.5708], GM=20log10(16e6)? (|L(π/2)|=1e-6/4 -> GM 132.04 dB). MATLAB allmargin returns values.
Likely same class as 6WSXWR (sticky eval.at on a candidate next to a pole cluster, here phase-crossing/polish path near z=-1). Files: margin.go polish/phaseCrossings.

data.title: nyquist: axis indent fails when 2nd pole clusters near multiple integrator (value->error)
data.body:
Residual of 6AJN4Q sibling after fix/nyquist-wave6 89e92df (indentLimit 1e-2·gap).
Seeded 2000-case sweep (triple/double integrator, random num, input delay, delayed-gain K): 7 still error
"L not finite near the axis pole ω=0: errDelayLoopUnsupported". All have another open-loop pole within ~1e-2 of 0,
so indentLimit (1e-2·0.0098 etc) < first ω where L finite (1e-4..1e-3). Argument-principle oracle on
χ = den + num·ΣK e^{-τs}: all unstable (2-3 RHP roots); base 86ae800 also errors (no regression).
Repro: P = [3.310364316932462 -3.4690921208593335]/[1 -0.0066905036607369794 0 0 0] (TransferFunc.StateSpace),
SetInputDelay(0.3333286130472003), K = -0.9519745006566804·e^{-0.2094256006355884 s}; Feedback(P,K,-1).IsStable errors;
oracle 2 RHP roots -> expect false, HinfNorm +Inf. L NaN at ω≤1e-5, finite 1e-4 (2·4.9e14).
Fix idea: indent around the cluster (poles within radius enclosed; adjust rhp count for enclosed RHP poles),
or evaluate L near origin via partial fractions instead of the singular pencil solve.
Files: delay_nyquist.go indent/indentLimit.

data.title: Pidtune PIDF returns PM 2.4 deg design on integrator+two-real-pole plants (Tf ~ 1.3/wc)
data.body:
Found by tunepid wave6 track (CZXBZU) while checking the TunePID repro plants against Pidtune. Base fix/tunepid-wave6 9f3e8dc (pidtune.go unchanged vs 86ae800).
Repro (continuous, no delay):
  p := G(num {-3.8562437633148288}, den {1, 2.38218255046348, 0.43053693845881924, 0})
  Pidtune(p, PidtunePIDF, 0, nil) -> Kp -0.10217 Ki -0.025176 Kd -1.67374 Tf 1.63819 (parallel), err nil.
  AllMargin(Series(pid.System(), p)): PM 2.376 deg at 1.2321 rad/s (only gain crossing), GM 0.797 at 1.289 rad/s (and -35 dB at 0.0565).
  Independent closed-form sweep of L=G*C agrees: single crossing 1.2321, PM 2.37.
Second: num {6.021719327000207}, den {1, 3.3266544288844027, 0.13253243642255236, 0} -> Kp 0.10217 Ki 0.02666 Kd 1.58054 Tf 1.54697; PM 2.82 deg at 1.3047, GM 1.17.
Expected (MATLAB parity): ~60 deg target; TunePID PIDF on the same plants now returns PM 57 deg, |S| <= 1.38 at the same wc.
Guess: the filter Tf (Tf*wc ~ 2) adds ~63 deg lag the design does not account for, or the margin gate is skipped on this path. Files: pidtune.go.

data.title: delay nyquist: defective double imaginary-axis pole pair misclassified -> false unstable
data.body:
Found during fix/nyquist-wave6 (GFXRCX). Pre-existing: same on base 86ae800 and branch 89e92df.
Repro A (exact double pair): P = num/den, num=[4 8 8 4 0], den=(s^2+1)^2(s+1)=[1 1 2 2 1 1] (TransferFunc.StateSpace),
SetInputDelay(0.01), Feedback(P,nil,-1).IsStable() -> false, nil; HinfNorm +Inf.
Oracle: argument principle on chi = den + num e^{-0.01 s} on box bounding RHP roots -> 0 RHP roots (tau=0 gives (s+1)^5).
Cause: Poles() splits the defective pair ±j into ±8.6e-9 ± j(1∓6.8e-9); classifyPoleStability/poleStabilityTolerance
call one RHP (l.rhp=2) and one LHP, l.axis is empty, so no indentation; refine then hits the pole at ω≈1 and reports
axisRoot (false unstable). Tolerance ignores eps^(1/m) sensitivity of an m-fold defective eigenvalue.
Repro B (near-coincident, separation 9e-8): num=[1.7733920073898735 0.4376675554475584 0.0633521995049906
-0.3280049239511615 -0.17086077595238047], den=[1 0.41818100387501744 1.296612937471446 0.5422200140535021
0.42030127740454004 0.17576273247407195], SetInputDelay(0.5412512384391044): IsStable false, oracle 0 RHP roots.
Also: other double-pair loops error "response at ω=w0: singular complex matrix" (value->error in base too).
Files: delay_nyquist.go addPoles/addAxisPole, stability.go poleStabilityTolerance.
Fix idea: cluster eigenvalues within eps^(1/m)-scaled radius of the axis and treat them as an m-fold axis pole.

data.title: delay nyquist: stable loop errors when two small poles cluster at multiple integrator (GFXRCX residual)
data.body:
Found reviewing fix/nyquist-wave6 (fd8905a, 6AJN4Q/GFXRCX). Pre-existing: base 86ae800 also errors ("response at ω=1e-07: singular complex matrix"); not a regression.

Value->error on an oracle-STABLE loop (GFXRCX fix covers single nearby pole only).
Repro: P = num/den via TransferFunc.StateSpace,
  num=[4.142627854570593 1.2271211903141908 0.11276344373801922 0.003433033463902915 3.306252694392361e-05]
  den=[1 -0.0013350213545146655 -1.8267006382290283e-09 0 0 0]   (s^3 · poles ≈ +1.3365e-3, -1.367e-6)
  P.SetInputDelay(0.030755962059159137); P.SetOutputDelay(0.10588402844719585)
  K = Parallel(1.2938430639742877·e^{-0.13168802070035582 s}, 0.07787111691968329·e^{-0.07929680193337156 s}) (NewGain+SetInputDelay)
  Feedback(P,K,-1).IsStable -> err "|L| near the poles at the origin does not follow them: errDelayLoopUnsupported" (HinfNorm, DiskMargin(Series(K,P)) same).
Oracle: argument principle on χ = den + num·K(s)·e^{-(tin+tout)s} over RHP box (|s|<R bound): 0 RHP roots -> expect IsStable=true, finite HinfNorm (dense sweep).
Rate: 1/665 oracle-stable cases in seeded sweep (mode: lead num, small delay); 17 more errors were oracle-unstable (2-3 RHP roots), all with 2 poles within ~1e-2 of origin.
Likely: indentCluster growth check (0.3 dec) fails because L is NaN until g beyond the tiny pole's window and nearby L zeros (~1e-2..1e-1) break growth for k=2; or a pole at -1.4e-6 just above the 1e-6 'other pole' cutoff.
Files: delay_nyquist.go indentCluster/indentLimit.

data.title: TunePID explicit low wc: nonfinite plant response error on rounded z=1 double pole
data.body:
Repro (fix/tunepid-wave7 a8bec7f, also base 7346787): G = tf2ss(-0.14994524256120972/((z-1)^2 (z-0.98722)), den=[1 -2.9872237308563525 2.974447461712705 -0.9872237308563525], Dt=0.018062614213725733) (HXK42S plant).
TunePID(ctx, G, PidtunePID, {CrossoverFrequency: 0.0035}) -> "TunePID: nonfinite plant response at 3.5e-05: controlsys: invalid argument".
The analysis band's low end wc/100 = 3.5e-5 rad/s hits a singular sisoEval solve next to the rounded double pole at z=1; the true |G| there is ~3e13 (finite). wc 0.035 and 0.35 give Schur-stable designs (pidtuneExactSchurStable). MATLAB pidtune(G,'pid',0.0035) returns a design.
Value->error on a valid explicit crossover; unknown whether a design with the 60 deg margin exists at 0.0035. Likely fix: evaluate the band floor via eval.try / shrink the band floor to the lowest finite sample (pid_tuning.go tuneAt / tunePIDScan band setup, sisoEval).

data.title: AllMargin: misses crossovers for tiny k over (z+1)^4 cluster (|k|<~5e-13)
data.body:
AllMargin misses crossovers of k·num/((z+1)^4·den) for |k| <~ 5e-13 (pre-existing at 7346787; after 5RWUVZ fix the former singular-matrix errors in this regime also return incomplete sets).

Repros (Dt as given, oracle: e^{jθ}+1 = 2cos(θ/2)e^{jθ/2}, bisect L(θ) on a grid graded to Nyquist):
1. -1.6726418877515324e-14/((z+1)^4 (z+0.7445460248190218)), Dt 0.1: want wgc 31.41087 and wpc 23.7411 (θ 2.37411, far from the cluster, |L| ~ 1e-14); got both empty. realCandidates returns only 31.4112, 31.4116, 31.4159 (all unevaluable), gainCandidates none.
2. 2.4983505154002314e-13 (z+0.8685335634364679)/((z+1)^4 (z+0.6851821799011946)), Dt 0.79: want wgc 3.97598; got none (gain pencil roots 3.94778, 3.94834 spurious, rejected); endCrossings top scan does not recover it.
Seeded sweep (k log-uniform 1e-14..1, ±, optional zero in (-1,1), 0-1 real pole in (-0.9,0.9), Dt in {1,0.1,0.79,0.01}, 2400 cases): 87 mismatches vs oracle, all |k| <= 2.5e-13; none above.
Likely: pencil (balanced realization of the 4-fold cluster) loses boundary roots when |L| is tiny, and the solve becomes singular (cSolveInPlace pivot tol) within ~1e-4 of Nyquist where |z+1|^4 ~ eps, so endCrossings cannot bracket. Files: margin.go gainCandidates/realCandidates/endCrossings, frequency.go cSolveInPlace.

data.title: plantCrossoverFreq: discrete pole fallback uses |z| as rad/s (ignores Dt)
data.body:
plantCrossoverFreq (pidtune.go) finite-DC pole fallback, reached when there is no gain crossover and Bandwidth(-3) is +Inf, returns 0.5*|p| for discrete poles: |z| has no units and Dt is never used.
Repro: plant 0.1(z-0.9)/(z+0.5) has |G| < 1 everywhere and gain rising with frequency. plantCrossoverFreq returns 0.25 rad/s for both Dt=0.1 and Dt=0.01. The pole's natural frequency is |ln(-0.5)|/Dt = 3.22/Dt, so the pick should scale with 1/Dt. pidtuneSlowestPole and the new pidtuneSlowestRoot in the same file already map poles that way.
Evidence: instrumenting the fallback shows about 200 hits from discrete plants in TestPidtuneAutoCrossoverRandomStable, so changing it changes existing auto crossovers and needs regression checks (back-off and stability oracles).
Found on fix/pidtune-wave7 (6RFH5N), which leaves this path unchanged on purpose. Fix: for Dt>0 use |ln z|/Dt, skip z near 1, and cap below Nyquist.

data.title: TunePID backOff gate skips design depths (3,5,11,13-15,17-18) on undelayed multi-integrator plants
data.body:
Found reviewing fix/tunepid-wave7 (a8bec7f, HXK42S). Not a regression: base 7346787 also unattainable.

backOff (pid_tuning.go TunePID) probes depths 1,2 then gates 20,19,9,12,16 and only scans between on a gate success. Undelayed discrete multi-integrator plants with designs only at ungated depths stay ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable, while TunePID with explicit CrossoverFrequency = wc0*2^(-j/2) gives a design that is exact-Schur-stable (pidtuneExactSchurStable) with sampled |S|<=4 to Nyquist, and Pidtune returns a design.

Repro (TunePID(ctx, tf2ss(num/den, dt), fam, {})):
- 1800: num=[0.2376376495436092 -0.22623825681198792] den=[1 -3 3 -1] dt=0.0411986772067474 PIDF. wc0=11.83; design only at depth 3 (4.18 rad/s). Pidtune: Kp=0.291 Ki=0.690 Kd=0.0824 Tf=0.0283.
- 1149: num=[0.05561793864532625 -0.055150540391457045] den=[1 -3.7172691807634135 5.151807542290241 -3.1518075422902405 0.7172691807634135] dt=0.022067595844186595 PIDF. wc0=16.58; design at depth 5.
- 908: num=[-0.26076155489343816] den=[1 -5.301065168243693 11.569174727312362 -13.256141604617728 8.364200100816014 -2.7313484558098238 0.3551804005428702] dt=0.14827014447740874 PID. wc0=5.614; designs depths 13-15. Pidtune returns a (tiny-gain) design.
- 1098: num=[0.0406846146866439] den=[1 -3.8564046132602567 5.569527491905905 -3.5698411440310416 0.8567182653853925] dt=0.060709355752838014 PID. depth 18 only.
Seeded sweep (2000 plants, PCG(4242,7)): 10 of 310 remaining undelayed D-family integrating unattainables have such depths in [1,20].
Files: pid_tuning.go TunePID backOff gate schedule.

data.title: delay nyquist: false unstable (axisRoot) for double integrator + LHP pole at -8e-9
data.body:
Found reviewing fix/nyquist-wave7 (YJINK6). Pre-existing: base 7346787 and branch 1dbf872 both wrong, arm64 and amd64.
Repro (public API): P = num/den via TransferFunc.StateSpace,
  num=[1.0220019540306915 2.4805485191105365 1.1305200275357294 0.01821221818505486]
  den=[1 -0.017718929845052005 -1.4494897693008775e-10 0 0]   (s^2 · poles +0.017719, -8.18e-9)
  SetInputDelay(0.0044056653976761095); Feedback(P,nil,-1).IsStable() -> false, nil; HinfNorm +Inf.
Oracle: argument principle on chi = den + num e^{-tau s} over [0,5.06]x[-5.06,5.06] (|L|<0.5 beyond) -> 0 RHP roots;
Newton root scan: rightmost closed-loop root -0.01672, others -0.245±1.473j, -0.491. Expect IsStable true, finite HinfNorm.
Internals: poles [0.017719, -8.18e-9, 0, 0]; base axis {w:0 mult:2}, indent gap 3.16e-5 encloses the -8.18e-9 pole,
nyquist returns axisRoot=true at w=0 (growth check sees 3 decades, mult 2). Branch pairs -8.18e-9 with 0 (mult 3), still axisRoot.
Sweep: 1/1000 in family s^2(s+a)(s+b), |b| 1e-9..1e-5, random num, tau 3e-3..2.
Files: delay_nyquist.go addPoles/indent/indentLimit (1e-6 'other pole' cutoff), axisGrowth.

data.title: AllMargin: polish drops genuine phase crossover when wide bracket end hits unevaluable ω near lightly damped pole
data.body:
Found reviewing fix/margins-wave7 (75e0691, fixes 5RWUVZ/6WSXWR). Base 7346787 errored on these; branch returns success but omits a real phase crossover (silent wrong value).
Repro (Dt=1): L = -0.02309469977260592*(z+0.4863575702993606) / ((z-(1+2.9030126265483175e-05i))(z-(1-2.9030126265483175e-05i))(z-0.9561590173593617)(z-0.8871366217113326)(z+0.43121472459012195)), via TransferFunc{...}.StateSpace().
Branch AllMargin: wpc [0.27790, π]; oracle (factored-form eval + bisection) also has wpc 2.8582737529213393e-05, GM -225.486 dB. MATLAB allmargin reports it.
Mechanism (margin.go polish): realCandidates gives 2.8752494685e-05 (0.6% off crossing; phaseOffset 0.0324° > tol 1e-7). Brackets d=1e-12..1e-4 don't span the crossing; d=1e-2 does (a=2.8465e-05 f=-0.011, ok), but b=2.9040e-05 is past the pole at ω≈2.903e-05 where eval fails -> ft NaN -> bracket discarded -> candidate dropped. ss eval at the crossing itself is fine (ok, phase matches oracle to ~1e-5°).
Second case, Dt=0.79: k=-0.21501793541077313, zs [-0.4405797671906855,-0.6838981765389421], ps [1±6.176538894270818e-05i, 0.9703560326623678, 0.8574995610377053, 0.7919093674641045]; oracle wpc 7.731566170130944e-05 (GM -256.95 dB) missing; same d=1e-2 b NaN pattern.
Fix direction: on NaN at a bracket end, shrink that end toward w (e.g. halve the offset) until evaluable rather than abandoning the bracket.

data.title: Pidtune discrete FE filter fallback returns non-robust PIDF (PM -34 deg at 2nd crossing, Ms 8.6)
data.body:
Found by pidtune wave7 (OW4BCI), branch fix/pidtune-wave7 9f84d62.
Repro (pinned by TestPidtuneDiscreteFilterFallsBackToForwardEuler, pidtune_backoff_test.go):
  G = 0.24591/(z^2-1.84612z+0.74449), Dt=0.274846; Pidtune(G, PIDF, 0, nil)
  -> FE design Kp 0.55146 Ki 0.15294 Kd 0.68912 Tf 0.12496, err nil.
  Signed margins (MATLAB convention) of the directly evaluated loop: 60 deg at wc, -34.5 deg at a second crossing; |S| peak 8.63.
Cause: pidtuneRun.signed's forward-Euler retry (taken when the backward-Euler design fails) is checked ungated on the first (non-backoff) design, so only stability is screened; base 7346787 behaves the same.
Second instance from a random sweep (explicit wc=3, nil opts): the BE Td/10 design misses its phase, FE retry gives PM -30 deg, |S| 9.
Expected (MATLAB parity): robust design (PM at every crossing, |S|<=4) or back off/unattainable. Fix likely gates the FE retry, but the pinned test gains must then be revisited. Files: pidtune.go, pidtune_backoff_test.go.

data.title: AllMargin misses phase crossover when pencil root lands past pole pair at L>0 (arm64)
data.body:
Found on fix/margins-wave8 (7ab3a18, UFBPWZ follow-up). Repro (Dt=1, arm64): num [-2.166935933035251 1.9807432626284676], den [1 -2.73127553541105 2.2142827468764708 -0.23473888724605785 -0.2482683242149491] via TransferFunc.StateSpace(); AllMargin wpc [1.6806]; oracle (float64 coeffs evaluated exactly in big.Float, log-grid bisection) also has wpc 1.45446e-05 (GM -246.7 dB). amd64 finds it after 7ab3a18; arm64 does not.
Mechanism: realCandidates gives 1.48876e-05, past the pole pair (~1.47e-05 unevaluable), where L is real positive (phase offset 179.9 deg), so phaseCrossings filters it (|offset|<90) before polish/walk can reach the crossing 2.3% below. Fix direction: let a candidate whose neighbourhood is unevaluable reach polish even if offset>=90, without sending every L>0 root through walk.

data.title: pidtuneIntegratorCluster swallows all roots for >=7 roots: integrating crossover uses zeros/wrong freq
data.body:
pidtuneIntegratorCluster (pidtune.go) tries m = len(roots) first with tol = 100*eps^(1/m)*scale. For m>=6 tol >= 0.25*scale, m>=8 tol >= scale, so every root lands in the "integrator cluster" (continuous: scale = max|root|, so for >=8 roots ALL roots are always within tol; discrete: all roots within 0.25 of z=1 for 6 roots, 0.58 for 7, 1.1 for 8). pidtuneSlowestRoot then skips them.

Pre-existing on b083afe/origin/main in pidtuneIntegratingCrossover (integrating plant without gain crossover).
Repro (continuous, Pidtune PI wc=0): G = 5*prod_{i<n}(s+0.5+0.1i)*(s+3) / (s*prod_{i<n}(s+1+0.2i)), n=7 and n=8.
plantCrossoverFreq gives 0.127 (n=7) and 0.0597 (n=8); expected half slowest nonintegrating pole = 0.5 (n=5,6 give 0.5 correctly). Pole set swallowed, falls back to zeros.
Resulting PI: n=7 Kp .41 Ki .116 min signed PM -128 deg; n=8 PM -100 deg (vs n=6 PM 104).
Fix idea: cap m so tol stays small (e.g. require gap between cluster and next root, or tol relative cap like 1e-3*scale), never count the largest root in a continuous cluster.
Note: fix/pidtune-wave8 (TFE7I2, e5dfeb5) reuses this helper in plantCrossoverFreq's nonintegrating pole fallback, exposing it there too (reviewer flagged blocking).

data.title: test oracleRHPRoots aliases phase near clustered near-axis poles
data.body:
Found in fix/nyquist-wave8 (YJINK6 sweep). Test helper oracleRHPRoots (delay_nyquist_test.go) samples the imaginary-axis edge uniformly (20000 pts); near clustered lightly-damped poles arg chi turns 2pi between samples and bisection (|dphase|>0.2) never triggers.
Repro: quasiLoop{num:[-8171.912837099235 1.6822882600399005 -7814.689216252464 -0.046521640682292836 -1868.165755288988], den:[1 8174.619511588051 0.9525453671937382 7815.785348697253 0.2268327569483714 1868.175614262993], tau:0.012138572095017666}; oracleRHPRoots(t, q.chi, 2e4) -> 2. Dense-axis oracle (extra samples at |Im p|(1±d), d geometric 1e-13..0.5, as sweepOracle in delay_nyquist_cluster_sweep_test.go) -> 0, stable with step 0.05/n=40000 too; new IsStable says stable.
Fix: add pole-frequency-clustered samples on the axis edge (den roots), as sweepOracle does. Existing tests using it may rely on boxes small enough; audit after fix.

data.title: AllMargin misses phase crossover below lightly damped pole pair when evaluable pencil root lands >1% off
data.body:
Found reviewing fix/margins-wave8 (d5f7a96, UFBPWZ/Y3RHVQ). Pre-existing at b083afe; branch unchanged (no regression). Distinct from UFBPWZ (NaN bracket end) and UJSGC2 (root past pole filtered by |offset|>=90): here candidate and crossing are both evaluable, but the realCandidates root lies 2-6% from the true crossing, so the polish brackets (max ±1e-2 relative) never span it and walk is not triggered (walk only runs when something is unevaluable).

Repro (Dt=0.1, arm64): TransferFunc num [-0.0013196134305395058 -0.00023536903292695072], den [1 -2.3854598907075455 1.770919781465705 -0.3854598907270551] (pole pair 1±j7.11e-6 · real pole), .StateSpace(), AllMargin.
Got wpc [31.4159] only. Oracle (float64 coeffs evaluated exactly in big.Float, log grid + bisection on Im L, Re L<0) also has wpc 4.707087894e-05 rad/s, GM -158.98 dB. ss eval at 0.999w/w/1.001w: Im L = +1.15, ~0, -1.16 with Re L = -8.9e7 (clean sign change). realCandidates gives 4.98111e-05 (5.8% above).
More (Dt=1): num [-4.737105371029762 -1.0653329101644098], den [1 -0.4415335279470294 -1.5153667659780603 0.355334116135632 0.6015661780899885]; oracle wpc 4.742164324e-06 (GM -208.06 dB) missed; candidate 4.8487e-06.
Sweep: pole pair 1±jε (ε log-uniform 1e-6..1e-2), k ±1e-3..10, 0-2 zeros, 1-3 real poles, Dt {1,0.1,0.79}: 60/500 miss a crossover at w/φ ≈ 0.5-0.95 (φ = pair angle/Dt); all are misses, none spurious.
Fix direction: when no bracket spans and f at candidate is small but nonzero, widen bracket beyond 1e-2 (e.g. walk also when evaluable, bounded by neighbours) while keeping walkClearance guard.
Files: margin.go polish/realCandidates.

data.title: Bandwidth +Inf for small DC gain (k/((s+1)(s+2)), k<=1e-4)
data.body:
Pre-existing at b083afe (also on fix/margins-wave8 a433167): Bandwidth returns +Inf, nil for small-DC-gain loops of order >= 2.
Repro (continuous): sys = tf(k, conv([1 1],[1 2])).StateSpace(); Bandwidth(sys, -3).
  k = 1e-3..1: 0.8358236303817804 (correct; analytic -3 dB point of k/((s+1)(s+2))).
  k <= 1e-4 (checked 1e-4 .. 1e-16 per decade): +Inf, err nil. Wrong value; MATLAB bandwidth is 0.8358 independent of k.
Same for k/((s+1)(s+2)(s+3)): correct 0.78579 for k >= 1e-3, +Inf for k <= 1e-4 (threshold ~10^-3.5).
First order k/(s+0.597) is fine at b083afe for all k; fix/margins-wave8 d5f7a96 (scaleInputRowCol) breaks it for k <= ~1e-11 (reported in that review).
Likely: bandwidth() -> rationalLoop.gainCandidates(gamma) with gamma = DC*10^(-3/20) tiny; pencil divides C,D by gamma, so -c'c block ~ 1/gamma^2 dwarfs A and B; QZ loses the boundary roots. Possible fix: scale the loop (C or B) by 1/gamma before forming the pencil instead of c=C/gamma in the coupling block, or balance the pencil.
Files: margin.go bandwidth(), gainCandidates(), boundaryRoots().

data.title: Pidtune explicit wc PIDF returns stable design with PM -157 deg at another crossover (ungated primary design)
data.body:
Found by pidtune wave8 (YXFRDR), branch fix/pidtune-wave8 4579936.
Repro: G = (0.17032241632981948 z + 1.4143934743506665)/(z^2 - 1.8341193107935498 z + 0.756547032348602), Dt = 0.3419630736464782;
  Pidtune(G, PIDF, wc, nil) with explicit wc = 0.612 -> FE PIDF Kp 0.05388 Ki 0.006595 Kd 0.11296 Tf 0.20964, err nil;
  wc = 0.704 -> Kp 0.06043 Ki 0.008509 Kd 0.11053 Tf 0.18289, err nil.
Both closed loops are stable (char roots in z) but the directly evaluated loop (pidtuneSignedMargins on (0, pi/Dt]) has min signed PM -157 deg / -77 deg at another crossover, |S| peak 103 / 9.9.

Neighbouring explicit wc (0.53 and below, 0.81 and above) return unattainable.
Question (MATLAB parity): should an explicit-wc design that crosses over again with negative PM / |S| > 4 be rejected (gate) or returned as MATLAB would with its achieved margins? Files: pidtune.go (Pidtune, pidtuneRun.design/check).

data.title: pidtune back-off gate rejects robust designs at positive-phase crossovers (signed PM); TFE7I2 exposes PD/PID/PIDF losses
data.body:
Branch fix/pidtune-wave8 (after 70c9a83). TFE7I2 moved plantCrossoverFreq's pole fallback for discrete high-pass plants (|G|<1, gain rising to z=-1) from base's unitless 0.5|z| to min(0.5|ln z|/Dt, 0.1pi/Dt). On base the first, ungated design at the old pick happened to be stable; on the branch the first design is unstable and every back-off step fails pidtuneGate.check with a negative signed PM, so Pidtune(G, f, 0, nil) returns ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable.

Repro (Dt in seconds, wc=0, nil opts):
T0 num [-0.04189665061210819 0.07677735137479592 -0.03510307300396654] den [1 0.9371514351204928 0.13383773145948022] Dt 0.0757765515708101
T2 num [0.02168291613348848 -0.040003288616014994 0.018372574831365913] den [1 1.0961478669592766 0.30038125589712455] Dt 0.06586027470121651
Families PD, PID, PIDF on T0 and T2: base returned designs, branch errors.
Base oracle (pidtuneOracleStable + pidtuneSignedMargins over (1e-8, pi/Dt)):
T0 PD Kp -9184 Kd -5228 Tf .0569: stable, |S| 0.51, signed PM -165.8 (classical 180-|angle L| = 166)
T0 PID/PIDF Kp -490 Ki -807: stable, |S| 0.99, signed PM [104, -61] (classical min 61)
T2 PD Kp 31870 Kd 5843: stable, |S| 0.59, signed -125 (classical 125)
T2 PID/PIDF Kp 1882 Ki 8707: stable, |S| 0.56, signed [145, -130] (classical 130)
Branch: e.g. T0 PID back-off: "PID design at wc=0.4146 has phase margin -130 at a gain crossover", every step to 4e-6 rejected at about -37.5. Explicit-wc scan: T0 PID at wc 0.398 is stable, classical PM 128, |S| 0.58.
Cause: pidtuneGate.check (pidTuningCrossingsOn margins) uses MATLAB allmargin-style signed PM (180+angle wrapped), which is negative whenever the loop phase at crossover is positive, as in these high-pass loops where |L| rises through 1 far from -1. Test oracle pidtuneDenseRobust uses classical 180-|angle L|. Needs owner decision on gate convention (or a different fallback start).
Not regressions: T1 (num [-0.011302534772155698 0.019672327226871213 -0.008550308672972825] den [1 1.3218336193087052 0.4064581673333586] Dt 0.6967602637285988) PD base design has classical PM 28.6, |S| 2.03 (below 60 target); T1 PID/PIDF failed on base too.
Note: TunePID shares findCrossoverFreq; on these 3 plants base TunePID I/PI succeeded and branch errors, but base I had |S| 4.1/5.7/9.4 and PI |S| 43/6.9, so not robust by the |S|<=4 bar.

data.title: nyquist: oracle-stable s^2 + three small real poles errors (L unevaluable near origin)
data.body:
Found reviewing fix/nyquist-wave8 (e1a193f; YJINK6/3NHTS4/5IT7DX/RMVV47). Pre-existing: base b083afe and branch both error (value->error on oracle-stable loop). arm64.
Repro (public API): P = num/den via TransferFunc.StateSpace, P.SetInputDelay(0.0029979187523625347), Feedback(P,nil,-1).IsStable()
 num=[5.220393384215734 9.189246525763267 6.390061731529178 1.4385802578468079 0.06731719072338148]
 den=[1 -0.0046923109514164976 -1.0433945828807056e-05 7.829332736549319e-11 0 0]   (s^2 · poles 6.3369e-3, 7.4786e-6, -1.6521e-3)
