data.title: DCGain transfer-limit fallback wrong for integrators (Inf/finite/sign, dropped z=1 pole, near-singular solve)
data.body:
Found in wave 11 (branch fix/wave11).

DCGain: the transfer-function-limit fallback (dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit → rationalLimitAtReal) returns finite values or the wrong Inf sign for coupled integrators, because of roundoff in the TF coefficients. (a) fzDecode(0xab, {-40,10,0.4,1.5,42,0,0,2,-75,2,0,-204,-0.15625,-1,20,-17.5}) (discrete, two exact z=1 modes, C≈1e-6): DCGain[0,1] = 1.4194, exact +Inf; both arches. (b) fzDecode(0xd4, {84.6,1,-44.5,28,-78,34,-87,65.5,0,-90,0.37,0,-1.1111111111111112,-10,-0.4,23}): A has three exactly zero rows and B rows are nonzero; DCGain[0,0] = 1.73e16 finite, exact +Inf. (c) fzDecode(0xa2, {-92.33333333333333,36,33.5,3.4,0,0,-38,0.5,130,81,0,32.5,-100,-10,-5,6}): DCGain[0,0] = +Inf on arm64 and -Inf on amd64; exact is -Inf (num ~ -8.0e12·s, den ~ 1e8·s²). The numerical TF has den s¹ coefficient -0.0011 and num s⁰ coefficient -2726, where both are exactly 0. The arch-dependent result shows the cause is roundoff. All three contradict the DCGain doc (integrator entries are infinite for every realization). FuzzDCGain catches all three.

DCGain/TransferFunction drop a z=1 pole when another pole is tiny (wrong finite value; MATLAB gives Inf). Repro: NewFromSlices(3,1,1, A=[1 0 -3.1622776601683795; 0 1 -3.1622776601683795; 0 0 eps], B=[-0.38211320287195655 0.7882242424655154 0.8038113259779769]', C=[-0.9291407314223547 0.6502534890410231 0.5087003937751763], D=-0.23623091926062198, dt=100). With eps=1e-20, 1e-40 or 1e-69, DCGain=0.68521 and the TF den is [1 -eps], so the z=1 pole is gone. With eps=0, 1e-12, 1e-8 or 0.1 it gives +Inf correctly. Exact residue at z=1 is c1b1+c2b2+(c1+c2)a·b3/(1-eps) ≈ 1.576 ≠ 0. Files: response.go dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit/rationalTransferFunction path. Found by FuzzDCGain, input kind=0x61 vals=[-40 1 0.2 1.5 0 0 0 0.5 59 54 0 -552 -10 -10 -5 -10].

Pre-existing: the DCGain transfer-limit fallback (response.go: dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit -> dcGainByDecoupledSingularModes / rationalTransferFunction) reports +/-Inf for an integrator that cannot reach the output, depending on the scale of B or C. Repro on base 1ea79ad, case 1719 above with C multiplied by 2^10: G[0,0] = +Inf where the exact value is finite (about 3.31e-9*2^10), because row 0 of C is exactly zero on the two integrator states, whose A columns are zero. Case 207 above with B multiplied by 2^25: G[0,1] = +Inf where the exact value is about -2.2e-11*2^25 (C has an exact zero on the integrator state). Cause: the cancellation at s=0 for each input/output pair is not detected once B or C is moderately scaled relative to A. Oracle: structural, since the integrator states have zero A columns and zero C entries.

DCGain accepts a near-singular (I-A) Solve for near-cancelled integrators. Repro: New(A=[[0.2772706061286758,-0.29385449949935655],[0.6983526834182192,1.2839431743057481]], B=[-2.436691822351444; 2.3545054168716004], C=[-0.05023449497436656, 0.28984069544431224], D=0.7195914212138912, Dt=0.1).DCGain() returns 0.5577. The model is a similarity transform of 0.8048(z-1)/((z-1)(z-0.5612)) + D, whose limit is 2.5538, and G(1+d) for d in [1e-11, 1e-6] is 2.5538. det(I-A) = 3e-16, poles {0.5612, 1-8e-16}, zeros {1-2e-16, -0.557}. Files: response.go DCGain (the X.Solve branch has no conditioning check before dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit). Pre-existing on 1ea79ad. Since 5YRXMC's structural reduction, an entry can now also reach this path from a model that base handled correctly. Decide by MATLAB dcgain on the same float model.

data.title: DCGain dcGainPolyTol absolute floor 1 makes small-scale integrators vanish
data.body:
Found in wave 11 (branch fix/wave11).

DCGain: dcGainPolyTol has an absolute floor of 1, so small-scale integrators vanish. Files: response.go dcGainPolyTol (scale := 1.0), polynomialRootMultiplicityValue and trimLeadingNearZero. Minimal repro: sys, _ := NewFromSlices(2,1,1, []float64{0,1,0,-1}, []float64{0,1}, []float64{1e-14,0}, []float64{0}, 0); sys.DCGain() → 0. The model is G = 1e-14/(s(s+1)), so the exact gain is +Inf. With D=1 it returns 1 instead of +Inf. The discrete version (A=[1 1;0 0.5], dt=1) behaves the same. Reproduces on arm64 and amd64. Cause: the numerator [0,0,1e-14] is trimmed as near-zero relative to max(1,|coef|) and treated as identically zero.

data.title: Stabsep misclassifies a double stable pole arriving as a 2x2 Schur block
data.body:
Found in wave 11 (branch fix/wave11).

Stabsep puts a stable mode in Unstable when a repeated real eigenvalue arrives as a 2x2 Schur block. Repro (test pkg): s := fzDecode(t, 0xb2, [16]float64{0, -1.5, 1, 2, -4, -3, 0, 2, -17, -1, 44.9, 0, -10, -10, -10, -47}); res, _ := Stabsep(s.System(t, fzSysOpts{})) gives Stable order 1 / Unstable order 4, want 2/3 (intended poles 0.162, 6.16, 1e-4 unstable; -10 twice stable; condT=1.27, decidable). Unstable.Poles() contains -9.999999999999995. Deterministic in a normal arm64 build; correct on amd64. File: eigdecomp.go orderSchurGroupFirst (~L226-248). Evidence and hypothesis: sys.Poles() shows the double -10 as -10+/-4.0e-16i, a 2x2 block. After Dtrexc moves it, the block likely splits into two 1x1 blocks, size = schurBlockSize(t,n,placed) becomes 1, and i += size steps past the second -10, which never gets placed. Second instance: fzDecode(t, 0xcb, [16]float64{0.6, -2, 37.7, 3.5999999999999996, 0.2, 1, 0, 82, -0.06989700043360188, 38.2, 1.7, 0, -10, -10, 76, -50}) is discrete, with a near-triple cluster at z~0 and a well-separated spectrum (0.93 vs 29.6). Under go test -fuzz on arm64 it returns orders 3/3 with z=-5.6e-15 in Unstable. A normal arm64 build refuses with ErrSchurFailed (the scale<1e-12 check, eigdecomp.go:186). amd64 returns the correct 4/2. FuzzStabsep treats ErrSchurFailed as an expected skip, so this error-instead-of-value case only shows up as the wrong-order crash in fuzz mode.

Stabsep puts one of a double stable pole -10 into the Unstable part. Repro: fzDecode(kind=0xb2, vals=[0 -1.5 1 2 -4 -3 0 2 0 -1 9 0 -50 0 -10 -10]), a continuous model with n=5, m=2, p=3. Intended poles are 0.162, 6.162, 1e-4 and -10 (double); Poles() returns -10±4e-16i. Stabsep returns Stable poles [-10] and Unstable poles [-10, 6.16, 0.162, 1e-4]; expected 2 stable / 3 unstable. Files: stabsep code (Schur reordering/classification of a near-real 2x2 block). Found by FuzzStabsep.

data.title: HinfNorm underestimates peak (up to 30%) on badly scaled / tiny-pole models
data.body:
Found in wave 11 (branch fix/wave11).

HinfNorm returns a norm up to 30% below the true peak despite its documented 1e-10 accuracy. Repro (test pkg): sd := fzSeed{N:3, M:1, P:1, Mag:[3]float64{-8, 4}, Damp:[3]float64{2.5, 1}, Shear:-10, Rot:0.37, In:fzNoDelay, Out:fzNoDelay, IO:fzNoDelay, Tau:fzNoDelay}; k, v := sd.encode(); s := fzDecode(t, k, v). Poles are -3.16e-9+/-9.49e-9i and -1e4; Decidable() is true. HinfNorm(s.System(t, fzSysOpts{})) returns 168.76 at omega=7.197e-9. fzExactResponse gives sigma = 198.2 at 8e-9, 228.6 at 9e-9 and 239.35 at 1e-8. Same result on amd64 (168.76). Second instance, 0.1% low on a broad maximum: fzDecode(t, 0xc0, [16]float64{61, 0, 0.3, 0, -0.2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0.05555555555555555, 80.5, -29, -0.20833333333333334, -10, -35, -86}) returns 4.3930e-5 at omega=0.003992, while the exact value is 4.3973e-5 at omega=0.004283; float LU and exact agree to 4e-9 there. File: norms.go HinfNorm / peakGain (Bruinsma-Steinbuch path, ~L290-L400). Lead: three separate crashers with poles at |p|~1e-8 all returned omega~7.1969e-09, which looks like a grid floor or initial-sample limit rather than a convergence failure. Discrete models are affected too (crasher with dt=1e-4, poles near z=1).

HinfNorm underestimates the peak by 6e-5 relative; the doc promises 1e-10. Repro: fzDecode(kind=0xc0, vals=[0 0 2.6999999999999997 0 -0.2 0 0 0 21 -7.5 2.5 -56 -10 -10 -10 -10]), a continuous SISO model with n=6, poles from -1e5 to -0.00315, ‖A‖≈5e4, C≈1e-6, D=0. HinfNorm=1.0641783e-4 at ω=0.0012043, while the exact rational σmax at ω=0.00112285 is 1.0642417e-4. Files: norms.go HinfNorm (Bruinsma–Steinbuch on a badly scaled model). Found by FuzzHinfNorm.

data.title: Zeros inaccurate: eig(A-BD^-1C) shortcut and badly I/O-scaled staircase
data.body:
Found in wave 11 (branch fix/wave11).

Zeros: eig(A − B·D⁻¹·C) shortcut in mimoZeros is inaccurate when ‖B·D⁻¹·C‖ ≫ ‖A‖. File: zeros.go:165-183. The shortcut is taken whenever |det D| ≥ 1e-14, an absolute threshold that ignores conditioning. Repro: s := fzDecode(t, 0x8a, {0,0,0,0,71,0,-17,1e-06,0,-10,0.37,0.4,-10,-12,-5,-10}); s.System(t, fzSysOpts{}).Zeros() → -36.351222960513866 and -191.10861455360867. Exact roots of det P(s) (big.Rat with 512-bit Newton) are -36.34051311530382 and -191.1041566901274, a relative error of 3e-4. The staircase + Dggev path on the same data gives -36.34051311525194 and -191.10415669003385, so the error is in the shortcut. Reproduces on arm64 and amd64 (amd64 gives -36.3546). The data are D≈1e-6, C≈1e6, n=4, m=p=2. FuzzZeros fails on it with pencil σmin 6.7e-3 against scale 490.

Zeros inaccurate for a badly I/O-scaled square model (C≈1e5, D≈1e-6). Repro: fzDecode(kind=0x8a, vals=[0 0 0 0 0 0 -11 1e-06 0 -10 41.37 0.4 -10 -10 -10 -50]) (n=4, m=p=2). Zeros returns -75.917567598 and -178.524940163; the exact det P(s) roots (big.Rat bisection) are -75.917894563 and -178.525340687, about 4e-6 relative error. Unscaled pencil σmin at the computed zero is 3.5e-6 against ‖P‖≈2.1e5 (normwise backward error 1.7e-11, far above eps); at the exact root it is 5.6e-14. Files: zeros.go mimoZeros/zerosStaircase. Found by FuzzZeros. Possibly a scaling/rank-tolerance issue in the staircase.

Found in wave 10 (PR pending, branch fix/wave10).

TestAllMarginPhaseCrossNyquistZeroCluster still skips the Nyquist check when |N(-1)| <= 1e-13*scale. In those exact-(z+1) cases AllMargin reports π with GM about 290-570 dB, and |L(-1)| is up to 84 times the first-order coefficient-rounding bound. Whether such a π crossover is real depends on unrounded coefficients; MATLAB parity there was not checked. File: margin_nyquist_zero_test.go.


Wave 11 attempt (fix/margins-wave11 commits d2608c7 1fa338e 399b534) NOT merged; final review blocking:

{"desc": "Discrete loops with an integer I/O delay now report \u03c0 as a phase crossover even when the loop's exact L(\u22121) > 0. Base handled these correctly. Root cause is in margin.go nyquistPhaseCrossings: `aboveNoise(pointAt(-1), ..., !r.eval.sys.HasDelay())` passes nyq=false for any delayed loop, which switches off the `real(h) >= 0` test entirely. In the same change, nyqTol was widened from 1e-7 to 45\u00b0 for every loop without internal delays. So when z's rounding (fl(\u03c0)) puts a tiny positive real L within 45\u00b0 of \u2212180\u00b0, a delayed loop accepts \u03c0. Also, h from ddSISOResponseNoise(r.eval.sys, \u00b7) is the response without the delay, so for an odd delay k its sign is wrong anyway. Fix direction (not implemented): apply the sign test on the absorbed realization, or multiply h by (\u22121)^k. Caveat: |L(\u22121)| here is about 2 orders below coefficient-rounding noise. But for loops without delays the branch enforces the sign of the coefficients as given in exactly this regime (case 730 with delay 0 and 2 is right), so this is the branch contradicting its own CMVMWK rule, not a disagreement about semantics.", "evidence": "Repro: num=[-0.011204978782742445,-0.05984870582771428,-0.1273450360277268,-0.13499266094431892,-0.07132014320260238,-0.015028791241038416], den=[1,-0.21579742457949225,-0.6185444651785603,0.005936187798701448,-0.0008252966705985937,0.09760593278156476,0.0066096485407187225,-0.017048862169604856], Dt=1, tf.StateSpace(), sys.InputDelay=[k]. Two oracles agree: exact big-float tf\u00b7(\u22121)^k and bigSISOResponse of sys.AbsorbDelay() at z=\u22121 both give L(\u22121)=+3.358e-18 for k=1 and k=3, and \u22123.358e-18 for k=0 and k=2. Branch 399b534, k=1: PCF [1.0154,2.2795,\u03c0] GM [...,349.48]. k=3: PCF [0.7138,1.6530,2.5139,\u03c0] GM [...,349.48]. Both wrong. Base 1ea79ad: k=1 [1.0154,2.2795] and k=3 [0.7138,1.6530,2.5139], no \u03c0, which is correct. In a seeded sweep of 3000 cluster cases, the delay family (about 750 cases) had 3 of these regressions: 730 (delay 3), 2110 (delay 2, exact L(\u22121)=+1.82e-20 with D=0, so it is not just the delay parity), and 1902 (delay 1, D=2.58, absorbed ss L(\u22121)=+8.37e-16). There were no other base-ok\u2192branch-wrong cases across both sweeps (5000 cases)."}

Notes from the attempt:

Design note, not a bug: when D ≠ 0, AllMargin still applies the coefficient-rounding gate at π. So an ss model passed in directly, whose own L(−1) is negative but below that bound (about 1e-16), reports no π, where MATLAB on that ss would evaluate the values as given. This is kept on purpose to preserve the 6OPXWW-pinned TF behaviour, because TF→SS rounds num − D·den. Revisit only if TF provenance becomes available to AllMargin. Files: margin.go nyquistPhaseCrossings, margin_nyquist_zero_test.go TestAllMarginNyquistZeroClusterNoise.

Owner decision (not a bug), CMVMWK at D≠0: 'MATLAB on the coefficients as given' cannot be applied to biproper loops because AllMargin receives only *System, and rounding C = num − D·den makes ss L(−1) about 1 ulp of |D|. Case 406 (tf −5.1e-18) and 6OPXWW case 1 (tf exactly 0) both realize to −2^-59. The branch keeps the gate: π is dropped when |L(−1)| ≤ the coefficient-rounding bound. Changing this needs either a tf-aware AllMargin entry point that keeps num/den, or reversing the pinned 6OPXWW cases 1–2 in TestAllMarginNyquistZeroClusterNoise to accept π at about 355/319 dB from ss noise. Files: /Users/josephj/workspace/controlsys/.claude/worktrees/wf_29c66a72-05a-18/margin.go (nyquistPhaseCrossings, aboveNoise(pointAt(-1), D≠0)), /Users/josephj/workspace/controlsys/.claude/worktrees/wf_29c66a72-05a-18/margin_nyquist_zero_test.go (TestAllMarginNyquistBiproperClusterGate).

data.title: Pidtune retry/unshaped designs must meet the owner bar; search wc upward before unattainable (unstable plants)
data.body:
Found in wave 12. The PS6S32/IBWZGV/X7DDPS track reported that the retry path, and the unshaped rule, gated only on |S| and the existence of a crossing, return designs below the owner bar of classical PM >= 58.5 deg and |S| <= 4.
- Canonical case: Pidtune(1/(s-1), P or PI, 0) returns PM 45/42 deg. Its only crossover is at wc_auto ~0.9.
- About 301 of 11997 auto returns in the sampled population come from the retry, with worst classical margins of 10-58 deg.
- Zero-DC continuous P designs fall below the bar through the |S|-only unshaped rule. Example: pidtuneBackoffPlant(Poly{1.4392005301712567,0,0}, Poly{1,8.24762471156669,20.7899930...}).

## Decision (advisor, 2026-10-19; owner said open questions go to the advisor)
- Every returned auto design, retry and unshaped included, must meet the same bar (oracle-stable, classical PM >= 58.5 deg at every crossover, |S| <= 4).
- Before returning ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable when back-off fails, add a bounded UPWARD wc search through the same gate. Go up to about 1e3 x wc_auto, capped at Nyquist for discrete plants.
- Rationale: on unstable plants, PM grows with wc. For 1/(s-1), P with Kp=2 gives |L|=1 at sqrt(3), PM exactly 60 deg, |S|=1 everywhere, closed-loop pole -1. Back-off lowers wc, which moves the wrong way. Returning "unattainable" when Kp=2 exists would be a parity failure.
- Verify that 1/(s-1) P finds Kp ~2 with PM ~60. Report how much of the ~300 retry population gets a design that meets the bar via the upward search, and how much becomes an honest unattainable.
- If the upward search also fails, unattainable is correct.
- Fold the wave 12 reports "unstable plants still get fragile auto designs" and "zero-DC P below the bar via the unshaped rule" into this task.
Core priority for wave 13. Files: pidtune.go (pidtuneRun.attempt retry, unshaped, back-off loop).

data.title: Norms: support descriptor models (E≠I) in H2Norm/HinfNorm/Norm — MATLAB parity gap
data.body:
Found in wave 12. H2Norm, HinfNorm and Norm(2/Inf) return ErrDescriptorUnsupported for a descriptor model with E≠I, even for a nonsingular diagonal E (descriptor.go requireStandard, called in norms.go). MATLAB's norm, hinfnorm and getPeakGain accept dss models.

## Decision (advisor, 2026-10-19)
This is a parity gap, not a wrong value: the documented error is allowed under the Go error pattern. Treat it as feature work, scheduled after the correctness backlog.
- Step 1: support nonsingular E by converting to standard form and reusing the existing norm paths. Add a kappa(E) guard so an ill-conditioned E returns an error, not garbage.
- Step 2 (follow-up): singular E. First check what MATLAB hinfnorm and norm return for improper dss models, then implement to match.

Found in wave 11 (branch fix/wave11).

Zeros: eig(A − B·D⁻¹·C) shortcut in mimoZeros is inaccurate when ‖B·D⁻¹·C‖ ≫ ‖A‖. File: zeros.go:165-183. The shortcut is taken whenever |det D| ≥ 1e-14, an absolute threshold that ignores conditioning. Repro: s := fzDecode(t, 0x8a, {0,0,0,0,71,0,-17,1e-06,0,-10,0.37,0.4,-10,-12,-5,-10}); s.System(t, fzSysOpts{}).Zeros() → -36.351222960513866 and -191.10861455360867. Exact roots of det P(s) (big.Rat with 512-bit Newton) are -36.34051311530382 and -191.1041566901274, a relative error of 3e-4. The staircase + Dggev path on the same data gives -36.34051311525194 and -191.10415669003385, so the error is in the shortcut. Reproduces on arm64 and amd64 (amd64 gives -36.3546). The data are D≈1e-6, C≈1e6, n=4, m=p=2. FuzzZeros fails on it with pencil σmin 6.7e-3 against scale 490.

Zeros inaccurate for a badly I/O-scaled square model (C≈1e5, D≈1e-6). Repro: fzDecode(kind=0x8a, vals=[0 0 0 0 0 0 -11 1e-06 0 -10 41.37 0.4 -10 -10 -10 -50]) (n=4, m=p=2). Zeros returns -75.917567598 and -178.524940163; the exact det P(s) roots (big.Rat bisection) are -75.917894563 and -178.525340687, about 4e-6 relative error. Unscaled pencil σmin at the computed zero is 3.5e-6 against ‖P‖≈2.1e5 (normwise backward error 1.7e-11, far above eps); at the exact root it is 5.6e-14. Files: zeros.go mimoZeros/zerosStaircase. Found by FuzzZeros. Possibly a scaling/rank-tolerance issue in the staircase.

Wave 12 attempt (fix/linalg-wave12 commits 3373ec0 80cdb0e fed3cf1) NOT merged. The final review was blocking: the staircase+QZ path gives wrong zeros, or drops one, where base's eig(A-BD^-1C) was correct to 1e-13. See the "SPWBDX redo" task filed in wave 12 for what was learned.

data.title: CORE: sisoEval.at fails singular or snaps +Inf where FreqResponse resolves (AllMargin, delay)
data.body:
Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12). Shared margin evaluator (margin.go sisoEval.at / evalWithPoleLimitGated, ddGate) reports singular complex matrix or a snapped +Inf with nil error at frequencies FreqResponse evaluates exactly; reaches AllMargin on delayed near-double-pair loops (172/200 family g0, 76/200 HNOB6S family). Pidtune gate has a local evalPlantAt workaround (e3d0a6d); fix belongs in the evaluator. See also the TunePID task (same evaluator, separate unresolved-vs-evaluated constraint).

[w12 #52 pidtune/FI3ZIB] sisoEval.at reports singular where FreqResponse resolves (margin.go, frequency_pole.go). Repro: G=1.1974308853542987e-16/[1 -6.184746550403649 16.242438259051475 -23.437999081676736 20.022569140290482 -10.09289718715969 2.766371287397997 -0.31573586749987936], dt=0.01, built as a TF then StateSpace(). newSISOEval(p).at(w) fails at w = 1e-6, 1e-4, 1e-3, 0.01 and 0.1043 with 'singular complex matrix: singular matrix in transformation', while p.FreqResponse at the same w matches an extended-precision evaluation of num/den to about 1e-15 relative. The stability screen, pidtuneGainSign and the margin code share this evaluator. The pidtune gate now works around it with an evalPlantAt fallback (e3d0a6d); the solver's singularity threshold, or an opt-in to its extended/dd path, is the broader fix.

[w12 #54 pidtune/review] sisoEval.at returns a snapped +Inf with no error well off any pole. Repro: dt=0.01, num [6.110773630519141e-14 3.4198170787824316e-15], den [1 -5.71016988999306 13.887907770588715 -18.645468986193702 14.92072833819654 -7.1153754170879235 1.8719233030765783 -0.20954511858714697]. eval := newSISOEval(plant); eval.at(1.9111864778082823e-05) gives +Inf+0i with eval.err == nil. plant.FreqResponse gives 0.000147-0.321i (|G| 0.32), consistent with neighbouring samples. The slowest pole, 0.99999999678, maps to about 3e-7 rad/s, roughly 60x below. Files: margin.go:124-144 (evalWithPoleLimitGated with ddGate{snap: true}). The pidtune gate now works around it; other callers of sisoEval.at (margins, TunePID) may still see bogus Inf spikes.

[w12 #19 nyquist/HNOB6S] AllMargin still errors on the same plants after this fix (margin.go, another track; not fixed). Repro: P = TF num [0.11076720035335656 -6.130423072572409 -1.025734097506373 2.740715007718803], den [1 2.511832216255788e-06 6.992159985979351e-07 8.781546547116625e-13 1.2222520172891677e-13], input delay 0.26598736421075958. AllMargin(P) returns 'loop response at ω=0.0005408987382166641: singular complex matrix'. Case 2 of the task (num [0.7888666874022671 3.8654855207558545 -0.12212921074024871 -0.1829508091600904], den [1 1.4334915553463322e-07 6.39209078346261e-08 4.581503711340512e-15 1.0214704504120125e-15], tau 0.00039642299973125048) errors at ω=1.0567e-4. Cause: the same wide band of conditioning failures in the double solve. The margin sisoEval (margin.go at/evalWithPoleLimitGated) has no matching relaxation. The task's probe reported 76/200 AllMargin failures for this family.

[w12 #28 nyquist/review1] Pre-existing: AllMargin errors 'loop response at ω=…: singular complex matrix' on most delayed loops with near-double lightly damped low-frequency pairs (172/200 in family g0 of the sweep, identical on base and branch). Example: the HNOB6S repro plant with num [0.11076720035335656 -6.130423072572409 -1.025734097506373 2.740715007718803], den [1 2.511832216255788e-06 6.992159985979351e-07 8.781546547116625e-13 1.2222520172891677e-13], tau 0.26598736421075958. The dd fallback added for IsStable and HinfNorm does not reach the AllMargin crossover sweep. File: margin.go (AllMargin loop response).

data.title: CORE: TunePID value->error on stable near-z=1 discrete plants (sticky eval.at singular)
data.body:
Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12). TunePID fails with singular complex matrix / +Inf plant gain where Pidtune designs robustly (65/420 dstable, 392/420 discrete-integrator calls). Constraint from IP3XIC (#6): simply giving TunePID eval FreqResponse semantics breaks the blind-gate back-off tests; the PID track must separate unresolved from evaluated samples, and the phase walk/crossing samplers should use try or a FreqResponse fallback.

[w12 #1 margins/IP3XIC] TunePID returns value->error on a plant whose loop FreqResponse resolves (PID track). Repro: TF Num {{{k*2.761969998249568e-16, k*2.6332895798497864e-16, k*6.196985260193668e-17}}}, Den {{1, -5.388323209156541, 12.045405202918547, -14.292531743733242, 9.488502158799133, -3.339413745774066, 0.486361336946173}}, Dt 0.01, then StateSpace(). TunePID(ctx, sys, P|I|PI|PID|PIDF, PIDTuningOptions{}) fails with 'loop response at w=5.640647128789107e-05: singular complex matrix' for k=100, and at w=4.954e-6 for k=10 and w=5.639e-5 for k=1e4. Stack: TunePID -> tunePID -> tunePIDScan -> hard eval.at (pid_tuning.go) on a non-extended sisoEval. The double solve fails over w in [~1e-9, 1.8e-4], but FreqResponse and an exact fzExactResponse oracle give finite L. Pidtune finds designs on the same plant. Files: pid_tuning.go (tunePIDScan, evalFailed), margin.go (sisoEval.at, ddGate.limit). Evidence: if only newRationalLoop's eval keeps ddGate.limit (TunePID's eval gets FreqResponse semantics), TunePID P on k=100 gives |Kp*L(wc)|=1 and a phase margin that match the exact oracle, and all margin tests pass. But TestTunePIDBackOffScansPastBlindGates cases (z-0.95)/(z-1)^3 and (z-0.99)/((z-1)^3(z-0.72)) PIDF then report unattainable: the evaluated deep gates reject every crossover down to 0.01156 rad/s (5152 evaluations). The back-off's blind-gate logic depends on those gates failing, so the PID track needs to separate 'unresolved' from 'evaluated' before eval can match FreqResponse.

[w12 #6 margins/review] Coordinator decision for IP3XIC: close it with the doc correction (baebd3d) plus the regression test (33c7a84). Making the non-extended evaluator match FreqResponse breaks TestAllMarginLeadIntegratorSweep, TestAllMarginNyquistPoleCluster, TestAllMarginNoCrossoverBesideNyquistCluster and TestTunePIDBackOffScansPastBlindGates. The only rule that separates the repro from those cases is pole multiplicity at DC, which would be an ad hoc threshold.

[w12 #43 pidtune/GK5SUC] TunePID phase walk fails at wc0*1e-6 (same sticky-at class as GK5SUC, one layer down). Repro: plant A (num [1.5379663637764417e-12 -3.387450861436736e-13], den [1 -3.9146780141541093 5.7453934609919255 -3.7467528452104566 0.9160373983726545], dt 0.01; DC 84.4; wc0 0.0025038). TunePID PI fails on arm64 and amd64, and TunePID PID fails on amd64 only, with 'loop response at ω=2.503790234594087e-09: singular complex matrix'. Plant B (num [1.7295311989236164e-12], den [1 -2.999890083275418 2.999780168026009 -0.999890084750586], dt 0.01): TunePID PI, PD, PDF, PID and PIDF fail at ω=1.0909e-08 = wc0*1e-6. Pidtune returns robust designs on both plants, so these are value-to-error cases. Files: pid_tuning.go, pidTuningUnwrappedPhase / pidTuningPhaseWalk (start w*1e-6, ~line 1484) and pidTuningPhaseCrossing(eval.at, ..., wc0*1e-6, ...) (~line 1325), which call eval.at, not try.

[w12 #44 pidtune/GK5SUC] TunePID P and I on plant B (num [1.7295311989236164e-12], den [1 -2.999890083275418 2.999780168026009 -0.999890084750586], dt 0.01) return 'plant gain (+Inf+0i) at crossover is zero or not finite: invalid argument' at wc0=0.010909. newSISOEval(p).try(wc0) gives a finite -0.753+0.658i there, and Pidtune P/I succeed. This may be the known false-pole +Inf-with-nil-error class from frequency_pole.go (poleSpacing/poleLimitInto), reached through tuneOneGain's evaluation path in pid_tuning.go. Not diagnosed further.

[w12 #59 pidtune/review1] TunePID fails with 'loop response at ω=...: singular complex matrix' on stable discrete plants with poles near z=1, where Pidtune now designs robustly. Repro: dt 0.01, num [1.1201261000572445e-12 7.985425046796576e-13], den [1 -4.956471969268471 9.826418031565801 -9.740421021787181 4.827475826360807 -0.95700086687092]. TunePID fails for every family at ω=1.257e-3, while Pidtune gives P Kp 0.0542 at PM 65 deg and PID at 60 deg. It fails the same way on 65 of 420 dstable TunePID calls and 392 of 420 discrete-integrator calls, identical on 2e4a07d. Files: pid_tuning.go (TunePID phase walk / tuneAt); a sample is evaluated with the sticky eval.at past pidTuningDCSign.

[w12 #62 pidtune/review2] TunePID fails with an error on stable discrete plants that Pidtune designs robustly. The cause is a sticky eval.err in samplers after pidTuningDCSign, so GK5SUC's fix does not reach it. It happens on base and on the branch. Repro 1 (dt 0.01): num {1.6478992314667082e-12}, den {1,-3.9988962961964294,5.996689296298131,-3.9966897039442033,0.998896703842506}. TunePID fails for every family with 'loop response at ω=0.0010899379808273421: singular complex matrix', while branch Pidtune returns all 7 families robust (PM 59.7 to 60.8, |S| <= 2.07). Repro 2 (dt 0.01): num {8.58763892349696e-12,-2.307232265714587e-12}, den {1,-3.997506422481467,5.9925206599047645,-3.992522052100717,0.9975078146774358}. TunePID PI/PD/PDF/PID/PIDF fail at ω=1.38e-7 (wc·1e-6, the start of the phase walk), while Pidtune returns all families robust. File: pid_tuning.go (TunePID: pidTuningPhaseCrossing / pidTuningPhaseWalk use eval.at; the lo := wc0*1e-6 sampling near line 1116/1325). Suggested fix: sample through try, or a FreqResponse fallback, as the gate now does.

data.title: CORE: DCGain +Inf vs exact finite FreqResponse(0) at near-integrator discrete DC points
data.body:
Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12). Owner decision needed between Option A (finite everywhere, MATLAB parity, retarget TestPidtuneDisplacedIntegratorDCSign) and Option B (Inf everywhere); also whether a z=1 cluster rule is wanted in poleSpacing. Includes the comment fix in pidtune_wave9_test.go.

[w12 #2 margins/IP3XIC] DCGain returns +Inf for a discrete plant with no pole at z=1 (response.go:403, discrete path). Repro: same TF as above with k=1, then StateSpace(), then sys.DCGain() gives +Inf, and Bandwidth(sys,-3) fails with 'DC gain is +Inf, bandwidth undefined'. The exact realization value from fzExactResponse at z=1 is 0.20837663904890938, and the TF coefficients agree: N(1)/D(1) = 6.0150e-16/2.8866e-15. The nearest pole is 0.9999998669 (1-1.3e-7), not an integrator; FreqResponse at w=6.3e-7 gives |G| of about 0.203. Cause: the (I-A) X.Solve fails on condition, and the code falls back to dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit, which returns +Inf. MATLAB parity requires a finite value, e.g. a double-double or pole-aware fallback before declaring an integrator.

[w12 #10 freq/4M7RB3] Decision needed (coordinator/owner), DCGain vs FreqResponse at a near-integrator DC point. Repro: TF Num {2.761969998249568e-16, 2.6332895798497864e-16, 6.196985260193668e-17}, Den {1,-5.388323209156541,12.045405202918547,-14.292531743733242,9.488502158799133,-3.339413745774066,0.486361336946173}, Dt 0.01; and Num {1.8748015424080903e-16}, Den {1,-6.656527066165689,18.974082402962605,-30.020939359334676,28.473509438245436,-16.187809823253666,5.1075991528389695,-0.6899147452929796}, Dt 0.1. DCGain gives +Inf; FreqResponse(0) gives 0.2084 and 0.3377, which are exact for the stored coefficients (true poles 2.71e-8 and 3.59e-7 inside z=1). Option A, finite everywhere: change response.go DCGain so a near-singular Solve with a successful double-double evaluation returns the exact finite gain; this breaks the premise of TestPidtuneDisplacedIntegratorDCSign (pidtune_wave9_test.go, 2e4a07d), which relies on DCGain=+Inf, so that test would need re-targeting. Option B, Inf everywhere: FreqResponse would need a DC conditioning test (cond(I-A) > 1/eps means a pole) in frequency_pole.go. That is not MATLAB parity and swaps exact values for Inf. Files: response.go (DCGain, dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit), frequency_pole.go (evalWithPoleLimitGated, poleSpacing near).

[w12 #11 freq/4M7RB3] Minor: the pidtune_wave9_test.go comment in TestPidtuneDisplacedIntegratorDCSign says case 1's pole 'lies 3.4e-5 outside z = 1'. That is the computed eigenvalue; the exact root of the stored denominator is 3.586e-7 inside z=1 (400-bit Newton). The comment should say computed pole.

[w12 #12 freq/review] Scope note (not fixed): FreqResponse at z=1 misses a rounded discrete repeated integrator, and DCGain now copies that. Repro: den = Poly{1,-1}.Mul(Poly{1,-1}).Mul(Poly{1,-0.9999}) = [1 -2.9999000000000002 2.9998 -0.9999], num {1}, Dt 0.1, then StateSpace(). On base, DCGain is +Inf. Now DCGain = FreqResponse([0]) = -4.5036e15, which equals the exact rational value N(1)/D(1) of the rounded coefficients (D(1) = -2.2e-16). integratingDCGain, used by pidtune, is still +Inf. Cause: in poleSpacing (frequency_pole.go), the poleClusterTol near-rule only applies when s == 0, not z == 1. The double-pole spread of about 1e-8 next to 0.9999 then fails the poleStepFraction*rho test, so near=false and the dd solve succeeds. Whether a z=1 cluster rule is wanted is an owner/MATLAB-parity call.

data.title: EDGE: DCGain wrong finite value / wrong Inf next to near-DC or exact DC poles
data.body:
Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12). DCGain disagrees with FreqResponse(0) and the exact rational oracle when the DC solve is near-singular: absolute coefficient floors drop tiny B, transfer-limit path returns neither Inf nor the exact value, MIMO near-DC poles, and an exactly singular dense block missed by dcGainByBlockLaurent. All pre-existing on base 2e4a07d.

[w12 #16 freq/review1] DCGain returns a finite value at a reachable, observable continuous integrator (MATLAB gives Inf). Repro: sys := &System{A: [[0,0],[1,-1.3258457598967608e-08]], B: [7.29653485561532e-14; 1.0337733234010072e-13], C: [0 1], D: [0]} (continuous). DCGain gives 7.797085843999098e-06/nil; FreqResponse(0) gives +Inf. G(s) = (1.03e-13 s + 7.30e-14)/(s(s+1.33e-8)), so G(0) = Inf. The value equals B2/1.3258e-8, i.e. B1 was dropped as zero. The likely cause is the absolute coefficient floor in dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit or dcGainByStructuralEntries for tiny B (response.go). The branch gives the same result as base 2e4a07d. The sweep found 13 more TF.StateSpace realizations with a trailing-zero den (exact pole at s=0) where DCGain returns 0 and FR(0) returns +Inf.

[w12 #17 freq/review1] DCGain returns a finite value with the wrong sign and magnitude when the transfer limit is reached with a computed pole near DC. Repro (continuous companion): A row0 = -[6.325495602920146 12.427798551146598 7.785922515524618 2.9590313755032033e-05 2.830045401741772e-11 5.223977207934464e-19], subdiagonal ones, B=e1, C=[-0.1661821972150368 0.6204228877798674 1.5965704467083484 -0.2679049847206111 -0.17326373644234616 -0.9184631132625503], D=0.18013697908513038. The A solve fails (cond 1.4e21) and poleSpacing near=true (pole -1.88e-8). DCGain returns +9.684e11. The exact big.Rat G(0) is -1.758e18, FreqResponse(0) is +Inf, and ddResponseInto gives the exact value. Correct answers would be Inf (pole at DC) or -1.76e18; 9.7e11 is neither. Files: response.go (dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit). Same result on base 2e4a07d.

[w12 #18 freq/review2] Pre-existing (identical on base and branch), DCGain wrong next to near-DC poles in MIMO state-space models: for 49 of 1400 sweep models DCGain is +/-Inf or off while FreqResponse(0) matches the exact oracle. Example dc9: a continuous upper-triangular A with diagonal entries -2.89e-5, -3.09e-11, -1.75e-5, ... gives DCGain [-Inf, -78626.6], while FreqResponse(0) and the exact big.Rat solve give [-1.1129e18, -3.0967e18]. Another: discrete 2x2 A=[0.9998853776327908 0.0001224178710512369; -6.299779160740249e-05 1.000067282291557], B=[-0.7525840543357618 -1.8936563902987011; -0.3336326973535324 -0.8822404525470022], C=[-1.3323341784633906 -0.2326700817740477; 0.48991627788123343 0.8587983672300241], dt=0.01. Its DCGain is finite but has relative error 5e-5 against the exact value (789372732529716 vs 789410222466333), and FreqResponse(0) is +Inf in every entry. Files: response.go (DCGain explicit solve / dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit), frequency_pole.go. Oracle: exact rational solve of C(s0 I-A)^-1 B+D.

[w12 #41 dcgain/review1] DCGain finite for an exactly singular dense block with no 1x1 exact pole (pre-existing, same on base 2e4a07d and branch). Repro: NewFromSlices(3,2,2, A=[0.38629023905802873 3.851534645926291 -3.23782488498432; 0 4 -3; 4 1.6251019182011088 -4.625101918201109], B=[-0.5 0; -1.75 0; 0 0], C=[-1 -2.176206339653932 1; 0 -0.06848213510526557 0], D=[5.737696031494993 0; 0.75 0], dt=0.1). DCGain[1,0] = 6.73e13; exact rational limit on the float model is +Inf (det(I-A) = 0 exactly, exact pole order 1, computed eigenvalue 2e-15 from 1). The value comes from dcGainByStructuralEntries. dcGainByBlockLaurent declines because it needs a 1x1 block with A_kk == x0, although the branch's exactDetIsZero could detect this block. Files: response.go dcGainByStructuralEntries / dcGainByBlockLaurent.

data.title: CORE: Bandwidth errors on infinite DC gain (MATLAB returns Inf); -Inf sign suspect
data.body:
Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12).

[w12 #15 freq/review0] Bandwidth on a loop with poles at the origin returns an error, 'DC gain is -Inf, bandwidth undefined', with a negative-infinite DC gain. Repro: makePlant(ergoOffOriginLoop.num, ergoOffOriginLoop.den); Bandwidth(p,-3) gives 0 and invalid argument on both base 2e4a07d and the branch. MATLAB's bandwidth returns Inf for infinite DC gain, and the -Inf sign is suspect for a double integrator. Low priority. Files: margin.go bandwidth / response.go DCGain.

data.title: EDGE: DCGain fuzz extremes: finite where exact is Inf, undocumented staircase SVD error
data.body:
Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12). FuzzDCGain pre-existing failures on ||A|| 1e5..1e128 models. #33/#34/#36 are the same kind=0xf7 seed (one fix: map/fallback the staircase SVD non-convergence error). #31 may not be fixable in float64; the Laurent path correctly defers there.

[w12 #31 dcgain/E2AY73] FuzzDCGain pre-existing failures, ill-conditioned: kind=0xe2 vals=[2.5 -2.75 -5 89.75 -35 2 -55.25 -25.5 100 19.5 -74.5 -10 -100 -8.75 -86.5 61.5] and kind=0xcc vals=[93.5 -57.75 -5 -19.5 -100 -72.75 -71.75 -48.75 23.75 85.75 84.6 -58.75 -65.5 12.75 -75.5 41.75]. An exact integrator sits beside a +/-1e-5i pole pair at ||A|| about 1e5 (cond about 1e10, plus cancellation). Base and the new code both return the same wrong finite value (e.g. -6.77e12 where -Inf is exact). The new Laurent path finds its finite value inaccurate and defers to the TF limit. Probably not fixable in float64 without exact arithmetic.

[w12 #33 dcgain/E2AY73] DCGain returns an undocumented error on an extreme model, both base and new: kind=0xf7 vals=[-80 -78 0.5 -0.33333333333333337 0 0 0 0.5 0 12 0 0 -10 57 -10 -10] (||A|| about 1e128, upper triangular, two exact z=1 poles) gives 'DCGain: SVD of staircase block 1 did not converge: Schur decomposition failed to converge' from the TF fallback (transfer.go / staircase.go). The Laurent path defers because cancellation of 1e128-sized terms leaves no correct digits.

[w12 #34 dcgain/JBKTCQ] DCGain returns an undocumented error 'SVD of staircase block 1 did not converge' (pre-existing, also fails on base fd13c59). Repro: FuzzDCGain seed bytes: byte('\xf7') then float64 values -80 -78 0.5 -0.33333333333333337 0 0 0 0.5 0 12 0 0 -10 57 -10 -10 (n=6 m=3 p=3, dt=1, A entries up to 6.5e128 with eigenvalues 1,1,1.03,3e127,0.995,1.4e-87, C around 1e-6). Put it in testdata/fuzz/FuzzDCGain/ and run go test -run=FuzzDCGain/<name>. Error: 'DCGain: SVD of staircase block 1 did not converge: controlsys: Schur decomposition failed to converge'. Files: staircase.go (svd.Factorize error path), response.go (dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit should fall back or map the error), possibly gonum Dgesvd on extreme-range input. The seed was not committed.

[w12 #36 dcgain/review] DCGain returns an error where a value is expected (pre-existing on base 2e4a07d and 8e45103; not a regression). FuzzDCGain kind=0xf7 vals=[-80 -78 0.5 -0.33333333333333337 0 0 0 0.5 0 12 0 0 -10 57 -10 -10]: discrete n=6 m=3 p=3, A entries about 1e128, eigenvalues include 1, 1 and 1e-87. DCGain fails with 'SVD of staircase block 1 did not converge: Schur decomposition failed to converge', which FuzzDCGain flags as an undocumented error. Files: response.go (dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit, then rationalTransferFunction / staircase SVD). Seed id was 2687dba4947a5ec6 (not committed).

[w12 #37 dcgain/review] DCGain returns a finite -3.46e70 where the exact limit is +Inf (pre-existing on base and 8e45103). FuzzDCGain kind=0xa7 vals=[-59.5 -8 81.22222222222223 -4 -4.875 -51 -1.125 -47.5 0 0 0 94 7.75 -93 -150 -0.2777777777777778]: discrete n=5 m=3 p=1, A entries about 1e43, eigenvalues 1, 1, a pair at about -2.6e43 and 1.0000133. The test fails at dcgain_fuzz_test.go:86 with DCGain[0,0] = -3.4594733814883594e+70 while the exact limit at the integrator is +Inf. File: response.go (transfer-function limit path). Seed id 55b1585182981755 (not committed).

data.title: CORE: TF/MinimalRealization staircase not scale-invariant; Dgebal on A alone drops modes
data.body:
Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12). Common root: staircase tolerances are absolute/normwise (tol*||A||, |[A;C_i]|) and balancedABC balances A alone, so tiny or inflated B/C cause dropped states and TF(k*sys) != k*TF(sys). Likely fix: joint balancing of [A B; C 0] as MATLAB does plus scale-relative rank tests. Previous patches regressed testdata/fuzz/FuzzDCGain/0adb1555e65760b9 on amd64/arm64 (see #30). Check MATLAB minreal on #35 before deciding.

[w12 #30 dcgain/E2AY73] TransferFunction drops controllable z=1 modes (transfer.go, balancedABC/convert). Repro: NewFromSlices(3,1,1, A=[1 0 -3.1622776601683795; 0 1 -3.1622776601683795; 0 0 eps], B=[-0.38211320287195655 0.7882242424655154 0.8038113259779769]', C=[-0.9291407314223547 0.6502534890410231 0.5087003937751763], D=0, dt=100). With eps in {1e-20, 1e-40, 1e-69}, TF den = [1 -eps] and MinimalOrder = 1. Exact: order 2, with a pole at z=1 of residue c1b1+c2b2+(c1+c2)a*b3/(1-eps) = 1.576. Evidence: Dgebal scales state 3 by about 1/eps, so B row 3 becomes about 1e20. controllabilityStaircase gives NCont=2 on the unbalanced model and 1 on the balanced one. With eps=1e-12 the balanced path keeps the order but the residue is off by 4e-4 relative. Two patches each regressed fuzz input testdata/fuzz/FuzzDCGain/0adb1555e65760b9 (||A|| about 1e43): falling back to the unbalanced staircase (broke amd64), and clamping the scaling by B/C (broke arm64). Likely needs joint balancing of [A B; C 0], as MATLAB does.

[w12 #35 dcgain/JBKTCQ] MinimalRealization drops a tiny-but-nonzero B as uncontrollable. Repro: r,_ := (&TransferFunc{Num:[][][]float64{{{-8.70643320022765e-16, 2.9186581655941266e-16, 1.3545850066477854e-16}}}, Den:[][]float64{{1, -5.609886783435264, 13.099973168748164, -16.29841103348229, 11.394314088807377, -4.243853507030152, 0.6578640663921657}}, Dt:0.01}).StateSpace(); r.Sys.MinimalRealization() gives order 0 (TransferFunction now gives order 6). Cause: same absolute staircase floor tol·‖A‖ (staircase.go:99) against ‖B‖ about 1e-15. Files: minimal.go, staircase.go; CtrbF/ObsvF (ctrbobsv.go) likely the same. I have not checked MATLAB minreal's behaviour on this model; it decides whether this is a bug.

[w12 #42 dcgain/review1] TransferFunction drops a well-defined first-order system when norm(A) is huge (pre-existing, base and branch). Repro: NewFromSlices(1,1,1, A=[-1e155], B=[1], C=[1], D=[0], 0).TransferFunction(nil) gives Num [[[0]]] / Den [[1]], instead of 1/(s+1e155) as MATLAB tf(ss) gives. DCGain is correct (1e-155). Same for A=-1e200, and for a 2x2 triangular A with entries ~1e150. Files: transfer.go rowRealizationConverter (staircase / numerator trimming relative to norm(A)).

[w12 #72 fuzz/AULHZC] TransferFunction minimality depends on output scaling, so TF(k*sys) != k*TF(sys) at O(1). The row observability tolerance (ssToTFRow / ObservabilityTol, transfer.go:287) is relative to |[A; C_i]|. Repro: A=[-3.162277660168379e-14, 9.486832980505137e-14; -9.486832980505139e-14, -3.162277660168378e-14], B=[-0.9667981925794609; -0.01238866346289056], C=[856888.7533689471, 210795.79943077973], D=0, continuous. Result: MinimalOrder 1, and at x=9.32e-14+3.62e-14i tf = -6.14e18+1.78e18i against an exact -3.62e18+1.15e17i. Scaling C by 1e-6 gives order 2 and the correct value. FuzzSSToTF accepts this because its bound uses nu = max(|A|,|B|,|C_i|), a normwise backward-error model.

[w12 #73 fuzz/AULHZC] TransferFunction balances A alone with Dgebal (balancedABC, transfer.go:249, from the BLYSOP fix), which can inflate B or C by about 1e13; the staircase then drops states that matter. Repro: discrete Ts=1, n=4, A=[0.7214294796518126 -0.3045829930861377 -0.00041016443744005306 -4.0917982190015664e-18; -0.3045829930861377 0.12979857966165384 -0.0009701301233358639 1.7299845394387501e-18; -0.00041016443744002493 -0.0009701301233358758 0.0010844921094764262 2.026087561733075e-44; -8.123803525336596e-45 -1.9214602234118876e-44 -2.0260875617330751e-44 -2.319905867103475e-44], B=[-0.9667981925794609; -0.01238866346289056; 0.9601702866503661; 0.5260775173811046], C=[-8.568887533689471e-07 -2.1079579943077972e-07 9.931849187581927e-07 -4.3137684497061916e-07], D=0. The Dgebal scale is [1 1 1 1.14e-13]. TF order is 2 while MinimalRealization gives 3. At x=1.1613383804294024+0.06822811668058017i, tf = 2.72084e-6 against ss EvalFr = 2.72149e-6, a 2.4e-4 relative error in the dynamic part. FuzzSSToTF skips this case only when its check would fail and the Dgebal scaling ratio (max/min) exceeds 1e6 (reason 'Dgebal scaling of A alone inflates B or C').

data.title: EDGE: ZPK.TransferFunction merges distinct poles within 100*eps window, wrong numerators
data.body:
Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12).

[w12 #70 fuzz/AULHZC] ZPK.TransferFunction gives wrong numerators when distinct poles fall in its merge window. commonDenomPoles and poleSetDifference (zpk.go:369,399) treat poles within 100*eps*(1+|p|) as equal, so a real pole can match a complex one. sortConjugatePairs (zpk.go:322) then re-adds the conjugate and the numerator degree is too high (polynomial_channel.go:90). Repro 1: NewZPKMIMO(zeros {{nil,nil}}, poles {{{1e-14+1e-14i, 1e-14-1e-14i},{1e-15}}}, gains {{1,1}}, dt 0) -> TransferFunction gives Den=[1 -2e-14 2e-28] and Num[0][1] equal to Den, so tf.Eval(10)[0][1] = 1 but zpk.Eval = 0.1. Repro 2 (unit scale): poles {1+-1e-15i} and {1} -> Den=[1 -2 1], Num1=[1 -2 1], tf(3)[1] = 1 vs zpk(3) = 0.5. MATLAB tf(zpk) converts each channel separately and gets this right. FuzzZPKToTF skips these rows with reason 'distinct row poles within the ZPK pole-merge tolerance'.

data.title: CORE: D2C(zoh) fast path inaccurate when Ad-I nearly singular; route to matrixLogISS
data.body:
Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12).

[w12 #71 fuzz/AULHZC] D2C(zoh) fast path (d2cZOHFast, convert_reverse_hold.go:254) is unstable when Ad-I is nearly singular. It computes Bc = (Ad-I)^-1*log(Ad)*Bd, so the error grows like eps/sigma_min(Ad-I); matLogSpectral also loses entries of a near-identity non-normal Ad. Repro: NewFromSlices(2,1,1, A=[0.9999999999999999,-2e-16; 1e-16,1], B=[1;1], C=[1 0], D=0, Ts=1).D2C(zoh) gives Bc=[-4e-18, 0.055] instead of about [1,1]. C2D(D2C(sys)) at z=2 then gives 4e-18 against an original 1. With 1e-12 off-diagonals the relative error is 1.7e-5. FOH on the same model is accurate. The augmented-log path (matrixLogISS) should be used whenever Ad-I is ill-conditioned. FuzzC2DD2C treats sigma_min(Ad-I)/max(1,|Ad|) < 1e-6 as this known bug and carries 1/gap in its D2C(zoh) bounds.
