data.title: CORE: Pidtune gate NaN margin / spurious crossover rejects or accepts designs
data.body:
Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12). pidtuneGate.check/crossing and pidTuningCrossingsOn produce NaN margins on the displaced-integrator plant (#46/#48 same plant), and auto PID returns a design with no oracle-visible crossover (#49, not from retry).

[w12 #46 pidtune/IBWZGV] Bug: on near-integrator discrete plants the back-off gate reports 'phase margin NaN deg at a gain crossover' and rejects designs the oracle finds robust. Repro: Pidtune on 1.8748015424080903e-16 / [1 -6.656527066165689 18.974082402962605 -30.020939359334676 28.473509438245436 -16.187809823253666 5.1075991528389695 -0.6899147452929796], dt 0.1, families P and PD, wc 0. The gated first design fails with the NaN margin. The oracle (pidtuneSignedMargins on pidtuneOracleLoop over [1e-9, pi/dt]) gives P Kp 141.9 with every margin >= 85 deg and |S| 1.004, and PD with every margin >= 91.9 deg and |S| 1.018. These designs only come back through the retry, so a stricter retry gate would lose them. Likely a NaN plant sample in pidTuningCrossingsOn or crossExcess (newPidtuneGate's at returns NaN on a failed eval). Files: pidtune.go pidtuneGate.check/crossing, pid_tuning.go pidTuningCrossingsOn.

[w12 #48 pidtune/X7DDPS] Gate gives a NaN margin on a displaced-integrator plant: with the retry fully gated, Pidtune on pidtuneBackoffPlant(Poly{1.8748015424080903e-16}, Poly{1,-6.656527066165689,18.974082402962605,-30.020939359334676,28.473509438245436,-16.187809823253666,5.1075991528389695,-0.6899147452929796}, 0.1, 0) for P/PI/PD/PID/PIDF failed with 'design at wc=0.000171848 has phase margin NaN° at a gain crossover'. pidtuneGate.check / pidTuningCrossingsOn produce a NaN margin there, and a NaN should not be the reason for rejecting a design. Files: pidtune.go pidtuneGate.crossing/check. Test: TestPidtuneDisplacedIntegratorDCSign (pidtune_wave9_test.go).

[w12 #49 pidtune/X7DDPS] Auto PID returns Kd=0 with no gain crossover the oracle can find: Pidtune(pidtuneBackoffPlant(Poly{1.7837475641504483,0.7946993866758785,1.4552772148607651,6.888693123877885e-07}, Poly{1,0.1506135003142426,1.3911883292147762,0.612642264165268},0,0), PID, 0, nil) gives Kp -1.2564, Ki -0.5501, Kd 0. The oracle finds no crossover on [1e-6,1e6], |S| 3.31, closed loop stable. The plant is unstable. This is not from the retry: it persists with the retry disabled. Check whether the gate's crossover is below 1e-6 or is spurious. Files: pidtune.go gate/backedOff.

data.title: EDGE: Pidtune integrating crossover 3-5x off when z=1 integrator scatters into a cluster
data.body:
Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12).

[w12 #60 pidtune/review1] Crossover is still 3-5x off on discrete integrators that rounding scatters into a cluster of conjugate or comparable-distance poles (the integrator is not isolated), outside FI3ZIB's scope. Example from a seeded (z-1)·∏(z-e^(-a·dt)) sweep: nearest pole 2.07e-3 from z=1 with a second pole at the same distance (a conjugate pair); plantCrossoverFreq gives 0.1035 vs 0.0304 for half the slowest pole. Other examples: 0.50 vs 0.163 at ratio 1.22, and 0.245 vs 0.059 at ratio 1.66. These cases have no gain crossover and the same value on base. File: pidtune.go pidtuneIntegratingCrossover / pidtuneSlowestRoot. Designs stay stable.

data.title: CORE: HinfNorm accuracy misses documented 1e-10 (under-report up to 3.6e-4, race-build 3e-10)
data.body:
Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12). Race-build case (test now skips it under race): HinfNorm slow-resonance model decoded under -race build is 3e-10 low vs 1e-10 contract: fzSeed{N:3,M:1,P:1,Mag:{-8,4},Damp:{2.5,1},Shear:-10,Rot:0.37,no delays} in TestHinfNorm_BadlyScaledIOMatchesExactOracle (norms_test.go). Re-enable under race once fixed. Common suspects: norms.go certifyPeak treating sub-probe candidates as no crossing, hasImagEigs nearAxisTol on stiff unbalanced pencils (Dggbal before Dggev), peak search missing narrow humps, sigmaEvaluator over-report.

[w12 #68 linalg/LASTBLOCK] The new test TestHinfNorm_BadlyScaledIOMatchesExactOracle (norms_test.go, 5YUZIK) fails under -race, which CI runs. It is deterministic and does not skip when raceEnabled.
`go test -race -count=2 -run TestHinfNorm_BadlyScaledIOMatchesExactOracle .` on fed3cf1 (arm64) fails both times: "norms_test.go:2044: slow resonance: HinfNorm = 239.388723153999, oracle 239.388723226662 (rel -3.04e-10)". assertHinfNormMatchesOracle allows 1e-10 relative (norms_test.go:1854). Without -race it passes on arm64 and on amd64. In the race build fzDecode produces slightly different A data, and on that model the norm is 3e-10 low, against a documented accuracy of 1e-10. Base is 30% low on the same model, so this is a CI test failure, not a value regression. Fix: either reach 1e-10 on that data, or skip/loosen only under raceEnabled.

[w12 #74 fuzz/XQYP43] HinfNorm/Norm(Inf) under-reports a lightly damped discrete peak near z=1 by about 3.6e-4 relative, although norms.go peakGain documents certification to 1e-10. The result is still within MATLAB's default 1e-2 tolerance, so parity holds; the library's own claim is what's breached. Repro: NewFromSlices(2,1,1, A=[0.9999999959758767 5.3457259458380696e-09 -1.3269470226717082e-08 0.9999999927772968], B=[-0.6656134553337595 0.5410494509487578], C=[-999097.8260547261 363185.4084160624], D=[-736.7935074839925], dt=1e-4). HinfNorm gives 9.467722253631506e13 at ω=8.685e-5; the exact rational response gives 9.471110502171495e13 at ω=8.8388e-5. A naive float LU sweep agrees with the exact value to 1e-15, and the backward-error sensitivity is about 1e-7, so this is a search or certification miss, not conditioning. The exact γ-crossing test confirms a crossing at norm·(1+1e-6). Fuzz tuple: FuzzHinfNorm kind=0x41 vals=[-4 2.25 0.5 -145 -26 18 34 5629.5 -8 -0.3 1.1 32 1044 -0.5 0.2 -10]. The MIMO variant kind=0x5b with the same vals is also low by 3.6e-4. Suspect: norms.go peakGain/certifyPeak/upperBound. The rule 'candidates whose evaluated gains stay below the probe count as no crossing' probably certifies falsely when the candidate ω is off the true peak (2.5% off here).

[w12 #78 fuzz/review0] HinfNorm/linfNorm under-reports the peak gain of a stable, stiff, symmetric continuous SISO model by 2.1e-4 relative. This is present at base 2e4a07d (the base FuzzHinfNorm fails on the same input). Repro: put a corpus file `go test fuzz v1` / byte('À') / float64 vals 39,0,0.3,0,-0.2,0,0,0,0,-9.5,2.5,-76,-10,-10,-10,-10 into testdata/fuzz/FuzzHinfNorm/x, then run `go test -run FuzzHinfNorm/x .`. The decoded model has n=6, m=p=1, D=0, condT=1 (symmetric A, ‖A‖≈2e6) and stable eigenvalues {-0.00316, -0.00998, -50, -126, -399, -2e6}. HinfNorm returns 4.865840926965868e-05 at ω=0.003992. The exact big.Rat σmax at ω=0.0038510 is 4.86684164441442e-05. The expected error bound is fzNormTol ≈ 1e-6, so the peak search misses a low-frequency hump between the two slow poles. Files: hinfnorm.go (HinfNorm/linfNorm peak search). Evidence: hinfnorm_fuzz_test.go:78 fails on base and :50 on the branch; norms_fuzz_test.go:113 also fails.

[w12 #80 fuzz/review1] Pre-existing, outside the task scope: certifyPeak accepts candidates whose evaluated σ is below the probe as 'no crossing'. On undecidable lightly damped models (ζ≤1e-7) this certifies values up to 2e-6 below the exact σmax of the float64 model. Repro: sweep #1261 (kind=254, n=6, m=p=3, poles -4.65e-10±9.1206258e-4i). Branch HinfNorm 10322113722.95 at ω=9.1206258284e-4, while fzExactResponse at ω=9.1206258415e-4 gives 10322135171.8. Files: norms.go certifyPeak/candidatePeak. Conditioning is ~551, so this may be acceptable; filing is optional.

[w12 #77 fuzz/review] The norms.go change touches the library under-report the reviewer already filed (FuzzLinfNorm/FuzzHinfNorm, kind=0xc0 crasher). Climbing the sampled peak fixes the case where the true peak lies next to a grid sample. It does not fix the root cause: on stiff models (pole spread around 1e9), unstructured QZ in hamiltonianWS.hasImagEigs can still push genuine γ-crossings outside nearAxisTol=0.1. In norms.go hasImagEigs, the pencil eigenvalues at γ=4.8668e-5 for this model came out as (-5.0e-4+3.88e-3i)/0.9998, a ratio of 0.13. So a narrow peak between grid samples on a stiff model could still be under-reported. Possible fixes: balance the pencil (Dggbal 'B') before Dggev, or scale nearAxisTol to the eigenvalue condition. No concrete repro beyond the fixed crasher yet; the 5-minute fuzz runs found none.

[w12 #66 linalg/review0] HinfNorm reports a norm 3e-8 to 9e-8 above the exact σ_max at its own returned ω, and above a dense exact sweep, on high-gain models. The doc promises 1e-10. This happens on both base 2e4a07d and the branch, on arm64 and amd64. Repro: s := fzDecode(t, 0xa1, [16]float64{-4.840958682425959, 5.75742924209089, -4.840958682425959, 5.75742924209089, -4.974373469618411, 0.8119640876303578, -5, 1e-06, -0.6935062785976278, -9.308799076568224, 0.871442593513744, 9.362982810868214, -10, -10, -10, -10}); HinfNorm(s.System(t, fzSysOpts{})) = 154118350.60 at ω=1.44225e-5. fzExactResponse σ_max there is 154118336.72 (rel +9.0e-8), and the fzSweepMax exact peak is 154118336.724. Second instance: kind 0xc9 vals {0.6413769500533629, 3.225485305446771, -6.920211238942823, 5.194656803421655, 2.5649118927522707, 5.9960354875740425, 0.7321123327177131, 0, 0.8225408446783429, -8.084719954920434, -0.12421061853394999, -14.98391252021944, -10, -10, -10, -10} gives 10252.94430 vs exact 10252.94379 (+5e-8). Files: norms.go sigmaEvaluator / certifyPeak.

data.title: EDGE: H2Norm ErrSingularEquation on stable model with poles 4e-10 from the imaginary axis
data.body:
Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12).

[w12 #76 fuzz/XQYP43] Low severity, boundary input: on one model the routines disagree with each other. IsStable() says stable (poles −3.9e-10±0.6309573j, −9.3e-10, −3.8e-8, −50, −2e6), HinfNorm returns a finite 7.14e5, but H2Norm and Norm(2) return ErrSingularEquation ('Lyap: A and -A share an eigenvalue'). MATLAB norm(sys,2) would return a large finite value. Tuple: fzDecode kind=0xc0 vals=[72 0 -9.7 0 -0.2 -400 0 0 0 0.01 2.5 0 -10 -10 -70 -10] (n=6, SISO, continuous). Files: norms.go H2Norm, lyapunov.go:146, energy_policy.go requireStable. The fuzz target treats this input as undecidable and skips it.

data.title: CORE: SPWBDX redo: Zeros accuracy (per-zero eig/staircase hybrid + tzero-style prescale)
data.body:
Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12). SPWBDX redo. Attempt (commits 3373ec0/80cdb0e, pencilIOScale fed3cf1) NOT merged. Learnings: (1) Routing square models whose dInvZeros gate fails to staircase+QZ gives wrong moderate zeros (up to 3e-4 rel) and drops huge finite zeros where base eig(A-BD^-1C) was right to 1e-13 (G1810, G1979, G1383); the 80cdb0e build without fed3cf1 scaling gives the same outputs, so routing causes it. (2) fed3cf1 pencilIOScale still regresses 6 vs base. (3) The all-or-nothing per-model gate is the wrong granularity: for small-D models eig(M) is accurate for large zeros and the staircase for small ones; needs a per-zero hybrid or a better gate. (4) Unscaled staircase loses ~1e-9 even on well-conditioned models; non-square and descriptor models never use eig, so MATLAB-style tzero prescale (diagonal state scaling + power-of-two B/C balance) in mimoZeros before zerosStaircase is needed regardless. (5) Over the sweep the branch improved 152 exact roots and regressed 14; base FuzzZeros fails 38/1788 inputs, branch 0. Oracle: fzPencilDetRat (big.Rat) + 400-bit Durand-Kerner.

[w12 #69 linalg/LASTBLOCK] Zeros (SPWBDX, commits 3373ec0/80cdb0e): square models whose dInvZeros gate fails now go to staircase+QZ. That path returns wrong values for some moderate-size zeros that base's eig(A-BD^-1C) computed to 1e-13, and it drops a finite zero. Per the rubric ('wrong value vs oracle') I count it as blocking, but the coordinator may reasonably downgrade it (mitigations below).
Oracle: exact roots of det P(s), from fzPencilDetRat (big.Rat) followed by 400-bit Durand-Kerner. Case G1810 is SISO, n=6, D=1e-9, ‖A‖_F=6.5e5, kind=0xc0 vals=[-8.369173697008657,-3.952195487192786,4,1,4,-2,-5.426620385568855,1e-09,-4,0.03908835077813827,0,-59.556335212925134,-10,-10,-10,-10]. Exact zeros: 5.0887e-10, -517.0344036, 9295.945282, 10000, -305614.05504, 3.5475035e8. Base returns all 6 and gets -305614.0550391 (2.9e-13) and 3.547503549e8 (5e-16) right, but the smallest zero is off (2.3e-8). Branch returns 5 zeros: -305705.709 (3.0e-4 rel), 9295.9575 (1.3e-6) and -517.03442 (3e-8), and drops the 3.5475e8 zero (545·‖A‖). Second instance G1979: kind=0xf4 vals=[0,-2,-4,2,3,-6,0,-3.3409962664434967,1.3864778279157017,-1,0.15091351157347344,-37,-10,...], m=p=3 with D nearly rank 2. The pair -209.97726537±357.2716147i is at 0.28·‖A‖. Base error is 4.6e-9; branch gives -209.9759±357.2721i (3.5e-6) and drops the -3.68e8 zero. Mild third instance G1383 (kind=0x74): moderate zeros at 5e-7 error vs base 1.4e-8, and the 1.6e11 zero is dropped. A build of 80cdb0e (without the fed3cf1 scaling) gives the same outputs, so the routing causes this, not pencilIOScale. Mitigations: over the whole sweep 152 exact roots improved vs 14 regressed, base FuzzZeros fails 38 of the 1788 sweep inputs and branch 0, and in each regressed model base was also wrong on another zero. The gate is all-or-nothing per model, while for small-D models eig(M) is accurate for the large zeros and the staircase for the small ones. The fix probably needs a per-zero combination or a better gate. Not implemented.

[w12 #67 linalg/review1] Zeros staircase lacks I/O prescaling (pre-existing, zeros.go mimoZeros/zerosStaircase). On models with ||B|| and ||C|| far apart, the unbalanced staircase+QZ loses accuracy: small zeros at C≈1e5-1e6 with D≈1e-6, large zeros at D≈1e-9 with B≈4e4 and C≈5e-6. It also drops a finite zero when cond(D)≈3e9. Repro: the case-23 SISO model above with the eig shortcut bypassed gives 2.2278e8 vs exact 2.15996e8. Evidence: scaling B by α and C by 1/α (power-of-two balance, as pencilIOScale does) gives all zeros to <= 1.3e-7 on case 23 and on cond(D)=2.9e9 case 645. MATLAB tzero prescales by default. This finding is filed as blocking for SPWBDX, but the fix (balance in mimoZeros before zerosStaircase) also covers non-square and descriptor models, which never use the eig path.

[w12 #65 linalg/review] Huge-zero accuracy (|z| much larger than ||A||, e.g. 1e12 with ||A|| about 1): with the B/C scaling, the staircase+QZ result can be 1e-6..5e-3 relative off. eig(A-BD^-1C) is accurate here but is gated out. A per-zero hybrid or a full MATLAB-style prescale (diagonal state scaling plus input/output scaling) might close this. Repro: sweep with B, C scales 10^U(-5,5) and D 10^-U(0,10), e.g. A=[0.6863883501311974 0.8550271126517397; 1.6708868232151954 0.11946342859322057], B=[-0.026829097335336855; -0.1334147041955197], C=[-70618.48253548339 155535.57430302448], D=-4.10051011325682e-09. The huge zero should be -4.598477256509821e12; the fixed code gives -4.59841e12 (1.4e-5 rel), while the branch gave 6.9e-9. File: zeros.go (mimoZeros/zerosStaircase).

[w12 #63 linalg/review] Scope note, not a confirmed bug: the unscaled staircase in zerosStaircase loses about 1e-9 relative accuracy even on simple well-conditioned square models. In the scratch sweep (fzDecode, square n=1) ids 230, 274 and 323 gave about 1e-9 from the staircase against about 1e-17 from eig. Those square cases now use eig, but non-square models, square models the gate rejects, and descriptor models still use the staircase, and their accuracy is unmeasured. A sweep like the one in this task, against exact pencil-rank roots for non-square models, would show whether the staircase needs balancing or rank-tolerance work (zeros.go zerosStaircase, zerosStaircasePass).

Found in wave 12. The PS6S32/IBWZGV/X7DDPS track reported that the retry path, and the unshaped rule, gated only on |S| and the existence of a crossing, return designs below the owner bar of classical PM >= 58.5 deg and |S| <= 4.
- Canonical case: Pidtune(1/(s-1), P or PI, 0) returns PM 45/42 deg. Its only crossover is at wc_auto ~0.9.
- About 301 of 11997 auto returns in the sampled population come from the retry, with worst classical margins of 10-58 deg.
- Zero-DC continuous P designs fall below the bar through the |S|-only unshaped rule. Example: pidtuneBackoffPlant(Poly{1.4392005301712567,0,0}, Poly{1,8.24762471156669,20.7899930...}).

## Decision (advisor, 2026-10-19; owner said open questions go to the advisor)
- Every returned auto design, retry and unshaped included, must meet the same bar (oracle-stable, classical PM >= 58.5 deg at every crossover, |S| <= 4).
- Before returning ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable when back-off fails, add a bounded UPWARD wc search through the same gate. Go up to about 1e3 x wc_auto, capped at Nyquist for discrete plants.
- Rationale: on unstable plants, PM grows with wc. For 1/(s-1), P with Kp=2 gives |L|=1 at sqrt(3), PM exactly 60 deg, |S|=1 everywhere, closed-loop pole -1. Back-off lowers wc, which moves the wrong way. Returning "unattainable" when Kp=2 exists would be a parity failure.
- Verify that 1/(s-1) P finds Kp ~2 with PM ~60. Report how much of the ~300 retry population gets a design that meets the bar via the upward search, and how much becomes an honest unattainable.
- If the upward search also fails, unattainable is correct.
- Fold the wave 12 reports "unstable plants still get fragile auto designs" and "zero-DC P below the bar via the unshaped rule" into this task.
Core priority for wave 13. Files: pidtune.go (pidtuneRun.attempt retry, unshaped, back-off loop).


Wave 12 reports folded in:

[w12 #45] Owner decision: the retry still returns designs below the 58.5 deg bar. After the fix, 301 of 11997 auto returns in the population come from the retry with |S| <= 4 but a worst classical margin of 10 to 58 deg. Canonical case: Pidtune(1/(s-1), PI, 0) returns Kp 1.411, Ki 0.0704 with PM 42.1 deg (P gives Kp 1.413, PM 44.9 deg). Gating the retry on the full bar would turn these into errors, but would also break TestPidtune_PI_Unstable and the 'unst' mustTune lists in TestPidtuneUnstableMirrorsPositive. It would also lose oracle-robust designs (next item). For 1/(s-1) a P with Kp 2 at wc 1.73 meets the bar, so an upward wc search for unstable plants may be the better fix. Files: pidtune.go attempt/backedOff.

[w12 #47] Unstable plants still get fragile auto designs: the retry, gated only on |S| and a crossing, is kept for plants that are not stable and returns designs under the owner bar. Repro: Pidtune(1/(s-1), P or PI, 0) gives PM 45° / 42° (the only crossover is at wc=0.9976; P at wc=sqrt(3) would give 60°). Auto PID on pidtuneBackoffPlant(Poly{0.08119770312059038,1.4299696862733304,1.1509782187662239,0.74301299939046}, Poly{1,1.5247143694217347,0.26500427775406976,1.1490289607929067}) gives Kp 0.04998, Kd 1.843, Tf 0, signed PM -28.3°. PID on {0.012117279206722564,0.6998831440522459,1.7138236892014762,1.8876491780936953}/{1,0.30102668894257456,1.2322300903394714,1.7765490062040799} gives -46.8°. PD on {0.4820870937175388,1.3079853107003931,1.9844096182517548,-1.0452039084558389}/{1,0.8298649253038679,1.349639061840446,1.53625974244542} gives -51.5°. All three plants are unstable (a1*a2 < a3). Back-off only lowers wc, which is the wrong direction for unstable plants; a fix needs an upward crossover search. Files: pidtune.go attempt/backedOff. Evidence: pidtuneCheckRobust on these plants.

[w12 #51] Pidtune P on zero-DC continuous plants returns designs below the 58.5 deg bar through the same |S|-only unshaped rule (pidtune.go pidtuneRun.unshaped/check). Repro: Pidtune(pidtuneBackoffPlant(t, Poly{1.4392005301712567,0,0}, Poly{1,8.24762471156669,20.7899930610465,15.321468764445184},0,0), PidtuneP, 0, nil) gives Kp 28.89, signed margins [-48.5, 101.4] deg, |S| 1.57, oracle-stable. Also P on 0.8542595646531987 s^2/(s^3+7.023342124760237 s^2+12.926235567617814 s+2.066641791908522): Kp 348.1, margin 29.5 deg, |S| 2.19. A seeded sweep (PCG(5,7), 400 plants k*s^m/prod(s+a_i)) found 83 P designs below 58.5 and 0 PD designs after this fix. The P exemption is the older EU24XW MATLAB-parity decision, so gating P on margin is the owner's call.

[w12 #53] Ungated retry on unstable plants returns designs below the owner's 58.5 degree bar (pidtune.go, pidtuneRun.attempt). Repro: Pidtune(PI, wc=0) on num=[6.749592744149843e-16 -6.056872503393394e-16], den=[1 -7.9623743329365935 28.09350817041953 -57.63766640485889 75.76142091126783 -66.14845014857204 38.35309958277561 -14.235001137708403 3.067835464760931 -0.29237210514798584], dt=0.01 (one pole at 1.000115). It returns Kp 176.3, Ki 0.514: closed loop stable by extended Schur–Cohn, |S| at most 4, but PM 30.5 degrees at its crossover. Base returned a design with |S| 64.2 on the same plant. The retry for gain-source crossovers on open-loop-unstable plants is gated only on |S| and on crossing 0 dB, by design (IBWZGV). The owner should decide whether such plants must return ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable instead.

[w12 #55] MATLAB parity: auto P and PI on unstable plants now return errors where MATLAB designs. Repro: Pidtune(1/(s-1), PidtuneP or PidtunePI, 0, nil) gives ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable at wc=0.9976. With PM = atan(w) + angle(C), at most 45 deg at w=1, while P reaches 60 deg at w=sqrt(3) with Kp=2. The auto crossover for unstable plants only backs off downward; an upward wc search would give designs that meet the 58.5 deg bar. Files: pidtune.go (backedOff, backoffFloor, attempt).

[w12 #61] Pidtune auto P on zero-DC k·s^m plants still passes on |S| alone through the unshaped-P rule, which PS6S32 kept unchanged. That is outside PS6S32, which covers the legacy PD only, and is the same on base. These designs miss the owner bar (PM >= 58.5 at every crossover). Repro: Pidtune(pidtuneBackoffPlant(t, Poly{-0.4747823914433865,0,0}, Poly{1,1.7019690144285535,0.19889294875649396},0,0), PidtuneP, 0, nil) gives Kp -117.685, one crossover at PM 28.9 deg, |S| 2.23. More: num {-3.815515468598575,0,0}, den {1,7.773322676859117,15.64159738856245,2.4039470279016206}: Kp -100.719, PM 29.1. num {0.17174745558754434,0,0}, den {1,4.304762793303786,3.0119125343741975}: Kp 102.277, PM 33.9. In all, 22 of 70 random zero-DC plants gave a P below 58.5 deg. File: pidtune.go, pidtuneRun.check (case r.pidType == PidtuneP: sensitive only) and unshaped. Oracle: roots of the characteristic polynomial, plus signed margins and |S| of the directly evaluated loop.

[w12 #57] Cleanup candidate: the non-stable retry in pidtuneRun.attempt (pidtune.go) is now likely redundant with the first gated design in backedOff (same gains, same gate). Confirm that the gated and ungated design paths (PIDF fallbacks, mirror) cannot diverge, then remove it.

Found in wave 11 (branch fix/wave11).

SLOWDOWN, large but tail-only: on the crowded-integrator sweep (den = s^m * tiny real roots 1e-10..1e-5, sometimes a tiny complex pair, plus one 1e-3..1 pole; 2000 cases, seed PCG(77,fam)), wall clock went from 42s on base to 1728s on the branch (41x). Per-case IsStable timing over 300 cases: 7 cases (2.3%) slow down by more than 2x, and the total goes from 1.09s to 99.4s. Worst cases: c1/0061 (num=[0.009773188260746423 0.04489604727967583 0.020323824184367914 0.025820219062960566 0.025797214642228176 0.006646947890672527 0.0211410669887515], den=[1 0.003649069685529213 2.4765632608475385e-08 1.738276564214012e-13 1.3318081161564088e-18 -1.5346094421104906e-24 0 0], tau=0.106793461122868, verdict U, matching the oracle) goes from 0.7ms to 26.9s. c1/0038 goes from 32ms to 34s and errors on both base and branch. c0/0474 (num=[6.147829022841792 10.216695150719099 7.832026243562451 3.0229141413956437 0.6108677798926465 0.060153027952126306 0.002148638203899052], den=[1 -0.46362065820370524 -8.844990464639967e-06 -5.1310852993591357e-11 -8.387818654264996e-17 0 0 0], tau=0.0034389605674428696): IsStable goes from 0.30s to 23.3s and DiskMargin from 0.68s to 22.9s.

Slowdown attribution: with 9e0e49a's margin_ddeval.go placed on base's delay_nyquist.go, c0/0474 still takes 21.6s. So the cause is the DOIFRS pivot test alone, not the formCluster order change or axisAt. The cost per solve is small (BenchmarkDDSISOSolve response 2661 to 2999 ns, noise 2594 to 2811 ns, about 1.1x). The cost is in how many solves run: the dd solve now succeeds where base failed early, so refine walks through the crowded band. The profile shows about 28% of the time in poleSpacing, which calls descriptorPolicy.poles and then Dgeev again on every evalWithPoleLimit call, and about 25% in ddSISOSolve. These two are the places to cut cost. The shipped tests are only mildly affected (TestDelayNyquistClusterSweep 85s to 96s).

Descriptor certifier reach collapses in the band between a crowded origin cluster and the next real pole. Repro: at 9e0e49a, set formCluster back to ascending k for dd, then run TestDelayNyquistTinyRealPolesDDCircles case 1 (den 1, 0.006386411776610228, 3.0129825054035514e-08, 1.2921688426134479e-17, 0, 0, 0; tau 0.025221635624798323). The dd pass verifies a k=4 cluster at g≈1.09e-7; the walk then returns refineBudget (2,097,152 points) at ω≈4.7107e-6 after about 15 s. Certified spans in [1e-7, 4.7e-6] average about 2e-12 wide. Files: delay_nyquist.go (refine, certifiedSpan), delay_nyquist_cert.go (descriptorCertifier kind 0/1 models). Descending k in the dd pass avoids it, but any walk that starts inside that band will hit the same budget wall.


Wave 12 reports folded in:

[w12 #22] No new defect. The certifier-reach collapse already filed in wave 11 (w11-fu.txt item: descriptor certifier reach collapses in the band between a crowded origin cluster and the next real pole; delay_nyquist.go refine/certifiedSpan, delay_nyquist_cert.go) is still present. Trying the outer dd radii first avoids it, but any walk that has to start inside that band still exhausts the 2M-point budget. New repro: c1/0277 (num=[11.804907045235103 47.69278444420078 78.93833711881778 56.554249325501495 20.364449939570378 4.073141801943374 0.4707595594277479 0.0310525592479381 0.0010784630364785225 1.5231794863841214e-05], den=[1 -0.030506554427827935 5.2038982663217025e-08 -8.555476402942147e-14 1.4908513010377137e-19 -4.276994673844071e-28 1.8994237953309433e-37 -2.30930559019089e-47 0 0 0], tau=0.012199028614811678). With formCluster's dd order set back to {0.5,0.25,0.75}, IsStable fails after about 50s; the S-model reach near ω≈3e-4 is about 1e-12.

[w12 #25] Pre-existing extreme slowness on crowded-integrator delay loops (both revisions): DiskMargin takes over 145s or does not finish in 150s. Repro c1/1225 (rand.NewPCG(20261019,1225) with the review generator) times out on both revisions. Explicit repro c1/1117: num=[-0.012235734044675426 -0.006311583925569351 0.02414059228419912 -0.008061845117263832 0.00512661893265594 0.010735185448027559 -0.0008198734917113229], den=[1 0.011355350040403025 -7.55495339499703e-08 8.009233485927711e-12 -4.209496182030594e-17 -1.9086774397679433e-23 9.940606728217147e-29 0], tau=0.0006115707778961484 (oracle 3 RHP roots): DiskMargin took 149.5s on base 2e4a07d, and IsStable also hit the 150s limit. Files: delay_nyquist.go (refine/clusterWinding), margin.go (DiskMargin).

[w12 #29] Pre-existing slow fail-closed case: num=[0.37252309338771605 0.4625825403441033 0.9274824381636989 0.8389534845815284 0.004072616333200653 -0.14458113372741474 4.1608923438942696e-06], den=[1 0.0077345812020016055 3.193020496185404e-08 8.971080898815777e-14 3.7045363670280857e-19 -6.605723732890916e-28 0 0], tau=0.001695591587321757 (double integrator, real poles 1.8e-9, -4.1e-6, -0.0077, pair at 3.4e-6i with Re +1.3e-11). Oracle gives 4 RHP roots. IsStable, DiskMargin and HinfNorm all error on both base and branch, taking about 255s for the three calls. It fails closed, but the error is slow.

Found in wave 12. H2Norm, HinfNorm and Norm(2/Inf) return ErrDescriptorUnsupported for a descriptor model with E≠I, even for a nonsingular diagonal E (descriptor.go requireStandard, called in norms.go). MATLAB's norm, hinfnorm and getPeakGain accept dss models.

## Decision (advisor, 2026-10-19)
This is a parity gap, not a wrong value: the documented error is allowed under the Go error pattern. Treat it as feature work, scheduled after the correctness backlog.
- Step 1: support nonsingular E by converting to standard form and reusing the existing norm paths. Add a kappa(E) guard so an ill-conditioned E returns an error, not garbage.
- Step 2 (follow-up): singular E. First check what MATLAB hinfnorm and norm return for improper dss models, then implement to match.


Wave 12 reports folded in:

[w12 #75] Parity gap, not a defect: H2Norm, HinfNorm and Norm(2/Inf) return ErrDescriptorUnsupported for a descriptor model with E≠I, even nonsingular diagonal E (descriptor.go requireStandard, called in norms.go). MATLAB norm/hinfnorm/getPeakGain accept dss models. The fuzz targets assert the current contract (fzDescriptorNorm in norms_fuzz_test.go).

Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12). Owner decision needed between Option A (finite everywhere, MATLAB parity, retarget TestPidtuneDisplacedIntegratorDCSign) and Option B (Inf everywhere); also whether a z=1 cluster rule is wanted in poleSpacing. Includes the comment fix in pidtune_wave9_test.go.

[w12 #2 margins/IP3XIC] DCGain returns +Inf for a discrete plant with no pole at z=1 (response.go:403, discrete path). Repro: same TF as above with k=1, then StateSpace(), then sys.DCGain() gives +Inf, and Bandwidth(sys,-3) fails with 'DC gain is +Inf, bandwidth undefined'. The exact realization value from fzExactResponse at z=1 is 0.20837663904890938, and the TF coefficients agree: N(1)/D(1) = 6.0150e-16/2.8866e-15. The nearest pole is 0.9999998669 (1-1.3e-7), not an integrator; FreqResponse at w=6.3e-7 gives |G| of about 0.203. Cause: the (I-A) X.Solve fails on condition, and the code falls back to dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit, which returns +Inf. MATLAB parity requires a finite value, e.g. a double-double or pole-aware fallback before declaring an integrator.

[w12 #10 freq/4M7RB3] Decision needed (coordinator/owner), DCGain vs FreqResponse at a near-integrator DC point. Repro: TF Num {2.761969998249568e-16, 2.6332895798497864e-16, 6.196985260193668e-17}, Den {1,-5.388323209156541,12.045405202918547,-14.292531743733242,9.488502158799133,-3.339413745774066,0.486361336946173}, Dt 0.01; and Num {1.8748015424080903e-16}, Den {1,-6.656527066165689,18.974082402962605,-30.020939359334676,28.473509438245436,-16.187809823253666,5.1075991528389695,-0.6899147452929796}, Dt 0.1. DCGain gives +Inf; FreqResponse(0) gives 0.2084 and 0.3377, which are exact for the stored coefficients (true poles 2.71e-8 and 3.59e-7 inside z=1). Option A, finite everywhere: change response.go DCGain so a near-singular Solve with a successful double-double evaluation returns the exact finite gain; this breaks the premise of TestPidtuneDisplacedIntegratorDCSign (pidtune_wave9_test.go, 2e4a07d), which relies on DCGain=+Inf, so that test would need re-targeting. Option B, Inf everywhere: FreqResponse would need a DC conditioning test (cond(I-A) > 1/eps means a pole) in frequency_pole.go. That is not MATLAB parity and swaps exact values for Inf. Files: response.go (DCGain, dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit), frequency_pole.go (evalWithPoleLimitGated, poleSpacing near).

[w12 #11 freq/4M7RB3] Minor: the pidtune_wave9_test.go comment in TestPidtuneDisplacedIntegratorDCSign says case 1's pole 'lies 3.4e-5 outside z = 1'. That is the computed eigenvalue; the exact root of the stored denominator is 3.586e-7 inside z=1 (400-bit Newton). The comment should say computed pole.

[w12 #12 freq/review] Scope note (not fixed): FreqResponse at z=1 misses a rounded discrete repeated integrator, and DCGain now copies that. Repro: den = Poly{1,-1}.Mul(Poly{1,-1}).Mul(Poly{1,-0.9999}) = [1 -2.9999000000000002 2.9998 -0.9999], num {1}, Dt 0.1, then StateSpace(). On base, DCGain is +Inf. Now DCGain = FreqResponse([0]) = -4.5036e15, which equals the exact rational value N(1)/D(1) of the rounded coefficients (D(1) = -2.2e-16). integratingDCGain, used by pidtune, is still +Inf. Cause: in poleSpacing (frequency_pole.go), the poleClusterTol near-rule only applies when s == 0, not z == 1. The double-pole spread of about 1e-8 next to 0.9999 then fails the poleStepFraction*rho test, so near=false and the dd solve succeeds. Whether a z=1 cluster rule is wanted is an owner/MATLAB-parity call.

## Decision (advisor, 2026-10-19): Option A, with Pidtune decoupled
- MATLAB parity: dcgain(ss) is evalfr(sys,1). DCGain and FreqResponse(0) must agree. MATLAB snaps to Inf only at an exact pole; a near-singular pencil returns the finite value (check against dcgain(tf(1,[1 1e-15])) = 1e15). So DCGain returns the exact finite gain when the double-double solve succeeds. Option B (a conditioning test in FreqResponse) is rejected as non-parity.
- Pidtune must stop using DCGain as its integrator detector. pidTuningDCSign returns 0 when a pole is within pidtuneClusterRadius of z=1 (the existing rounded-integrator recognition: pidtuneRoundedIntegrator/pidtuneClusterRadius), independent of DCGain.
- TestPidtuneDisplacedIntegratorDCSign keeps the same pinned gains; its premise becomes "Pidtune recognises the integrator". Do this in the same track as V2AYQB/X46RST (pid_tuning.go).

Found in wave 12. The PS6S32/IBWZGV/X7DDPS track reported that the retry path, and the unshaped rule, gated only on |S| and the existence of a crossing, return designs below the owner bar of classical PM >= 58.5 deg and |S| <= 4.
- Canonical case: Pidtune(1/(s-1), P or PI, 0) returns PM 45/42 deg. Its only crossover is at wc_auto ~0.9.
- About 301 of 11997 auto returns in the sampled population come from the retry, with worst classical margins of 10-58 deg.
- Zero-DC continuous P designs fall below the bar through the |S|-only unshaped rule. Example: pidtuneBackoffPlant(Poly{1.4392005301712567,0,0}, Poly{1,8.24762471156669,20.7899930...}).

## Decision (advisor, 2026-10-19; owner said open questions go to the advisor)
- Every returned auto design, retry and unshaped included, must meet the same bar (oracle-stable, classical PM >= 58.5 deg at every crossover, |S| <= 4).
- Before returning ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable when back-off fails, add a bounded UPWARD wc search through the same gate. Go up to about 1e3 x wc_auto, capped at Nyquist for discrete plants.
- Rationale: on unstable plants, PM grows with wc. For 1/(s-1), P with Kp=2 gives |L|=1 at sqrt(3), PM exactly 60 deg, |S|=1 everywhere, closed-loop pole -1. Back-off lowers wc, which moves the wrong way. Returning "unattainable" when Kp=2 exists would be a parity failure.
- Verify that 1/(s-1) P finds Kp ~2 with PM ~60. Report how much of the ~300 retry population gets a design that meets the bar via the upward search, and how much becomes an honest unattainable.
- If the upward search also fails, unattainable is correct.
- Fold the wave 12 reports "unstable plants still get fragile auto designs" and "zero-DC P below the bar via the unshaped rule" into this task.
Core priority for wave 13. Files: pidtune.go (pidtuneRun.attempt retry, unshaped, back-off loop).


Wave 12 reports folded in:

[w12 #45] Owner decision: the retry still returns designs below the 58.5 deg bar. After the fix, 301 of 11997 auto returns in the population come from the retry with |S| <= 4 but a worst classical margin of 10 to 58 deg. Canonical case: Pidtune(1/(s-1), PI, 0) returns Kp 1.411, Ki 0.0704 with PM 42.1 deg (P gives Kp 1.413, PM 44.9 deg). Gating the retry on the full bar would turn these into errors, but would also break TestPidtune_PI_Unstable and the 'unst' mustTune lists in TestPidtuneUnstableMirrorsPositive. It would also lose oracle-robust designs (next item). For 1/(s-1) a P with Kp 2 at wc 1.73 meets the bar, so an upward wc search for unstable plants may be the better fix. Files: pidtune.go attempt/backedOff.

[w12 #47] Unstable plants still get fragile auto designs: the retry, gated only on |S| and a crossing, is kept for plants that are not stable and returns designs under the owner bar. Repro: Pidtune(1/(s-1), P or PI, 0) gives PM 45° / 42° (the only crossover is at wc=0.9976; P at wc=sqrt(3) would give 60°). Auto PID on pidtuneBackoffPlant(Poly{0.08119770312059038,1.4299696862733304,1.1509782187662239,0.74301299939046}, Poly{1,1.5247143694217347,0.26500427775406976,1.1490289607929067}) gives Kp 0.04998, Kd 1.843, Tf 0, signed PM -28.3°. PID on {0.012117279206722564,0.6998831440522459,1.7138236892014762,1.8876491780936953}/{1,0.30102668894257456,1.2322300903394714,1.7765490062040799} gives -46.8°. PD on {0.4820870937175388,1.3079853107003931,1.9844096182517548,-1.0452039084558389}/{1,0.8298649253038679,1.349639061840446,1.53625974244542} gives -51.5°. All three plants are unstable (a1*a2 < a3). Back-off only lowers wc, which is the wrong direction for unstable plants; a fix needs an upward crossover search. Files: pidtune.go attempt/backedOff. Evidence: pidtuneCheckRobust on these plants.

[w12 #51] Pidtune P on zero-DC continuous plants returns designs below the 58.5 deg bar through the same |S|-only unshaped rule (pidtune.go pidtuneRun.unshaped/check). Repro: Pidtune(pidtuneBackoffPlant(t, Poly{1.4392005301712567,0,0}, Poly{1,8.24762471156669,20.7899930610465,15.321468764445184},0,0), PidtuneP, 0, nil) gives Kp 28.89, signed margins [-48.5, 101.4] deg, |S| 1.57, oracle-stable. Also P on 0.8542595646531987 s^2/(s^3+7.023342124760237 s^2+12.926235567617814 s+2.066641791908522): Kp 348.1, margin 29.5 deg, |S| 2.19. A seeded sweep (PCG(5,7), 400 plants k*s^m/prod(s+a_i)) found 83 P designs below 58.5 and 0 PD designs after this fix. The P exemption is the older EU24XW MATLAB-parity decision, so gating P on margin is the owner's call.

[w12 #53] Ungated retry on unstable plants returns designs below the owner's 58.5 degree bar (pidtune.go, pidtuneRun.attempt). Repro: Pidtune(PI, wc=0) on num=[6.749592744149843e-16 -6.056872503393394e-16], den=[1 -7.9623743329365935 28.09350817041953 -57.63766640485889 75.76142091126783 -66.14845014857204 38.35309958277561 -14.235001137708403 3.067835464760931 -0.29237210514798584], dt=0.01 (one pole at 1.000115). It returns Kp 176.3, Ki 0.514: closed loop stable by extended Schur–Cohn, |S| at most 4, but PM 30.5 degrees at its crossover. Base returned a design with |S| 64.2 on the same plant. The retry for gain-source crossovers on open-loop-unstable plants is gated only on |S| and on crossing 0 dB, by design (IBWZGV). The owner should decide whether such plants must return ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable instead.

[w12 #55] MATLAB parity: auto P and PI on unstable plants now return errors where MATLAB designs. Repro: Pidtune(1/(s-1), PidtuneP or PidtunePI, 0, nil) gives ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable at wc=0.9976. With PM = atan(w) + angle(C), at most 45 deg at w=1, while P reaches 60 deg at w=sqrt(3) with Kp=2. The auto crossover for unstable plants only backs off downward; an upward wc search would give designs that meet the 58.5 deg bar. Files: pidtune.go (backedOff, backoffFloor, attempt).

[w12 #61] Pidtune auto P on zero-DC k·s^m plants still passes on |S| alone through the unshaped-P rule, which PS6S32 kept unchanged. That is outside PS6S32, which covers the legacy PD only, and is the same on base. These designs miss the owner bar (PM >= 58.5 at every crossover). Repro: Pidtune(pidtuneBackoffPlant(t, Poly{-0.4747823914433865,0,0}, Poly{1,1.7019690144285535,0.19889294875649396},0,0), PidtuneP, 0, nil) gives Kp -117.685, one crossover at PM 28.9 deg, |S| 2.23. More: num {-3.815515468598575,0,0}, den {1,7.773322676859117,15.64159738856245,2.4039470279016206}: Kp -100.719, PM 29.1. num {0.17174745558754434,0,0}, den {1,4.304762793303786,3.0119125343741975}: Kp 102.277, PM 33.9. In all, 22 of 70 random zero-DC plants gave a P below 58.5 deg. File: pidtune.go, pidtuneRun.check (case r.pidType == PidtuneP: sensitive only) and unshaped. Oracle: roots of the characteristic polynomial, plus signed margins and |S| of the directly evaluated loop.

[w12 #57] Cleanup candidate: the non-stable retry in pidtuneRun.attempt (pidtune.go) is now likely redundant with the first gated design in backedOff (same gains, same gate). Confirm that the gated and ungated design paths (PIDF fallbacks, mirror) cannot diverge, then remove it.

## Decision (advisor, 2026-10-19): one 58.5° acceptance floor, applied everywhere
The gate floor pm - pidtuneMarginTol = 59.5° is an artifact; pidtuneMarginTol is a convergence tolerance around the 60° target. Keep aiming at 60°. Add a separate 58.5° acceptance-floor constant and apply it to the first design, back-off and the gated retry alike.
- Grep pidtuneMarginTol first. If it is used only as the gate floor, repoint it; otherwise keep it for convergence.
- Expected sweep changes: only error→design at ≥58.5°, plus earlier back-off steps now passing (changed gains, oracle-robust, non-blocking).
Source: wave 12 item 56. A PD at 58.56° became unattainable.

data.title: Audit test sweeps that filter on public DCGain (shrunk silently after 4M7RB3)
data.body:
Found in the wave 12 integration (fix/wave12).
After 4M7RB3, public DCGain solves near-singular pencils in double-double and returns finite values, as evalfr does. TestPidtuneIsolatedDisplacedIntegrator's sweep, which filtered on DCGain=Inf, kept 0 plants. It was re-targeted to select by poles (527e45a).
pidtune_wave9_test.go:243 and pidtune_wave10_test.go:620 also filter on p.DCGain(). They still pass, but their selection may have shrunk silently.
Fix: select by poles (pidtuneClusterRadius) or by integratingDCGain, and assert a minimum kept count.

data.title: CORE: Dare fails/wrong near-zero A eigenvalues (explicit symplectic path, scale-blind rcond test)
data.body:
Found by fuzz wave 12f. Common root: regularDiscreteStableSubspace uses A^-T whenever rcond(A)>=sqrt(eps); with tiny nonzero eigenvalues this gives false ErrNoStabilizing, silent non-stabilizing gains (Dlqr/Lqg), lost digits and PSD loss. Fix direction: always extended pencil (idare) or scale-aware suitability test; rename misleading ErrSingularR at riccati.go:438. Gates to revisit: syNearZeroDiscreteEig, syTinyDiscreteEig; FuzzRiccati has none. #12 attached per reporter; its eigenvalues give rcond far below sqrt(eps) (extended-pencil path) and it may belong to the tiny-X class - verify.

[w12f #1 fuzzmat/ML2GAC] [CORE] Dare explicit symplectic path is unreliable; regularDiscreteStableSubspace (riccati.go ~561) builds the symplectic matrix from A⁻ᵀ whenever rcond(A) >= sqrt(eps), a test that ignores scale. Repro 1 (realistic stiff c2d): Ac=[[-50,10],[0,-80]] sampled at dt=0.5 gives A=[[1.3887943864964021e-11,4.6293132055365885e-12],[0,4.248354255291589e-18]], B=[0.3;1], Q=I, R=1; Dare returns ErrNoStabilizing. At dt=1, rcond falls below sqrt(eps), the extended-pencil path runs and Dare succeeds (X≈I). At dt=0.3 with R=1e-6, X[1][1]=0.99999992 against a true value of ≈1+O(1e-13), a 1e-7 error. Repro 2 (scalar): a=1e-20, b=-0.9667981925794609, q=1e6, r=1e-3 gives ErrNoStabilizing. The true X≈q exists in closed form, and a=0 or a=1e-8 succeed. Repro 3: fuzz spec kind=0x7d vals=[0 10 0 0 -17 0 82 -13.285714285714286 0 11 0.3 0 -10 -10 -10 -40] with Q=CᵀC (~4e12) and R=DᵀD+1e-3·I (PD, min eig 1e-3). Plain Dare returns ErrSingularR (the R+BᵀXB Cholesky at riccati.go:438, reported as if R were singular). The same problem through the extended pencil (Dare with E=2I, A→2A, B→2B, X×4) gives relative residual 1.9e-12, PD X, rcnd 1e-3. Fix idea: always use the extended pencil as idare does, or bound ‖A⁻¹‖·‖G‖·‖Q‖ relative to ‖A‖ in the suitability test; also rename the error at :438. Found by FuzzRiccati (mateq_fuzz_test.go).

[w12f #4 fuzzmat/SWTCHJ] Dare wrongly returns ErrNoStabilizing, or loses about 7 digits, when A has near-zero eigenvalues [CORE-ish: discretized fast modes]. Files: Dare/Riccati solver (also reached through Kalman, Lqg, H2Syn). Repro: Dare(A=[3e-17], B=[-0.92], Q=[1], R=[1]) returns ErrNoStabilizing on arm64 and amd64, and Dare(1e-18, ...) fails too; a=0, 1e-16 and 1e-20 all solve with X close to 1. Also Dare(1e-18, [1 1], 1, I2) fails, and Kalman on the n=1 discrete model A=[1.93e-22] (dt=100, Qn=1e-3 I, Rn=1e-3 I) fails. Accuracy loss: on the fuzz tuple kind=0x61 vals=[-0.3010299956639812 2.6 -93 1 0 -6 0 94 24 -78.52287874528034 88.4 -7 -10 -10 18 -10] (fzDecode, then syNormC, then D scaled to |D|_F=1, syNoise covariances; eigenvalues about 3.5e-6 and 1), Kalman's P differs from the Hewer-Newton-converged solution by 1.5e-7 relative (1e-6 on amd64), although the Hewer Lyapunov condition is only 21 (expected error about 1e-14).

[w12f #12 fuzzmat/review] Dare loses PSD with a nonzero eigenvalue below 1e-4 (the known near-zero-eigenvalue followup class, already skipped in synth by syNearZeroDiscreteEig) also shows in FuzzRiccati's PSD check. Repro kind=0x61 vals=[-0.3010299956639812 1.8571428571428572 0 1 0 -82 0 -8 4 -73.52287874528034 0.4 0 -10 -10 -2 -96] (A eigenvalues 6e-10, 7e-52, 4e-44; S=CᵀD): min eig(X) = -7.4e-23 against ‖X‖ 2.9e-17 (2.6e-6 relative). The data bounds Q̄ rounding near 4e-28, far smaller. Corpus file testdata/fuzz/FuzzRiccati/04aa01082da1520a. Attach this to the existing near-zero-eigenvalue Dare followup.

[w12f #13 fuzzmat/review0] [CORE] Dlqr/Dare silently returns a non-stabilizing gain on a well-posed discrete LQR problem; Lqg inherits it. Repro: fzDecode(kind=0xcb, vals=[0 -2.1 -0.2 75 0.4 0.975 4.666666666666667 0.3 -0.5 -4.8999999999999995 -1.4 0.034722222222222224 3 -133 1 -10]) then syNormC. Plant: n=6, m=2, p=2, discrete, dt=0.316. Open-loop eigs 1.262±0.245i, 0.980±0.198i, 0.963 and 5.1e-8. Call Dlqr(A, B, CᵀC + 1000·I, 1e-3·I). Result: no error, Rcnd 0.012, res.Eig spectral radius 0.817, but the actual ρ(A − B·K) is 1.1235 (unstable) and the relative Riccati residual is 2.9e-2. Oracle 1: the fixed-point Riccati iteration from X=0 (200k steps) gives ρ(A − BK) = 0.8107, and the library X differs from it by 96%. Oracle 2: Dlqr on a similarity-transformed copy (T = cos-texture + 3I) gives ρ = 0.81073972648888, agreeing with the iteration to 1e-14. The FuzzLqg crasher (synth_fuzz_test.go:1199) fails on both arm64 and amd64. Suspected trigger: the near-zero nonzero eigenvalue, the same family as SWTCHJ's known 'Dare near-zero eigenvalue accuracy loss' followup. It is more severe than that note says, though: a wrong stabilizing claim with no error, not seven lost digits. Files: riccati.go (Dare), controller.go (Dlqr), lqg.go.

[w12f #14 fuzzmat/review0] [CORE] Dare reports a false ErrNoStabilizing on a solvable discrete Kalman problem with an eigenvalue of 3.2e-7, far above the 1e-12 window of the known followup. Repro: fzDecode(kind=0xc5, vals=[97.69897000433602 13 0 1 0 54 0 0 -0.125 -0.5228787452803376 0.4 0 29 -30 -7 -39]) then syNormC. Plant: n=6, m=3, p=1, discrete, dt=0.75, D=0. Eigs -0.99922±0.03956i, 0.9631, 3.18e-7 and 0.7318±0.6816i. Call Dare(Aᵀ, Cᵀ, B·1000I·Bᵀ, [1e-3]) and it returns ErrNoStabilizing (Kalman fails the same way). Oracle 1: the fixed-point iteration converges to a stabilizing P with ρ(A − LC) = 0.9628, ‖P‖ = 8.5e4 and absolute residual 2.4e-11. Oracle 2: the same Dare succeeds on a similarity-transformed copy, and also with Rn scaled by 1e-3 or 1e3. Only Rn=1e-3 fails, so this is a numerical failure, not infeasibility. The crasher fails on arm64 and passes on amd64. Files: riccati.go (Dare), observer.go (Kalman).

[w12f #16 fuzzmat/review1] [EDGE] Dare reports ErrNoStabilizing on a trivially solvable n=1 problem whose eigenvalue is a subnormal-scale nonzero 3.72e-44. |a| < 1, so even K=0 stabilizes. This is the known syTinyDiscreteEig family, but FuzzRiccati has no gate for it, so it fails at mateq_fuzz_test.go:800. Repro: FuzzRiccati with kind=0x31 vals=[0 10 -81 0 -2 0 -5.714285714285714 0 99 56 14.3 0 -10 -10 -10 -10] (also with v[11]=10); n=1 m=1 p=3, discrete, dt=100.

data.title: CORE: Care/Dare accuracy absolute not relative when ||X|| or Qbar tiny vs Hamiltonian; no scaling
data.body:
Found by fuzz wave 12f. Common root: no Hamiltonian/symplectic scaling (SB02MD SCAL='G') or refinement; when ||Q||/Qbar << pencil scale X has few/no correct digits, often indefinite, while Rcnd looks fine. Cost-scale invariance (Q=cI,R=c) fails. Fix: scale Q,G (sigma=sqrt(||Q||/||G||)) before Schur + Newton/defect-correction. Also revisit the test gates that hide this: synth_fuzz_test.go syQbarDigits/syQbarRatio (#11) and mateq_fuzz_test.go:841-847 ratio<1 gate (#15).

[w12f #2 fuzzmat/ML2GAC] [CORE-borderline] Care accuracy is absolute rather than relative when ‖Q‖ (or Q̄=Q−SR⁻¹Sᵀ) is small next to the Hamiltonian scale; there is no Hamiltonian/X scaling (SLICOT SB02MD SCAL='G'-style σ=√(‖Q‖/‖G‖)), only the power-of-two state scaling. Repro 1 (cost-scale invariance, where K should not depend on c): A=[[-300,900],[-900,-300]], B=[0.45;-0.74], Q=c·I, R=c. Relative error in X against a Newton–Kleinman reference (20 iterations with library Lyap): 8e-16 at c=1, 1.16e-6 at c=1e-8 and c=1e-12; X12 also flips sign. Repro 2: A=[[-3162.2776601683786,9486.832980505138],[-9486.832980505138,-3162.2776601683786]], B=[0.4543874744042692;-0.7367935074839924], C=[9.555985806128393e-07,-5.87782813560387e-07], Q=CᵀC, R=1e-3. Care returns the indefinite X=[[0,-2.6269e-17],[-2.6269e-17,-2.4181e-17]] (relative residual 0.57) against the true PSD X=[[1.30637e-16,4.5827e-18],[4.5827e-18,6.83747e-17]] (Newton and Lyap(Aᵀ,Q) agree), a relative error of 1.12. NoScaling gives the same wrong X. Solving with Q/σ, R/σ for σ=1e-8 or 1e-12 and multiplying X back by σ reproduces the reference to 15 digits. EDGE variants with S=CᵀD and D≫C (Q̄~1e-20): X comes out ~1e-20 and indefinite against a reference ~1e-15. Found by FuzzRiccati (residual and PSD checks).

[w12f #7 fuzzmat/SWTCHJ] Kalman/Care with a cross term loses about 5 digits when Q - S R^-1 S' cancels heavily (large noise feedthrough H) [EDGE]. Files: observer.go kalmanGain and the Care cross-term path. Repro: fuzz tuple kind=0x60 vals=[80.33333333333333 1 52 1 0 0 -74 -406 19 -80 -41.63 0 -60 -10 -10 -10], then fzDecode, syNormC and syNoise (continuous, n=3, m=p=1, eigenvalues -501, -1e4, -2e5, D=400.9, Qn=1e-3, Rn=1e-3). Kalman's P differs from the Newton-refined solution by 2.5e-5 relative (1.4e-5 on amd64), although the Newton Lyapunov condition is 398 (expected error at most 1e-8, even allowing for the cancellation).

[w12f #10 fuzzmat/review] Care/Dare return X with no correct digits when ‖X‖ ≪ eps·h/sep (tiny Q relative to the Hamiltonian/symplectic pencil). Files: riccati.go (Care, Dare); repros in testdata/fuzz/FuzzRiccati/{qbar_cancel_care,05f026066ef0152b,49bc55497b8edd5e,01cfcd9329a43a10,0a0a7a0366581a52} (run go test -run FuzzRiccati/<name> with the skip removed). Evidence from a 300-bit big.Float oracle (residual ~1e-94, closed loop Hurwitz). Case 1, Care with S, kind=0x44 vals=[0 5 0 0 -17 0 0 -93 86 11 0.075 -62 -10 -10 -1.6666666666666667 -10]: true X=[6.75e-16 -1.71e-15; · 4.63e-15], lib X=[3.3e-36 9.1e-20; · -1.1e-19], indefinite under a PSD cost; changing inputs by ±2^-52 moves X 3.8e-9. Case 2, Care with no S, kind=0x60 vals=[44.69897000433602 1.4444444444444444 6 0.5 0 -17 0 -80 0 4.294091292476962 -8.32 -61 -3.4285714285714284 -10 -72 -77]: lib X off by 106% (lib indefinite), data sensitivity 6e-13. Case 3, Care with generic S, kind=0x40 vals=[115 2 0 0 0 69 0 354 0 -0.1388888888888889 0.37 -240 -165 -10 96.57142857142857 -10]: lib off 5.2e-6, sensitivity 4e-16. Case 4, Dare with no S, kind=0x61 vals=[96.69897000433602 2.311111111111111 -2 8 40 0 0 11 -47 -0.5228787452803376 -9.6 71 -5 -10 -10 -54] (pole at 1-1e-6): true X11=6.58e-13 vs lib 5.7e-14; lib X eigenvalues include -2.26e-13 under a PSD cost; sensitivity 5e-11. Milder no-S case kind=0x82 vals=[-0.03762874945799765 4.875 0 6 -63 0 0 0 0 -0.05228787452803376 0.4 -88 -10 54 -10 -10]: lib off 4.2e-8, sensitivity 3e-12; still fails FuzzRiccati and is not skipped. Rcnd reported 0.26-0.52 (looks well conditioned) in all cases. Fix hint: Hamiltonian balancing/scaling of Q,G before the Schur step, then Newton or defect-correction refinement. Not checked whether MATLAB icare/idare share the loss.

[w12f #11 fuzzmat/review] synth_fuzz_test.go syQbarDigits/syQbarRatio gate (SWTCHJ, used in syRiccatiChecks and the Kalman checks) rests on the same false premise as finding ML2GAC: that a large Q̄ cancellation makes the residual pure rounding. The exact oracle shows that on such an input the given data fixes X to about 9 digits while Care returns a wrong, indefinite X. The gate likely skips or loosens checks exactly where the library is wrong. Coordinator should revisit it (replace with the mqRiccatiBelowSchurAccuracy known-followup skip, or remove). Files: synth_fuzz_test.go:480-535.

[w12f #15 fuzzmat/review1] [EDGE] Care/Dare: X loses accuracy far beyond its conditioning when ‖X‖ is small relative to eps·h/sep, at ratios ‖X‖·sep/(eps·h) of 1.67 to 1090. The 956ba4c gate covers only ratio < 1, so either this family is broader than the known tiny-X followup or that gate is too narrow. Files: mateq_fuzz_test.go:841-847 (gate), Care/Dare Schur path. Repro: corpus file `go test fuzz v1` / byte / 16 float64s replayed through FuzzRiccati. Oracle: Newton-Kleinman in 400-bit big.Float, started from the library X, solving the exact reformulated Ā = A−BR⁻¹Sᵀ, Q̄ = Q−SR⁻¹Sᵀ problem. The rounded exact X gives a relative residual of about 1e-17. Cases (kind|vals → lib relerr vs 1-ulp sensitivity): 0x82|-0.03762874945799765 4.875 0 6 -63 0 0 0 0 -0.05228787452803376 0.4 -88 -10 54 -10 -10 → Care 4.2e-8 vs 1.8e-12. 0xaa|-0.160270624793612 6 -0.16020781555467062 6.3 0.652072438895929 1 0 -3 0 -1 0.7 1.4000000000000001 -10 -10 -10 -10 → Care 1.7e-8 vs 2.0e-12. 0x61|96.69897000433602 1.4444444444444444 0 1 0 0 0 -30 -47 -0.5228787452803376 -9.6 71 -10 -10 -10 -54 → Dare 1.2e-4 vs 6.6e-14. 0xaa|... 0.4890543291719468 1 0 -69 0 -1 81.7 0.2 -10 -10 -10 -10 → Care 2.4e-7 vs 8.4e-13. 0x61|96.69897000433602 1.4444444444444444 39 1 0 0 0 -180 -235 -0.5228787452803376 -9.6 3.55 -10 21 -1 -54 (S = CᵀD) → Dare 3.3e-4 vs 1.0e-14. 0x82|-0.3010299956639812 1.625 0 6 -96 0 0 0 0 -0.05228787452803376 0.4 0 -10 54 -10 -10 → Care 1.75e-8 vs 2.5e-12. 0x61|... 11 -47 ... → Dare 1.0e-3 vs 6.6e-14. Typical features: ‖Q‖ around 1e-12 (C ~ 1e-6), lightly damped poles (Re ≈ -1e-4), large R.

data.title: CORE: Mixsyn discrete fast sampling + slow W1 pole near z=1 misses optimum or errors (Tustin route)
data.body:
Found by fuzz wave 12f. Arch-dependent gamma; continuous model and dt>=1e-2 give optimum 100.

[w12f #3 fuzzmat/SWTCHJ] Mixsyn on discrete plants with fast sampling and a slow W1 pole misses the optimum or errors [CORE]. Files: mixsyn.go, hinfsyn.go (Tustin route). Repro: G = static 3x2 D=[1.791152303441311 1.996271392265902; -1.5262459503191588 -1.9090913878947715; 1.1726896315364728 1.7110243499204902], dt=1e-4; W1 = 0.5 + 99.5(1-a)/(z-a) with a = exp(-wb*1e-2*dt); W2 = 0.01; Mixsyn(G, W1, W2, nil). The true optimum is 100 (the uncontrollable output direction leaves S=1 there, so gamma >= W1 DC gain = 100); the continuous model and dt >= 1e-2 return 100.000. Results with wb=0.01 (pole 1-1e-8): arm64 returns 'gamma = 5.6e10 not achievable', amd64 returns gamma=16016. With wb=1: gamma=101.39 (arm64) and 100.39 (amd64). Second case: square D with cond 9e15 (D=[-295.5624313490308 -362.7394643253653 -372.64791180215923; 231.37253359097448 328.52510561216616 373.81078706911444; -153.7436700139788 -275.228803176164 -353.26136004934426]) at dt=1e-4: wb=0.01 errors, wb=1 gives 252.8 (585.9 on amd64), against the expected ~100.

data.title: EDGE: HinfSyn false 'P21(z=1) not full row rank' for discrete pole within 1e-14 of z=1
data.body:
Found by fuzz wave 12f. Passes at A=1, 1-1e-12; H2Syn fine. Rank-test tolerance.

[w12f #5 fuzzmat/SWTCHJ] HinfSyn reports a rank-deficient P21(z=1) for a discrete pole within about 1e-14 of z=1 [EDGE]. Files: hinfsyn.go (handling of modes near z=±1). Repro: fuzz tuple kind=0x31 vals=[-10 1 -31 4 -24 -37 0 39 -783 -1.6666666666666667 -57.63 0 -10 -10 -10 -10], then fzDecode, syNormC and syRegPlant (n=1, m=1, p=3, dt=1e-4, B=[-0.9667981925794609], C=[-1.0153621182995027 -1.1701046921324967 -0.7745287458654208], D=[-38.51171102644574 38.865141783905486 -36.96114248311336], rho=sigma=0.01). With A=[1-1e-14], HinfSyn returns 'P21(z = 1) does not have full row rank 3: ErrInvalidPartition' on arm64 and amd64. data.title: CORE: Parallel drops I/O delay when equal totals split differently between input/output delay
data.body:
Found by fuzz wave 12f. parallelDelayPlan td1==td2 branch / parallelInputOutputDelay never moves residual into ioDelay.

[w12f #18 fuzzsys/U6H6TG] CORE: Parallel loses part of the I/O delay when both models have the same total delay per channel but split differently between input and output delay. Repro: g1 = NewFromSlices(1,1,1,{0.5},{1},{1},{0},0.1) with InputDelay [3] and OutputDelay [2]; g2 = NewFromSlices(1,1,1,{-0.3},{1},{1},{0},0.1) with InputDelay [2] and OutputDelay [3]. r, _ := Parallel(g1, g2) has InputDelay [2], OutputDelay [2], no IODelay and no internal delay. At z = 0.3+1.1i, r.EvalFr = 0.88187-0.33814i, while g1.EvalFr + g2.EvalFr = -0.08261-0.82424i; their ratio is exactly z, so one sample is lost. The continuous case fails the same way (in 0.3 / out 0.2 against in 0.2 / out 0.3). Files: interconnection_topology.go parallelDelayPlan (around lines 79-96, the td1 == td2 branch) and connect.go parallelInputOutputDelay: when residual1 == residual2 != 0 the residual is never added to resultIO. Found by FuzzParallel (delayed rerun).

[w12f #25 fuzzsys/review0] CORE: Parallel silently drops I/O delays when both channels have the same total delay but split it differently between input and output delay. Repro (connect.go Parallel -> interconnection_topology.go parallelDelayPlan / parallelInputOutputDelay): G1=1/(s+1) with InputDelay 2 and OutputDelay 0.5, G2=1/(s+2) with InputDelay 0.5 and OutputDelay 2. Parallel(G1,G2).EvalFr(0.1+0.7i) = 0.4211-1.0108i. The exact value e^{-2.5z}/(z+1)+e^{-2.5z}/(z+2) = -0.5743-0.7473i. The result has InputDelay [0.5], OutputDelay [0.5], no Delay and no LFT, so 1.5s of delay is lost. Second repro: G1 with InputDelay 2 and G2 with OutputDelay 2. The result has zero delays and returns the delay-free sum 1.0756-0.5546i; the exact value is -0.2978-0.9450i. Third repro: in/out (2,0.5) vs (1,1.5) gives InputDelay 1, OutputDelay 0.5, total 1.5 instead of 2.5. Cause: parallelDelayPlan sees equal total delays (mat.Equal(td1,td2)), skips the LFT path, and parallelInputOutputDelay keeps only the common in/out parts without moving the residual into ioDelay. Unequal totals (e.g. G1 delay-free, G2 InputDelay 0.5) correctly go through the LFT path and match exactly. Fuzz evidence: FuzzParallel -fuzz found kind=0x20 vals=[0 1 0 0 0 -52 44 0.5 20 -10 0.0925 -79 89 -1.4285714285714286 -4 55.083333333333336] within 2s. Got 488405.8-73451.9i; exact -167061.6-11570.2i, which equals g1+g2 from the delayed components' own EvalFr. MATLAB parallel keeps the full e^{-tau s} on each branch.

data.title: CORE: PullDelaysToLFT wrong for static gain with InputDelay+OutputDelay+IODelay
data.body:
Found by fuzz wave 12f. 

[w12f #19 fuzzsys/U6H6TG] CORE: PullDelaysToLFT gives a wrong model for a static gain (n=0) that has InputDelay, OutputDelay and an IODelay matrix all set. Repro: g := NewGain([[0.03,-0.24],[-0.47,-0.19]], 0); InputDelay [0 1]; OutputDelay [1 0]; SetDelay([[1 0],[0 0]]); pl, _ := g.PullDelaysToLFT(). At s = j, g.EvalFr matches D·exp(-s·(in_j+out_i+io_ij)) exactly, but pl.EvalFr entry (0,1) is off by 0.23 (|D01| = 0.24). A second case, in [1 0], out [1 0], io [[0 1],[0 0]], has entry (0,0) off by 0.029. This feeds LFT, Connect and ConnectByName with such static blocks. Example: LFT(gain -1.6787 with in = out = 19.95, a 2×3 static gain with in [19.95 39.9 59.85], out [39.9 19.95], io [[0 19.95 39.9],[0 19.95 39.9]]) is about 2.5% off at ω = 12, checked against a composition of the components' own EvalFr. File: delay.go PullDelaysToLFT, the static residual-merge block around lines 1410-1470.

data.title: EDGE: internal-delay EvalFr returns 0/+Inf when one pole is >=1e17x the others
data.body:
Found by fuzz wave 12f. 

[w12f #20 fuzzsys/U6H6TG] EDGE: evaluating an internal-delay model returns exactly 0 or +Inf when one component pole is about 1e17 or more larger than the others. The delay-free result and each component's EvalFr are correct. Repro inside the test package: s := fzDecode(t, 0x77, [0 15 v2 -40 95 -100 0.17142857142857143 0.5 0 -10 2.37 0 19 -10 67 -112.75]) with partner fzICPartner(t, s, 1, 3, 3). This is a 3-state discrete model (Dt = 1) with poles e^{±i} and one large real pole, with InputDelay [20 40 60] and an IO pattern; the partner is static with OutputDelay [60 40 20]. Parallel(delayed).EvalFr(-0.4933+0.9495i) is correct for v2 <= 1.3 (pole 4.6e8). It is +Inf for v2 = 1.6 (pole 1.9e17) and exactly 0 for v2 = 1.8 (pole 2.5e27) and v2 = 2 (pole 2.7e43), while the true value is 0.12607-0.02029i. Feedback, Connect and ConnectByName show the same behaviour with discrete Dt = 100 (pole e^{100}). The targets skip delayed reruns above a 1e12 pole-magnitude span, so this will not re-fire.

data.title: EDGE: scripts/fuzz.sh amd64 replay uses wrong package dir for root-package crashers
data.body:
Found by fuzz wave 12f. Tooling bug.

[w12f #21 fuzzsys/U6H6TG] Tooling: scripts/fuzz.sh never replays new crashers from the root package under GOARCH=amd64. For f = ./testdata/fuzz/FuzzX/hash, dir=$(dirname $(dirname $(dirname f))) gives ./testdata, so the replay prints 'FAIL ./testdata [setup failed]'. Seen when replaying the FuzzLFT crasher.
