data.title: CORE: C2D ZOH fractional output delay uses e^{-A*rho}; blows up for stiff modes (Step/Lsim)
data.body:
Found by fuzz wave 12f. 

[w12f #22 fuzzsys/ITZUOM] CORE: ZOH C2D fractional OUTPUT delay realized as C*e^{-A*rho} (backward-time exponential), numerically unstable for stiff modes. Files: conversion_delay.go discretizeZOHExternal (call conversionZOHKernel(cont.A, cont.B, -rho); out.C = C*backA), reached via C2D(ZOH), Step/Impulse auto-discretization and Lsim. Repro: sys = NewFromSlices(1,1,1, A=[-1e6], B=[1], C=[1e6], D=[0], 0); sys.SetOutputDelay([]float64{4.7471708}); Step(sys, 20) -> dt=2e-4 and max |y - (1-exp(a(t-tau)))| = 1.0e60 (exact response bounded by 1). A=-2e6 gives 3e134, A=-4e6 gives 1.4e283, A=-1e5 gives 1.1e-8 (all far above rounding). The same delay as InputDelay or as an IO Delay gives errors around 1e-14. Same numbers under GOARCH=amd64. Mechanism: the error grows like e^{(max Re s - min Re s)*rho}*eps. In a MIMO fuzz case with poles 0.32+-0.95i and 1.58, dt=100 and output delay 19.95, the relative error was 3e-5 with no overflow. In a first-order Lsim with A=-1.58, dt=100 and output delay 50, the relative error was 7e19. Realistic trigger: a fast mode plus a sensor delay on the Step automatic horizon, where the autoMaxSamples cap makes dt = tFinal/1e5. Suggested fix direction (not verified): sample forward from x_k with e^{A(dt-rho)} and the integral over [0, dt-rho] instead of propagating backward from x_{k+1}. Coverage note: timeresp_fuzz_test.go fzTROverflow skips this case for Step, Impulse and Lsim; remove the skip once fixed.

data.title: CORE: StepInfo uses yinit=y(0) instead of MATLAB yinit=0; wrong metrics when D!=0
data.body:
Found by fuzz wave 12f. MATLAB parity semantic bug; add yinit option.

[w12f #23 fuzzsys/ITZUOM] CORE (MATLAB parity): StepInfo and StepInfoForSystem use yinit = y(0) (response_info.go stepMetricForRow: initial := resp.Y.At(row, 0)), but MATLAB stepinfo uses yinit = 0, both for a model ('For a dynamic system model sys, stepinfo uses yinit = 0 and yfinal = steady-state value') and as the default of stepinfo(y,t). Rise limits, overshoot and undershoot normalization, and the settling band (threshold*|yfinal - yinit|) all depend on yinit, so metrics are wrong whenever D != 0. Repro: G = (s+2)/(s+1) as NewFromSlices(1,1,1, [-1],[1],[1],[1], 0); StepInfoForSystem(sys, 20, nil) gives RiseTime 2.1972 and SettlingTime 3.95. With MATLAB semantics y = 2 - e^{-t} gives RiseTime ln5 = 1.609 (10% level 0.2 already met at t=0) and SettlingTime about ln(1/0.04) = 3.22 (band 0.04). StepInfoOptions also has no yinit field (MATLAB has one). Responses without feedthrough are unaffected (y(0) = 0). When fixed, update fzStepMetric in timeresp_fuzz_test.go, which mirrors the current y(0) rule.

data.title: CORE: CtrbF/ObsvF/Reduce count rounding-noise SVs as rank (per-block relative threshold)
data.body:
Found by fuzz wave 12f. Common root: staircase.go threshold := tol*fnorm per block, absFloor only on block norm. Fix: per-SV threshold max(tol*||block||, absFloor) / MATLAB absolute default. Cross-ref PKUP2G and JBKTCQ (opposite direction: absolute floor drops tiny B) - fix must reconcile both.

[w12f #26 fuzzstruct/GHNJYJ] CORE: CtrbF/ObsvF/Reduce (staircase.go:114 `threshold := tol * fnorm`) count rounding noise as rank whenever a staircase block is small compared with ‖A‖. absFloor is applied only to the whole block's norm, not to each singular value. Primary repro, reproduces on both arm64 and amd64: A=[-1e4 0 0 0; 0 -1 0 0; 1 0 -2 0; 0 1e-13 0 -3], B=[1 0; 0 1; 0 0; 0 0], C=[1 1 1 1]. CtrbF(A,B,C,0).K=[2 2] and Reduce(ReduceUncontrollable).Order=4. With A[3,1]=0 K=[2 1]. The 1e-13 coupling is 1e-17 relative to ‖A‖, which MATLAB's absolute default tol (10·n·norm(A,1)·eps ≈ 9e-11) would treat as zero. Secondary repro, arm64 only (passes on amd64): s:=fzDecode(t,0xba,[0 1.5 66 1.5 0.7 25 0 0 0 -10 0.37 0 0.5 0 68.7 0.3]); e:=fzExtend(s). ObsvF gives K=[2 2 2] (6 states) although the exact rational rank is 5 (two exactly unobservable states injected). Step trace: singular values [5.78, 3.99e-13], threshold tol·fnorm=6.29e-14, absFloor=1.03e-9, so 3.99e-13 is counted. Suggested fix: per-singular-value threshold max(tol·‖block‖, absFloor). Reduce ReduceAll/ReduceUnobservable go wrong the same way (e.g. fuzz tuple kind=0xa8: 7 states kept, 5 expected). Not to be confused with the precision limit on ill-conditioned staircases (noise 5e-10 above the floor), which is not this bug.

[w12f #38 fuzzstruct/review0] CORE: CtrbF/ObsvF and Reduce (minreal) keep structurally unobservable/uncontrollable states. Cause: staircase.go uses a relative rank threshold for each block (tol*||block||_F, tol=n^2*eps), so in a small later block a singular value at rounding-noise level (~1e-14) clears the threshold (~3.7e-15). MATLAB ctrbf/obsvf use a default tolerance that is absolute in ||A|| (10*n*norm(A,1)*eps per the docs; I recalled this, did not run MATLAB), which would reject that noise. Repro: FuzzCtrbF input kind=0xda vals=[-1 335 58.25 3 -89.8125 0.13333333333333333 -40 0 -45 -4.3125 -78.92222222222222 0.6 -2 0 -6.6000000000000005 0.3] through fzExtend gives N=10: a 6-state core (poles -0.003, ±0.1i, -1000±9950i, ||A||_F=2.4e4, C~1e6) plus 2 states with exactly zero B rows that the core never drives and 2 states with exactly zero C columns that never drive the core. Results: ObsvF K=[3 3 3] (9 observable), but its own Abar/Cbar show state 1 with Cbar column <=2e-21 and Abar coupling <=6e-13, which is unobservable by the library's own absolute floor (5.4e-10). A reference SVD staircase with an absolute floor finds 8, with a 1e3 gap on each side of every rank decision. Downstream: Sminreal returns 6 states (correct), Reduce(ReduceUnobservable) returns 9 (expected <=8), Reduce(ReduceUncontrollable) and Reduce(ReduceAll) return 10, and CtrbF gives K=[2 2 2 2 2]. Same result on amd64. Files: staircase.go:66-125 (absFloor and threshold := tol*fnorm), ctrbobsv.go:105-141 (doc says the tolerance deliberately differs from MATLAB). The I/O response is unaffected; only the order/minimality is wrong. Coordinator: the author may already have filed a variant; please dedupe.

[w12f #41 fuzzstruct/review1] CORE: CtrbF/ObsvF overcount the rank of an exactly uncontrollable or unobservable state (staircase.go controllabilityStaircase), and Reduce(ReduceUnobservable) is affected too. Cause: once a block passes fnorm > absFloor (tol*||A||), each singular value is compared only against the relative threshold tol*fnorm; there is no absolute floor per value. A block whose real part is about 1e-5 therefore counts rounding noise of about 1e-15 as rank. MATLAB uses an absolute default, n*norm(A,1)*eps, and gets this right. Repro (N=6, m=1, p=2, state 3 exactly unobservable): A=[197.11151535898398 -125.58165054554455 129.30370945971754 0 59.76947800347428 -5.265470231350326; -173.82085079604235 110.9846205585125 -114.44113190250626 0 -9.172863226049667 4.351756247287568; 136.7917714371087 -87.3782153938056 89.80570195554552 0 198.7113470934537 -4.207586106182046; 65.96476980969965 168.26520163148763 20.78475297333022 -0.31697863849222285 -106.39718338430359 188.40590032108176; 0 0 0 0 -0.15848931924611143 0; -35.79801621875614 23.572121758723704 -24.270765434267762 0 -196.34760124624893 -5.173930199602784], B=[0.5260775173811046; -0.01238866346289056; -0.9667981925794609; 0.3422733332214033; 0; 0.9601702866503661], C=[-4.3137684497061916e-07 -2.1079579943077972e-07 -8.568887533689471e-07 0 0.44660305575466125 9.931849187581927e-07; -9.111302618846769e-07 4.685166713003763e-07 -9.87479769908865e-07 0 0.4537233907250981 6.845466664428065e-07]. ObsvF(A,B,C,0) returns K=[2 2 2] (6 observable). Evidence that 5 is correct: the column for state 3 has zeros in C and in every other state's A row (exact structure from fzExtend), Obsv(A,C) has smallest singular value 3.3e-25, and ObsvF with tol 1e-14, 1e-12 or 1e-10 returns K=[2 2 1]. Abar shows noise of about 1e-15 in the unobservable coupling column being counted. Reduce(ReduceUnobservable) keeps 6 states on the same model; ReduceAll gives 4. Frequency: 4/2000 random FuzzCtrbF inputs on arm64 and 1/2000 on amd64, one of them CtrbF on a plain stiff plant: kind=0xae vals=[3 0 0.041993326592123736 0 -2.5862264388196863 0 0.6290414021982818 0.9141879810006508 0.687592153854844 -2.6945352201173414 -0.3240245478126962 -2 -2.934290568198731 0 -0.9801932348643629 0] (n=5, eig -5, -2e5, -5.5e-3, -220, -2.6e-3, condT 1.01, CtrbF K=[2 2 2] > 5). More ObsvF repros: kind=0x8c vals=[3 -1.2125755640793665 0 1.7804972689269993 0 -0.9732752605414227 -0.270240917348071 0.8868798792968446 -1 0 -3 0 1.2607636759098273 -1.8433242554233757 2.1906446725604654 2.3295988701096793] and kind=0xd6 vals=[-1.9267753943343813 -2.8464772362559905 -2.0951328559193296 -2.0601571048480407 0 -1 -1.1840262596694635 1.341242491997211 0.882534697639497 0.38794678127426163 0 -0.44674391775313427 -2.985434453550364 -0.07822883375954204 -1.3364640952854452 -1.2337450091041635]. Files: staircase.go, ctrbobsv.go, minimal.go, minreal_fuzz_test.go:438 (FuzzCtrbF). The GHNJYJ fix summary was cut off in my task text, so the implementer may already have filed this; coordinator should dedupe.

[w12f #45 fuzzstruct/review2] [controlsys, CORE/MATLAB parity] With the default tol=0, CtrbF/ObsvF set the rank threshold at n²·eps times each staircase block's own norm, not times ‖A‖. A rounding-noise singular value is then counted as rank once a block is small relative to ‖A‖, so the routine reports states that are structurally unobservable as observable. Repro: FuzzCtrbF kind=0xaa vals=[0 3 0.25 -83.7 59 -66 -60 0 0 -1 0.8 0 2 2.2 30 -1.3] (fzExtend: N=9, Ko=2, ‖A‖₂=2.07e4, condT 1.27). The reference SVD staircase on (Aᵀ,Cᵀ) has step block SVs [0.594, 6.94e-14]; 6.94e-14 is below eps·‖A‖ (4.6e-12). ObsvF(A,B,C,0) returns K=[2 2 2 2], sum 8, but the structural maximum is 7. MATLAB obsvf's default absolute tol (about 10·n·‖A‖₁·eps ≈ 6e-10) gives 7, and ObsvF(…,1e-10) also gives [2 2 2 1]. Files: ctrbobsv.go, staircase.go controllabilityStaircase (threshold := tol*fnorm).

data.title: CORE: Modsep discrete splits on |z| instead of natural frequency |ln z|/Ts
data.body:
Found by fuzz wave 12f. Flip TestModsep_Discrete (modsep_test.go:108) and remove FuzzModsep discrete skip with fix.

[w12f #27 fuzzstruct/GHNJYJ] CORE: Modsep splits discrete models by |z| < cutoff (modsep.go isSlow uses cmplx.Abs(ev) on z). This contradicts its own doc ('natural frequency below cutoff'), MATLAB freqsep, and the library's Damp, which computes natural frequency as |cmplx.Log(p)/Dt| (response.go:915). Repro: A=diag(0.1,0.5,0.99), B=C=I, D=0, Ts=0.1, Modsep(sys,0.3). The library returns Slow={0.1}. By |ln z|/Ts (ωn = 23.0, 6.93, 0.1005) Slow should be {0.99} and Fast {0.1,0.5}. The existing TestModsep_Discrete (modsep_test.go:108) asserts the wrong split and must flip with the fix. FuzzModsep skips the discrete split check until this is fixed; that skip should be removed when it is.

[w12f #39 fuzzstruct/review0] CORE: Modsep on discrete models splits on |z| < cutoff instead of MATLAB freqsep's natural frequency |ln z|/Ts, which can reverse the slow/fast split. Repro: New(A=diag(0.1,0.5,0.99), B=[1;1;1], C=[1 1 1], D=0, dt=0.1), then Modsep(sys, 0.3) returns Slow.A=[0.1] (23 rad/s) and Fast.A=diag(0.5,0.99). MATLAB gives Slow={0.99} (0.1005 rad/s) and Fast={0.1 (23 rad/s), 0.5 (6.93 rad/s)}. File: modsep.go:28-30 (isSlow := cmplx.Abs(ev) < cutoff). TestModsep_Discrete (modsep_test.go:108) passes the wrong behaviour because only the state counts happen to match. The author already flagged this in modsep_fuzz_test.go:17-20.

[w12f #46 fuzzstruct/review2] [controlsys, CORE] For discrete models Modsep classifies modes by |z| < cutoff; MATLAB freqsep uses the natural frequency |ln z|/Ts. Repro: NewFromSlices(2,1,1, A=diag(0.5,0.99), B=[1;1], C=[1 1], D=0, dt=0.1), Modsep(sys, 1). The library puts both modes in Slow and none in Fast. MATLAB gives Slow={0.99} (wn 0.1005) and Fast={0.5} (wn 6.93). File: modsep.go isSlow.

data.title: CORE: Modsep puts near-defective double-integrator mode into Fast
data.body:
Found by fuzz wave 12f. 

[w12f #43 fuzzstruct/review2] [controlsys, CORE] Modsep puts a mode with |s| far below cutoff into Fast. Repro: A = T*diag-block([0 1;0 0], -100)*inv(T) with T having N(0,1) entries (rand PCG(1,2)), B=[1;1;1], C=[1 0 1], D=0, Modsep(sys, 1e-2). In 154 of 2000 trials Slow has 1 state instead of 2. Example (trial 9): poles are -100 and ±1.39e-7, and Fast poles are [-5.5e-8, -100]. MATLAB freqsep puts both double-integrator modes in Slow. Fuzz input: FuzzModsep kind=0x6a vals=[-27 10.5 2 -59.4 0 -39 -16 -92 0 62 0.8 -88 51 2 -1 -10], cutoff 3.16e-6: the poles computed from A are ±2e-13, yet Fast contains -2.05e-13. Files: modsep.go, decomposeByEigenvalues (the Schur reorder/split of nearly defective block).

data.title: EDGE: Canon modal trusts inaccurate eigenvectors (no residual check before Schur fallback)
data.body:
Found by fuzz wave 12f. 

[w12f #28 fuzzstruct/GHNJYJ] EDGE: Canon modal returns an Ac that is neither block diagonal nor quasi-triangular when gonum's eigenvectors are inaccurate. canonModalEig checks only cond(T) ≤ 1e12, never the residual ‖AV−VΛ‖, before trusting the eigenvector path instead of falling back to Schur. Repro (both platforms): s:=fzDecode(t,0x7f,[0.1 0.3 2.4000000000000004 0.2 -10.625 75 86 0 -0.23299000144533957 41 0.015416666666666667 550 -10 -1 9 -10]); Canon(s.System(t,fzSysOpts{}),CanonModal). The model is a 3×3 discrete A that is nearly rank 1 with a row of ~1e-34. gonum Eigen returns an eigenvector for λ ≈ -9.6e-35 with residual 0.17. Ac[2,0] = -0.17 on arm64 and 0.85 on amd64, against ‖A‖ ≈ 8, while cond(T) ≈ 46. Suggested fix: check the residual of A·T versus T·Ac and fall back to canonModalSchur when it is above rounding level.

data.title: EDGE: Prescale on static gain (n=0) returns unit scales instead of 1/max|D|
data.body:
Found by fuzz wave 12f. Remove FuzzPrescale n=0 skip with fix.

[w12f #29 fuzzstruct/GHNJYJ] EDGE: Prescale on a static gain (n=0) returns InputScale/OutputScale all ones instead of the documented reciprocal column/row maxima of [Bs; D] / [Cs D], which reduce to 1/max|D| when there are no states (prescale.go n==0 shortcut). Repro: NewGain(D=[[-3.95,-3.39,-2.30],[3.99,3.80,3.02]]). Prescale gives InputScale[0]=1, but 1/max(3.95,3.99)=0.2509. FuzzPrescale skips n=0 for the scale check until this is fixed.

[w12f #40 fuzzstruct/review0] EDGE/low: Prescale on a static gain returns InputScale/OutputScale = 1 regardless of D, while its own doc (prescale.go:13-16) says each is the reciprocal of the largest magnitude in the column of [Bs; D] or row of [Cs D]. Repro: Prescale(NewGain([[4]], 0)) gives Info.InputScale=[1], OutputScale=[1]; the doc implies 0.25. File: prescale.go:52-57 (n==0 branch). The author already flagged this in scaling_fuzz_test.go:201.

data.title: EDGE: SsbalResult doc states wrong transform (T^-1AT) vs code/MATLAB (TA/T)
data.body:
Found by fuzz wave 12f. Doc-only fix ssbal.go:10.

[w12f #30 fuzzstruct/GHNJYJ] Doc bug: the SsbalResult comment (ssbal.go:10) says Sys = (T⁻¹AT, T⁻¹B, CT, D), but the Ssbal function doc, the code (scaleRealization) and MATLAB ssbal all use (T·A/T, T·B, C/T). FuzzSsbal confirms the latter exactly. The struct comment should be fixed.

data.title: EDGE: AllMargin misses robust phase crossovers near lightly damped modes; realization-dependent
data.body:
Found by fuzz wave 12f. Crossovers robust under rounding (oracle). Cross-ref 42ZG7L, UFBPWZ, VT3OF7 (similar lightly-damped misses) - dedupe on fix.

[w12f #33 fuzzstruct/FUU523] EDGE: AllMargin and Margin miss a phase crossover at a lightly damped low-frequency pair when an exact double integrator and a stiff pole are present. Repro: TransferFunc num=[-4.969549555901367e-05 -136.49013836668794 -6930.639686355759 0.019408431409671963 -2.972934713546136e-06], den=[1 2e6 1.000000000001103e8 0.00859245157249671 0.08427408999794361 0 0], continuous, .StateSpace(). Poles: s^2, a pair at 2.9e-5 rad/s with zeta ~1.3e-6, and -50, -2e6. AllMargin returns PhaseCrossFreqs [] and Margin GM=+Inf. The exact oracle (componentwise-robust) has a phase crossover at w=2.9029824224235686e-05 with GM -190.46 dB; the phase offset is -180/+180 deg at w0*(1-/+1e-6). Same on amd64. Files: margin.go resonanceCrossings/phaseCrossings.

[w12f #35 fuzzstruct/FUU523] EDGE: AllMargin is realization-dependent for a feedthrough-dominated loop with a zeta=1e-7 mode and near-cancelled integrators. Repro: TransferFunc num=[-447.67661499638587 -0.27042549718475767 -4.083782716088854e9 -18.734339369971906 8.388141179041895e-12], den=[1 6.040586492872535e-4 9.12217118175434e6 -1.009712242922581e-5 -2.672975009877894e-18]. The companion realization (.StateSpace()) gives PhaseCrossFreqs [2702.46 3020.2886]. Applying any upper-shear similarity T=I+0.3*triu(ones) or larger gives []. The oracle requires 3020.2886362327736 (GM -53.02 dB; phase offset about 1e-6 deg either side, robust under rounding). Fuzz input: kind 0x84, vals=[-53.083808354550975 13 3.480049108858937 9 0 69 -0.2 -623 -58 19 47.37 98 -16 -10 -3.3333333333333335 -34]. File: margin.go phaseCrossings.

[w12f #44 fuzzstruct/review2] [controlsys, EDGE] AllMargin misses a phase crossover when the loop's realization is badly scaled, although it finds it on an equivalent well-conditioned realization. Repro: FuzzAllMargin kind=0xde vals=[-63 3 59.3 6.625 2 0.07142857142857142 1.4 -57.7 0 16 0.8 66.01 -104 -10 -1.6666666666666667 -60], channel (0,0): n=6, ‖A‖ about 7e5, poles -16966, -0.237±10000j, -0.589 and ~0, C ~ 1e-5, D = -56.6. In the exact rational evaluation the phase offset from -180 goes from +1.19e-6 deg at ω=10000.27 to -7.5e-6 deg at 10000.28. The realization rounding sensitivity there is about 5e-14 rad, so the crossover is robust. AllMargin(sys) returns PhaseCrossFreqs=[]; AllMargin(Ssbal(sys).Sys) also returns []. AllMargin(Canon(sys,CanonModal).Sys) returns [10000.2713, 18761.1] with GM -35.057 dB, matching the oracle. File: margin.go rationalLoop.phaseCrossings / polish / resonanceCrossings.

Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12). Race-build case (test now skips it under race): HinfNorm slow-resonance model decoded under -race build is 3e-10 low vs 1e-10 contract: fzSeed{N:3,M:1,P:1,Mag:{-8,4},Damp:{2.5,1},Shear:-10,Rot:0.37,no delays} in TestHinfNorm_BadlyScaledIOMatchesExactOracle (norms_test.go). Re-enable under race once fixed. Common suspects: norms.go certifyPeak treating sub-probe candidates as no crossing, hasImagEigs nearAxisTol on stiff unbalanced pencils (Dggbal before Dggev), peak search missing narrow humps, sigmaEvaluator over-report.

[w12 #68 linalg/LASTBLOCK] The new test TestHinfNorm_BadlyScaledIOMatchesExactOracle (norms_test.go, 5YUZIK) fails under -race, which CI runs. It is deterministic and does not skip when raceEnabled.
`go test -race -count=2 -run TestHinfNorm_BadlyScaledIOMatchesExactOracle .` on fed3cf1 (arm64) fails both times: "norms_test.go:2044: slow resonance: HinfNorm = 239.388723153999, oracle 239.388723226662 (rel -3.04e-10)". assertHinfNormMatchesOracle allows 1e-10 relative (norms_test.go:1854). Without -race it passes on arm64 and on amd64. In the race build fzDecode produces slightly different A data, and on that model the norm is 3e-10 low, against a documented accuracy of 1e-10. Base is 30% low on the same model, so this is a CI test failure, not a value regression. Fix: either reach 1e-10 on that data, or skip/loosen only under raceEnabled.

[w12 #74 fuzz/XQYP43] HinfNorm/Norm(Inf) under-reports a lightly damped discrete peak near z=1 by about 3.6e-4 relative, although norms.go peakGain documents certification to 1e-10. The result is still within MATLAB's default 1e-2 tolerance, so parity holds; the library's own claim is what's breached. Repro: NewFromSlices(2,1,1, A=[0.9999999959758767 5.3457259458380696e-09 -1.3269470226717082e-08 0.9999999927772968], B=[-0.6656134553337595 0.5410494509487578], C=[-999097.8260547261 363185.4084160624], D=[-736.7935074839925], dt=1e-4). HinfNorm gives 9.467722253631506e13 at ω=8.685e-5; the exact rational response gives 9.471110502171495e13 at ω=8.8388e-5. A naive float LU sweep agrees with the exact value to 1e-15, and the backward-error sensitivity is about 1e-7, so this is a search or certification miss, not conditioning. The exact γ-crossing test confirms a crossing at norm·(1+1e-6). Fuzz tuple: FuzzHinfNorm kind=0x41 vals=[-4 2.25 0.5 -145 -26 18 34 5629.5 -8 -0.3 1.1 32 1044 -0.5 0.2 -10]. The MIMO variant kind=0x5b with the same vals is also low by 3.6e-4. Suspect: norms.go peakGain/certifyPeak/upperBound. The rule 'candidates whose evaluated gains stay below the probe count as no crossing' probably certifies falsely when the candidate ω is off the true peak (2.5% off here).

[w12 #78 fuzz/review0] HinfNorm/linfNorm under-reports the peak gain of a stable, stiff, symmetric continuous SISO model by 2.1e-4 relative. This is present at base 2e4a07d (the base FuzzHinfNorm fails on the same input). Repro: put a corpus file `go test fuzz v1` / byte('À') / float64 vals 39,0,0.3,0,-0.2,0,0,0,0,-9.5,2.5,-76,-10,-10,-10,-10 into testdata/fuzz/FuzzHinfNorm/x, then run `go test -run FuzzHinfNorm/x .`. The decoded model has n=6, m=p=1, D=0, condT=1 (symmetric A, ‖A‖≈2e6) and stable eigenvalues {-0.00316, -0.00998, -50, -126, -399, -2e6}. HinfNorm returns 4.865840926965868e-05 at ω=0.003992. The exact big.Rat σmax at ω=0.0038510 is 4.86684164441442e-05. The expected error bound is fzNormTol ≈ 1e-6, so the peak search misses a low-frequency hump between the two slow poles. Files: hinfnorm.go (HinfNorm/linfNorm peak search). Evidence: hinfnorm_fuzz_test.go:78 fails on base and :50 on the branch; norms_fuzz_test.go:113 also fails.

[w12 #80 fuzz/review1] Pre-existing, outside the task scope: certifyPeak accepts candidates whose evaluated σ is below the probe as 'no crossing'. On undecidable lightly damped models (ζ≤1e-7) this certifies values up to 2e-6 below the exact σmax of the float64 model. Repro: sweep #1261 (kind=254, n=6, m=p=3, poles -4.65e-10±9.1206258e-4i). Branch HinfNorm 10322113722.95 at ω=9.1206258284e-4, while fzExactResponse at ω=9.1206258415e-4 gives 10322135171.8. Files: norms.go certifyPeak/candidatePeak. Conditioning is ~551, so this may be acceptable; filing is optional.

[w12 #77 fuzz/review] The norms.go change touches the library under-report the reviewer already filed (FuzzLinfNorm/FuzzHinfNorm, kind=0xc0 crasher). Climbing the sampled peak fixes the case where the true peak lies next to a grid sample. It does not fix the root cause: on stiff models (pole spread around 1e9), unstructured QZ in hamiltonianWS.hasImagEigs can still push genuine γ-crossings outside nearAxisTol=0.1. In norms.go hasImagEigs, the pencil eigenvalues at γ=4.8668e-5 for this model came out as (-5.0e-4+3.88e-3i)/0.9998, a ratio of 0.13. So a narrow peak between grid samples on a stiff model could still be under-reported. Possible fixes: balance the pencil (Dggbal 'B') before Dggev, or scale nearAxisTol to the eigenvalue condition. No concrete repro beyond the fixed crasher yet; the 5-minute fuzz runs found none.

[w12 #66 linalg/review0] HinfNorm reports a norm 3e-8 to 9e-8 above the exact σ_max at its own returned ω, and above a dense exact sweep, on high-gain models. The doc promises 1e-10. This happens on both base 2e4a07d and the branch, on arm64 and amd64. Repro: s := fzDecode(t, 0xa1, [16]float64{-4.840958682425959, 5.75742924209089, -4.840958682425959, 5.75742924209089, -4.974373469618411, 0.8119640876303578, -5, 1e-06, -0.6935062785976278, -9.308799076568224, 0.871442593513744, 9.362982810868214, -10, -10, -10, -10}); HinfNorm(s.System(t, fzSysOpts{})) = 154118350.60 at ω=1.44225e-5. fzExactResponse σ_max there is 154118336.72 (rel +9.0e-8), and the fzSweepMax exact peak is 154118336.724. Second instance: kind 0xc9 vals {0.6413769500533629, 3.225485305446771, -6.920211238942823, 5.194656803421655, 2.5649118927522707, 5.9960354875740425, 0.7321123327177131, 0, 0.8225408446783429, -8.084719954920434, -0.12421061853394999, -14.98391252021944, -10, -10, -10, -10} gives 10252.94430 vs exact 10252.94379 (+5e-8). Files: norms.go sigmaEvaluator / certifyPeak.


Fuzz wave 12f reports folded in:

[w12f #17] [CORE-ish] HinfNorm misses the true peak of a well-damped closed loop by 1.05e-4 relative, so HinfSyn returns Gamma below ‖CL‖∞. Exact evaluation shows the returned controller does not meet GammaOpt: exact σmax at ω=0.6408720941 is 1641555.339, while HinfNorm gives 1641383.506 at ω=4.8269, and GammaOpt = 1.64138e6. The minimum CL pole damping is 0.0074, so this is not the lightly-damped (ζ ≤ 1e-7) certifyPeak case already filed. σmax is near-flat, as expected for an H∞-optimal loop, and HinfNorm picks the wrong local maximum. This breaches the 1e-10 accuracy documented in norms.go/hinfsyn.go; it is within MATLAB's default 1e-2 tolerance, so parity holds. Repro: s := syNormC(fzDecode(t, 0xd2, [16]float64{0, 68, -0.2, 8.75, 0.4, -1.2, 7, -126.95714285714286, -3.5, -0.2333333333333333, -1.4, -55, 3, 148, 1, -63})); P,_,_ := syRegPlant(s); res,_ := HinfSyn(P.System(t,s), P.ny, P.nu). Then compare HinfNorm(res.CL) with fzExactResponse of res.CL at ω≈0.64087. Second case: kind=0xf4 vals=[0 68 -0.2 80.5 0.4 -1.2 7 -37.957142857142856 -0.5 -0.0875 50.6 158 3 54 1 29] gives 6.4e-6 under (207130.600 exact vs 207129.275), damping 0.0099. Both fail FuzzHinfSyn at synth_fuzz_test.go:1111. Files: norms.go (HinfNorm peak search), hinfsyn.go meets(). It may share a root cause with the filed HinfNorm under-report followups, so the coordinator should dedupe.

[w12f #32] CORE (low severity: documented accuracy violated): HinfNorm returns the high-frequency feedthrough level |D| at omega=+Inf, missing a slightly higher finite peak. Repro: NewFromSlices(2,1,1,A=[-2491.804346703939 15862.372233861133; -8932.767713905962 -8758.80383000371], B=[-0.013738160475694785; -0.005141010807114001], C=[-8479.999973995311 -7587.562358106949], D=-0.013822158423630349, 0). HinfNorm gives 0.013822158424321457 at +Inf. The exact rational response (fzExactResponse) at omega=268410.8133529991 is 0.013822180711973324, which is 1.61e-6 higher in relative terms; norms.go documents 1e-10 accuracy. Same on arm64 and amd64. This system is the sensitivity S of a FuzzDiskMargin crasher (testdata/fuzz/FuzzDiskMargin/a6ad2474856f46a7), so DiskMargin's PeakSensitivity and PeakFreq are off the same way. Simple bumps such as 1+eps*w*s/(s^2+0.5ws+w^2) are fine down to eps=1e-8; the failure is a broad peak that approaches |D| from above as omega goes to infinity. File: norms.go HinfNorm.

Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12). DCGain disagrees with FreqResponse(0) and the exact rational oracle when the DC solve is near-singular: absolute coefficient floors drop tiny B, transfer-limit path returns neither Inf nor the exact value, MIMO near-DC poles, and an exactly singular dense block missed by dcGainByBlockLaurent. All pre-existing on base 2e4a07d.

[w12 #16 freq/review1] DCGain returns a finite value at a reachable, observable continuous integrator (MATLAB gives Inf). Repro: sys := &System{A: [[0,0],[1,-1.3258457598967608e-08]], B: [7.29653485561532e-14; 1.0337733234010072e-13], C: [0 1], D: [0]} (continuous). DCGain gives 7.797085843999098e-06/nil; FreqResponse(0) gives +Inf. G(s) = (1.03e-13 s + 7.30e-14)/(s(s+1.33e-8)), so G(0) = Inf. The value equals B2/1.3258e-8, i.e. B1 was dropped as zero. The likely cause is the absolute coefficient floor in dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit or dcGainByStructuralEntries for tiny B (response.go). The branch gives the same result as base 2e4a07d. The sweep found 13 more TF.StateSpace realizations with a trailing-zero den (exact pole at s=0) where DCGain returns 0 and FR(0) returns +Inf.

[w12 #17 freq/review1] DCGain returns a finite value with the wrong sign and magnitude when the transfer limit is reached with a computed pole near DC. Repro (continuous companion): A row0 = -[6.325495602920146 12.427798551146598 7.785922515524618 2.9590313755032033e-05 2.830045401741772e-11 5.223977207934464e-19], subdiagonal ones, B=e1, C=[-0.1661821972150368 0.6204228877798674 1.5965704467083484 -0.2679049847206111 -0.17326373644234616 -0.9184631132625503], D=0.18013697908513038. The A solve fails (cond 1.4e21) and poleSpacing near=true (pole -1.88e-8). DCGain returns +9.684e11. The exact big.Rat G(0) is -1.758e18, FreqResponse(0) is +Inf, and ddResponseInto gives the exact value. Correct answers would be Inf (pole at DC) or -1.76e18; 9.7e11 is neither. Files: response.go (dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit). Same result on base 2e4a07d.

[w12 #18 freq/review2] Pre-existing (identical on base and branch), DCGain wrong next to near-DC poles in MIMO state-space models: for 49 of 1400 sweep models DCGain is +/-Inf or off while FreqResponse(0) matches the exact oracle. Example dc9: a continuous upper-triangular A with diagonal entries -2.89e-5, -3.09e-11, -1.75e-5, ... gives DCGain [-Inf, -78626.6], while FreqResponse(0) and the exact big.Rat solve give [-1.1129e18, -3.0967e18]. Another: discrete 2x2 A=[0.9998853776327908 0.0001224178710512369; -6.299779160740249e-05 1.000067282291557], B=[-0.7525840543357618 -1.8936563902987011; -0.3336326973535324 -0.8822404525470022], C=[-1.3323341784633906 -0.2326700817740477; 0.48991627788123343 0.8587983672300241], dt=0.01. Its DCGain is finite but has relative error 5e-5 against the exact value (789372732529716 vs 789410222466333), and FreqResponse(0) is +Inf in every entry. Files: response.go (DCGain explicit solve / dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit), frequency_pole.go. Oracle: exact rational solve of C(s0 I-A)^-1 B+D.

[w12 #41 dcgain/review1] DCGain finite for an exactly singular dense block with no 1x1 exact pole (pre-existing, same on base 2e4a07d and branch). Repro: NewFromSlices(3,2,2, A=[0.38629023905802873 3.851534645926291 -3.23782488498432; 0 4 -3; 4 1.6251019182011088 -4.625101918201109], B=[-0.5 0; -1.75 0; 0 0], C=[-1 -2.176206339653932 1; 0 -0.06848213510526557 0], D=[5.737696031494993 0; 0.75 0], dt=0.1). DCGain[1,0] = 6.73e13; exact rational limit on the float model is +Inf (det(I-A) = 0 exactly, exact pole order 1, computed eigenvalue 2e-15 from 1). The value comes from dcGainByStructuralEntries. dcGainByBlockLaurent declines because it needs a 1x1 block with A_kk == x0, although the branch's exactDetIsZero could detect this block. Files: response.go dcGainByStructuralEntries / dcGainByBlockLaurent.


Fuzz wave 12f reports folded in:

[w12f #31] CORE: DCGain returns a finite value for an exact integrator, so Bandwidth returns +Inf, nil instead of ErrInvalidArgument. Repro: NewFromSlices(2,1,1,A=[-1000 10; 0 0], b=[1;1], c=[1 1], d=0). Exact residue at s=0 is 1.01, so the DC gain is infinite (MATLAB dcgain gives Inf). DCGain returns -3.47e13 and Bandwidth(sys,-3) returns +Inf with nil error, on both arm64 and GOARCH=amd64. A sweep of A=[a k; 0 0], b=c=[1 1], with a in {-1..-1e3, 7, 250, 2.5e4} and k in {10..1e6}: 23/90 wrong on arm64, 18/90 on amd64, some with the wrong sign. Other wrong cases: [-250 1e4], [250 33000], [25000 1e6]. Likely cause: response.go DCGain uses X.Solve(A,B) on an exactly singular A and only falls back to dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit when Solve errors. Files: response.go:422-434, margin.go bandwidth(). FuzzBandwidth found this via a 4-integrator realization (now skipped as 'exact DC 0/inf beside an integrator cluster').

Repro (base 8015ead and fix/margins-wave5 a4aa6a2, identical): AllMargin of tf(-2, [1 0 0 0 0 0], Dt=1) (= -2 z^-5, also with InputDelay=5 on tf(-2,1,1)) returns PhaseCrossFreqs [1.2566] only.
Oracle: -2 e^{-5jθ} is real negative at θ = 2πm/5, so phase crossovers at 1.2566 and 2.5133 (GM -6.02 dB each); MATLAB allmargin lists both.
Also -2 z^-4 misses π (Nyquist), -2 z^-6 misses 2π/3, -2 z^-8 misses π/2 and π. Seeded sweep: -116.75 z^-5, Dt=0.79 misses 3.182.

So the tiny-B goal needs a mechanism that does not amplify noise columns, for example scaling only on raw user B, or an absolute floor that scales with the same factor.

TransferFunction regressed on models with ‖C‖≫‖A‖: the order rises and the denominator gains a nearly cancelled unstable pole (tfunst 0->1+ in 13/2400 sweep cases, all with C scaled by about 1e2-1e4). The 2531f51 row-stage floor max(n²,10n)·eps·‖A_stair‖_F (70·eps·‖A‖ at n=7) is about 2-3x below the noise left on structurally zero Hessenberg subdiagonals, which is 100-200·eps·‖A‖ on rotated models. Owner may downgrade this to informational: base was right only because its floor included ‖c‖, so it was not scale-robust.
Sweep case seed13/id55: continuous, n=7 (core 3, 2 uncontrollable, 2 unobservable, hidden blocks unstable), random orthogonal similarity, m=p=1, ‖A‖₂=6.03, ‖C‖=424. Base TF order 3, den [1 5.779 9.499 3.966] (stable, matches EvalFr). Branch TF order 5, den [1 7.2975 17.6727 14.9169 0.3165 -2.3821] with a positive real root, response error 1.9e-14. ObservabilityTol 1e-13 gives 5 and 3e-13 gives 3; it stays 3 up to 1e-6, so the gap is clear. Scaling C by 2^k: the branch gives 5 for every k in [-40,40]; base gives 5 for k≤-5, 3 for k in [0,20] and 2 at k=40. Other ids: 138 (6->10), 420, 507, 862, 880, 1297, 1575, 2127, 2157, 2166, 2210, 2335.

65BPNH (one rank rule; rounding-noise SVs must not count as rank): not met for Reduce's observability stage and for CtrbF/ObsvF on a B/C column that is small through cancellation. The per-column pow2 scaling makes noise SVs count again (blocking item 1, repro case 1571, Cc SVs [0.104, 1.07e-16] -> K=[2 1]). One rank rule fixing both directions is therefore not achieved: the tiny-B direction (PKUP2G/JBKTCQ) is bought by reopening the noise direction.

PKUP2G/65BPNH TF row stage: the scale-invariant subdiagonal floor (2531f51) is too tight for rotation noise of about 100-200·eps·‖A‖, so TF still counts noise subdiagonals and keeps hidden poles (blocking item 2). In the sweep, TF order is wrong in both base and branch in 502/2400 cases, mostly rotated models where the noise exceeds the floor.

Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12). Race-build case (test now skips it under race): HinfNorm slow-resonance model decoded under -race build is 3e-10 low vs 1e-10 contract: fzSeed{N:3,M:1,P:1,Mag:{-8,4},Damp:{2.5,1},Shear:-10,Rot:0.37,no delays} in TestHinfNorm_BadlyScaledIOMatchesExactOracle (norms_test.go). Re-enable under race once fixed. Common suspects: norms.go certifyPeak treating sub-probe candidates as no crossing, hasImagEigs nearAxisTol on stiff unbalanced pencils (Dggbal before Dggev), peak search missing narrow humps, sigmaEvaluator over-report.

[w12 #68 linalg/LASTBLOCK] The new test TestHinfNorm_BadlyScaledIOMatchesExactOracle (norms_test.go, 5YUZIK) fails under -race, which CI runs. It is deterministic and does not skip when raceEnabled.
`go test -race -count=2 -run TestHinfNorm_BadlyScaledIOMatchesExactOracle .` on fed3cf1 (arm64) fails both times: "norms_test.go:2044: slow resonance: HinfNorm = 239.388723153999, oracle 239.388723226662 (rel -3.04e-10)". assertHinfNormMatchesOracle allows 1e-10 relative (norms_test.go:1854). Without -race it passes on arm64 and on amd64. In the race build fzDecode produces slightly different A data, and on that model the norm is 3e-10 low, against a documented accuracy of 1e-10. Base is 30% low on the same model, so this is a CI test failure, not a value regression. Fix: either reach 1e-10 on that data, or skip/loosen only under raceEnabled.

[w12 #74 fuzz/XQYP43] HinfNorm/Norm(Inf) under-reports a lightly damped discrete peak near z=1 by about 3.6e-4 relative, although norms.go peakGain documents certification to 1e-10. The result is still within MATLAB's default 1e-2 tolerance, so parity holds; the library's own claim is what's breached. Repro: NewFromSlices(2,1,1, A=[0.9999999959758767 5.3457259458380696e-09 -1.3269470226717082e-08 0.9999999927772968], B=[-0.6656134553337595 0.5410494509487578], C=[-999097.8260547261 363185.4084160624], D=[-736.7935074839925], dt=1e-4). HinfNorm gives 9.467722253631506e13 at ω=8.685e-5; the exact rational response gives 9.471110502171495e13 at ω=8.8388e-5. A naive float LU sweep agrees with the exact value to 1e-15, and the backward-error sensitivity is about 1e-7, so this is a search or certification miss, not conditioning. The exact γ-crossing test confirms a crossing at norm·(1+1e-6). Fuzz tuple: FuzzHinfNorm kind=0x41 vals=[-4 2.25 0.5 -145 -26 18 34 5629.5 -8 -0.3 1.1 32 1044 -0.5 0.2 -10]. The MIMO variant kind=0x5b with the same vals is also low by 3.6e-4. Suspect: norms.go peakGain/certifyPeak/upperBound. The rule 'candidates whose evaluated gains stay below the probe count as no crossing' probably certifies falsely when the candidate ω is off the true peak (2.5% off here).

[w12 #78 fuzz/review0] HinfNorm/linfNorm under-reports the peak gain of a stable, stiff, symmetric continuous SISO model by 2.1e-4 relative. This is present at base 2e4a07d (the base FuzzHinfNorm fails on the same input). Repro: put a corpus file `go test fuzz v1` / byte('À') / float64 vals 39,0,0.3,0,-0.2,0,0,0,0,-9.5,2.5,-76,-10,-10,-10,-10 into testdata/fuzz/FuzzHinfNorm/x, then run `go test -run FuzzHinfNorm/x .`. The decoded model has n=6, m=p=1, D=0, condT=1 (symmetric A, ‖A‖≈2e6) and stable eigenvalues {-0.00316, -0.00998, -50, -126, -399, -2e6}. HinfNorm returns 4.865840926965868e-05 at ω=0.003992. The exact big.Rat σmax at ω=0.0038510 is 4.86684164441442e-05. The expected error bound is fzNormTol ≈ 1e-6, so the peak search misses a low-frequency hump between the two slow poles. Files: hinfnorm.go (HinfNorm/linfNorm peak search). Evidence: hinfnorm_fuzz_test.go:78 fails on base and :50 on the branch; norms_fuzz_test.go:113 also fails.

[w12 #80 fuzz/review1] Pre-existing, outside the task scope: certifyPeak accepts candidates whose evaluated σ is below the probe as 'no crossing'. On undecidable lightly damped models (ζ≤1e-7) this certifies values up to 2e-6 below the exact σmax of the float64 model. Repro: sweep #1261 (kind=254, n=6, m=p=3, poles -4.65e-10±9.1206258e-4i). Branch HinfNorm 10322113722.95 at ω=9.1206258284e-4, while fzExactResponse at ω=9.1206258415e-4 gives 10322135171.8. Files: norms.go certifyPeak/candidatePeak. Conditioning is ~551, so this may be acceptable; filing is optional.

[w12 #77 fuzz/review] The norms.go change touches the library under-report the reviewer already filed (FuzzLinfNorm/FuzzHinfNorm, kind=0xc0 crasher). Climbing the sampled peak fixes the case where the true peak lies next to a grid sample. It does not fix the root cause: on stiff models (pole spread around 1e9), unstructured QZ in hamiltonianWS.hasImagEigs can still push genuine γ-crossings outside nearAxisTol=0.1. In norms.go hasImagEigs, the pencil eigenvalues at γ=4.8668e-5 for this model came out as (-5.0e-4+3.88e-3i)/0.9998, a ratio of 0.13. So a narrow peak between grid samples on a stiff model could still be under-reported. Possible fixes: balance the pencil (Dggbal 'B') before Dggev, or scale nearAxisTol to the eigenvalue condition. No concrete repro beyond the fixed crasher yet; the 5-minute fuzz runs found none.

[w12 #66 linalg/review0] HinfNorm reports a norm 3e-8 to 9e-8 above the exact σ_max at its own returned ω, and above a dense exact sweep, on high-gain models. The doc promises 1e-10. This happens on both base 2e4a07d and the branch, on arm64 and amd64. Repro: s := fzDecode(t, 0xa1, [16]float64{-4.840958682425959, 5.75742924209089, -4.840958682425959, 5.75742924209089, -4.974373469618411, 0.8119640876303578, -5, 1e-06, -0.6935062785976278, -9.308799076568224, 0.871442593513744, 9.362982810868214, -10, -10, -10, -10}); HinfNorm(s.System(t, fzSysOpts{})) = 154118350.60 at ω=1.44225e-5. fzExactResponse σ_max there is 154118336.72 (rel +9.0e-8), and the fzSweepMax exact peak is 154118336.724. Second instance: kind 0xc9 vals {0.6413769500533629, 3.225485305446771, -6.920211238942823, 5.194656803421655, 2.5649118927522707, 5.9960354875740425, 0.7321123327177131, 0, 0.8225408446783429, -8.084719954920434, -0.12421061853394999, -14.98391252021944, -10, -10, -10, -10} gives 10252.94430 vs exact 10252.94379 (+5e-8). Files: norms.go sigmaEvaluator / certifyPeak.


Fuzz wave 12f reports folded in:

[w12f #17] [CORE-ish] HinfNorm misses the true peak of a well-damped closed loop by 1.05e-4 relative, so HinfSyn returns Gamma below ‖CL‖∞. Exact evaluation shows the returned controller does not meet GammaOpt: exact σmax at ω=0.6408720941 is 1641555.339, while HinfNorm gives 1641383.506 at ω=4.8269, and GammaOpt = 1.64138e6. The minimum CL pole damping is 0.0074, so this is not the lightly-damped (ζ ≤ 1e-7) certifyPeak case already filed. σmax is near-flat, as expected for an H∞-optimal loop, and HinfNorm picks the wrong local maximum. This breaches the 1e-10 accuracy documented in norms.go/hinfsyn.go; it is within MATLAB's default 1e-2 tolerance, so parity holds. Repro: s := syNormC(fzDecode(t, 0xd2, [16]float64{0, 68, -0.2, 8.75, 0.4, -1.2, 7, -126.95714285714286, -3.5, -0.2333333333333333, -1.4, -55, 3, 148, 1, -63})); P,_,_ := syRegPlant(s); res,_ := HinfSyn(P.System(t,s), P.ny, P.nu). Then compare HinfNorm(res.CL) with fzExactResponse of res.CL at ω≈0.64087. Second case: kind=0xf4 vals=[0 68 -0.2 80.5 0.4 -1.2 7 -37.957142857142856 -0.5 -0.0875 50.6 158 3 54 1 29] gives 6.4e-6 under (207130.600 exact vs 207129.275), damping 0.0099. Both fail FuzzHinfSyn at synth_fuzz_test.go:1111. Files: norms.go (HinfNorm peak search), hinfsyn.go meets(). It may share a root cause with the filed HinfNorm under-report followups, so the coordinator should dedupe.

[w12f #32] CORE (low severity: documented accuracy violated): HinfNorm returns the high-frequency feedthrough level |D| at omega=+Inf, missing a slightly higher finite peak. Repro: NewFromSlices(2,1,1,A=[-2491.804346703939 15862.372233861133; -8932.767713905962 -8758.80383000371], B=[-0.013738160475694785; -0.005141010807114001], C=[-8479.999973995311 -7587.562358106949], D=-0.013822158423630349, 0). HinfNorm gives 0.013822158424321457 at +Inf. The exact rational response (fzExactResponse) at omega=268410.8133529991 is 0.013822180711973324, which is 1.61e-6 higher in relative terms; norms.go documents 1e-10 accuracy. Same on arm64 and amd64. This system is the sensitivity S of a FuzzDiskMargin crasher (testdata/fuzz/FuzzDiskMargin/a6ad2474856f46a7), so DiskMargin's PeakSensitivity and PeakFreq are off the same way. Simple bumps such as 1+eps*w*s/(s^2+0.5ws+w^2) are fine down to eps=1e-8; the failure is a broad peak that approaches |D| from above as omega goes to infinity. File: norms.go HinfNorm.


Wave 13 attempt (HinfNorm commits 8dd9a00 ea9c423 on fix/normszeros-wave13; the Zeros commits were merged) NOT merged; final review findings:

[XK2GY2] HinfNorm value regressions vs 690c75a. On HinfSyn closed loops near the w12f#17 repro seeds, base is within 1e-10 of the exact peak and the branch under-reports by 2e-7 to 3e-6. Results are deterministic: an 800/800 rerun gave identical values. 4 to 6 of 800 cases regress, and the regressing set changes with platform: arm64 has 589, 593, 725 and 479, amd64 has 142 and 203. That breaks the requirement that results be robust to platform rounding, and it shows the near-top-sample refinement is fragile. Against that, the branch fixes about 380 of these 800 that base gets wrong.
Oracle: exactSigmaMax (high-precision response) evaluated at base's own returned omega, plus oraclePeakGain. Repro: s := syNormC(fzDecode(t, kind, vals)); P,_,_ := syRegPlant(s); res,_ := HinfSyn(P.System(t,s), P.ny, P.nu); then compare HinfNorm(res.CL) with exactSigmaMax(res.CL, w_base).
(a) arm64, CL built and evaluated on the branch tree: kind=0xf4 vals=[0.18349609056653815 70.02594970793999 -0.2 80.5 0.4 -1.4081301978376826 6.786926955408581 -37.957142857142856 -0.5 -0.0875 50.6 155.906837811452 3 54 1 29]. Branch HinfNorm = 129251.81386735462 at w=1.518870; base = 129251.87196016147 at w=0.639697, and the exact sigma there matches to 4.7e-11. Branch is 4.49e-7 low.
(b) arm64, CL built with the 690c75a HinfSyn: kind=0xf4 vals=[-0.2522184515726155 68 -0.2 79.57938094308341 0.4 -1.2 6.7804395187608195 -37.957142857142856 -0.5 -0.0875 50.6 158 3 54 1 29]. Branch 207637.1936801683 at w=0.55925; base 207637.26946871637 at w=0.647367 (exact +5e-11). Branch is 3.65e-7 low.
(c) Same family under GOARCH=amd64: kind=0xd2 vals=[-0.2475394537283681 67.43328299628585 -0.2 8.914263152790271 0.2991543196013393 -1.2 7 -126.95714285714286 -3.4051424800440846 -0.2333333333333333 -1.5572154376874732 -55 3 148 1 -63]. Branch 1619041.1002122518 at w=0.570518; base 1619045.7560809054 at w=0.641005. Branch is 2.88e-6 low.
(d) amd64: kind=0xf4 vals=[-0.021343084004861467 68 -0.2 80.5 0.4 -1.2 6.9599220858052275 -37.957142857142856 -0.28228331591394096 -0.04253829221573548 50.6 156.14386341589463 3 54 1 29]. Branch 167462.8438022881 at w=0.606903; base 167462.9380114957 at w=0.959895. Branch is 5.63e-7 low.
Other arm64 regressions: kind=0xf4 vals=[-0.27770605200913423 68 -0.2 80.5 0.4 -1.1564613977302485 7 -38.058403255272914 -0.5 -0.0875 49.37591907386475 154.82285204002307 3 54 1 29], branch 2.21e-7 low; and vals=[0 66.29110017916157 -0.3833723365061832 80.5 0.4 -1.2 6.870613820583085 -37.957142857142856 -0.3307326129810297 -0.0875 50.6 158 3 54 1 29], branch 2.97e-7 low where base was 5.4e-10 off.
In every case the branch returns a lower local hump: at its own omega it is within 5e-11 of the exact sigma, but not at the global peak.

[XK2GY2] The documented 1e-10 accuracy is still not met on the targeted flat HinfSyn closed-loop family. I perturbed the 0xd2/0xf4 w12f#17 seeds 800 times. The branch still misses 1e-10 on 19 to 21 of 800 (base misses 352 to 404). The worst miss is -2.17e-5, on kind=0xd2 vals=[0 68 -0.2 8.990234452886758 0.4 -1.2 6.850514126121088 -126.95714285714286 -3.5 -0.2333333333333333 -1.4 -55 3 148 1 -63], CL built with the 690c75a HinfSyn: branch 1645353.773231371 at w=0.64597. Another is -2.34e-6 on kind=0xf4 vals=[0 68 0.08412681363029778 80.5 0.4 -0.9367143783484548 7 -37.957142857142856 -0.5 -0.0875 51.34440318432133 162.02540765613801 3 54 1 29], where base has the same miss. Most of these misses are shared with base; the cause is that HinfNorm picks the wrong local hump on near-flat sigma_max curves. The five frozen CL tests and the fuzz-finding tests do pass, and the -race slow-resonance case is re-enabled and passes.

data.title: DECISION: TunePID |S|<=4 / 58.5deg PM bar for undelayed first designs (PD |S| 17 near z=1)
data.body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13). tuneAt(wc0,...,robust=false) bounds |S| only with delay; V2AYQB exposes it on near-unit plants. Owner: apply Pidtune bar to TunePID all families?

[w13 #4 pidtune/V2AYQB] TunePID: an undelayed first-pass design has no |S| bound. Repro: dt 0.01, num 10*{2.761969998249568e-16, 2.6332895798497864e-16, 6.196985260193668e-17}, den {1,-5.388323209156541,12.045405202918547,-14.292531743733242,9.488502158799133,-3.339413745774066,0.486361336946173}; TunePID PD with PIDTuningOptions{} returns Kp 0.5639 and Kd -1.667e5, PM 63, with oracle |S| 16.9 inside the reported band (17.04 at 7.7e-4 rad/s with the plant evaluated in 256-bit). Pidtune PD on the same plant gives Kp 0.9985, Kd 1.009e4, Tf 1010. Cause: tuneAt(wc0, gainSign, tau > 0, false) only bounds |S| when the plant has a delay (pid_tuning.go TunePID default path). Base returned an error on this plant, so this is a new value of low robustness, not a regression of a correct value.

[w13 #6 pidtune/V2AYQB] Observation, not a bug: TunePID free I or free P accepts the plant's margin at wc0 when |S| <= 4, as documented. The IP3XIC k=10 plant (above) with I returns PM 28.7 deg and |S| 2.24; GK5SUC A with P returns 45.7 deg, same on base. The coordinator should decide whether the owner's 58.5 deg bar applies to TunePID as well as Pidtune.

[w13 #8 pidtune/review2] Title: TunePID PD can return |S| 17 inside its own analysis band on near-z=1 plants (pre-existing: the first design at wc0 is not |S|-bounded for undelayed plants). Repro: num {2.761969998249568e-15, 2.6332895798497864e-15, 6.196985260193668e-16}, den {1,-5.388323209156541,12.045405202918547,-14.292531743733242,9.488502158799133,-3.339413745774066,0.486361336946173}, Dt 0.01, StateSpace(), then TunePID(ctx, sys, PidtunePD, PIDTuningOptions{}). It returns Kp 0.5639, Kd -166694 (gains of opposite sign, since gainSign is 0 once the integrator is recognised) at PM 63 deg. The |S| peak is 17.0 at w=7.7e-4, inside FrequencyBand [4.95e-8, 4.95e-4 x...] (in-band peak 16.9); stability is exact Schur-stable. A second case, nearunit plant num {-5.917373360562065e-16,-3.1176768703785916e-16}, den {1,-3.9985941793495767,5.995783163531163,-3.99578378890103,0.9985948047194504}, Dt 0.01, PD: |S| 6.31 in band. Base also returns |S|>4 TunePID PD/PDF/PIDF designs on ordinary plants. Cause: pid_tuning.go TunePID calls tuneAt(wc0, gainSign, tau > 0, false), so robust is false without a delay. V2AYQB now exposes this on near-unit plants, and its test only checks |S| for P/I. Owner call whether TunePID should bound |S| <= pidTuningMaxSensitivity for all families. Files: pid_tuning.go (TunePID tuneAt robust flag), pid_tuning_fallback_test.go.

data.title: CORE: TunePID certifies unstable designs as closed-loop-poles stable (pidTuningIdealStable)
data.body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13). Two paths: float Poly.Roots with no exact retest (#7), and collapsed TF from transfer() (#59, root cause in shift-chain TF task).

[w13 #7 pidtune/review1] Pre-existing (same gains on 690c75a and da18f22): TunePID returns an unstable mixed-sign PID and certifies it as closed-loop-poles stable. Repro: dt 0.01, num [2.761969998249568e-16 2.6332895798497864e-16 6.196985260193668e-17], den [1 -5.388323209156541 12.045405202918547 -14.292531743733242 9.488502158799133 -3.339413745774066 0.486361336946173] (IP3XIC k=1), TunePID(ctx, sys, PidtunePID, PIDTuningOptions{}). Result: Kp 105572.5, Ki -38.475, Kd 483.4, Tf 0, reported PM 62.1° at wc 0.0533, Stability closed-loop-poles. pidtuneExactSchurStable gives false. A negative Ki on a plant with DC gain +0.208 puts a real closed-loop root above z=1. File: pid_tuning.go, pidTuningIdealStable (float Poly.Roots only, no exact retest; the same root cause as the BLOCKING item).

[w13 #59 fuzz/QNALQV] CORE (downstream of the TransferFunction collapse): TunePID returns an unstable discrete PD while reporting Stability=closed-loop-poles. Repro: the plant above with a=3.720075976020836e-44, InputDelay 20 samples, Dt=100 (also Dt=1 and 0.1). TunePID(ctx, sys, PD, PIDTuningOptions{}) with the default ForwardEuler DFormula returns Tf=0, Kp=0.008945, Kd=9.7288 (Dt=100). Exact Schur–Cohn finds 19 roots with |z|>1. Float Poly.Roots of the characteristic polynomial gives max|root| 1.129. The ideal-derivative screen in pid_tuning.go (closedLoopPoles -> pidTuningIdealStable -> s.transfer()) uses the collapsed TF. Corpus: testdata/fuzz/FuzzTunePID/e69a3565ab5664af; gated in fzPidCheckTune.

data.title: CORE: S2RNHI remainder: AllMargin/Margin miss phase crossovers beside z=1 cluster
data.body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13). S2RNHI partly fixed in wave 13; 123/2000 cluster-family sweep cases still miss (base 167).

[w13 #14 margins/review] S2RNHI residual (known limit, not fixed): a phase crossing far below the first pencil root is still missed beside a z=1 cluster. Repro: dt=0.01, num [2.8120621156929326e-07 3.52296574605969e-07 8.824538827371326e-08], den [1 -4.99774725235864 9.990990156853018 -9.986486956145953 4.990992451167435 -0.9977483995158617]. The big.Float oracle has a crossing at w=0.014696823 (|L|=4.3e8, a sign change that holds over w(1±1e-4)). AllMargin reports [131.17, 314.16] and the first pencil root is 0.0888, more than w/2 away. Files: margin.go polish/wideBracket. 1 out of 698 oracle crossings in the sweep.

[w13 #18 margins/LASTINCOMPLETE] S2RNHI (AllMargin/Margin miss phase crossovers beside a z=1 cluster) is only partly fixed. In the seeded 2000-case sweep, the branch still misses at least one oracle phase crossing in 123 cluster-family cases (base: 167). FreqResponse agrees with big.Float to about 1e-15 at those crossings, and the phase-offset sign change there is robust, so these are not precision limits. Repro (dt=0.01, no delay): num [2.8357027642397935e-15 -2.5512293296672896e-15 1.7314681787761854e-16], den [1 -7.991403327904192 27.939842959360206 -55.81958786155226 69.69941139400636 -55.69950967106022 27.819764760250035 -7.93994123641546 0.991422983315524]. Base and branch both return AllMargin PhaseCrossFreqs [188.598902], GM [320.744 dB]. The big.Float oracle also finds a crossing at w=1.15248109 with |L|=0.1824 (GM 14.78 dB); phase offset is +0.033 deg at w(1-1e-3) and -0.033 deg at w(1+1e-3). So Margin reports 320.7 dB where the true GM is 14.8 dB: the same symptom as FI3ZIB. More repros: num [3.086531715571932e-05 4.748257100155147e-06 -1.6656262775276625e-06], den [1 -5.999572410897895 14.997861879983766 -19.995723410958078 14.995723061950578 -5.997861356472517 0.9995722363941447] misses w=0.167802713 (GM -210.4 dB). num [2.27310135283274e-06 -1.3781887605808078e-06], den [1 -6.995478220522176 20.972874243896655 -34.93219791120347 34.909613616290855 -20.932222512785664 6.972893925162413 -0.9954831408386168], 1-sample input delay, misses w=0.387276661 (GM -188.2 dB). data.title: EDGE: AllMargin misses phase crossings of delay-absorbed discrete loops (realCandidates)
data.body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13). Distinct from S2RNHI singular band; cross-ref YIWBXS (continuous lightly damped misses).

[w13 #9 margins/S2RNHI] AllMargin misses phase crossings after discrete delays are absorbed (margin.go realCandidates/boundaryRoots). Repro: num [1.1974308853542987e-16], den [1 -6.184746550403649 16.242438259051475 -23.437999081676736 20.022569140290482 -10.09289718715969 2.766371287397997 -0.31573586749987936], dt 0.01, SetInputDelay([]float64{3}). AllMargin gives PhaseCrossFreqs [0.1801 267.8]. A big-float oracle also has crossings at 14.73, 87.71 and 175.93 rad/s, with GM 218, 307 and 341 dB. realCandidates on the absorbed loop returns [0.1795 1.234 13.248 279.16], so two candidates are more than 10% off and two are missing. The double solve evaluates those frequencies correctly (L(14.73) = -1.2437513636616553e-11 + 3.98e-15i, matching the oracle). Margin itself is correct, since the missed crossings have larger GMs.

[w13 #17 margins/review0] AllMargin/Margin miss a phase crossover beside a cluster near z=1 with a 3-sample delay, even where at() resolves (a different mechanism from S2RNHI's singular band). Repro: dt=0.01, num [1.391607534896511e-15], den [1 -5.996928959245808 14.984645931608547 -19.969294133971424 14.969296404721078 -5.984649337733024 0.9969300946206339], SetInputDelay([3]). At w=2.25925, FreqResponse is real negative at -1.0409e-05, and its imaginary part changes sign across w(1±2%) (-6.4e-8i to +4.9e-8i). The crossing survives 20/20 one-ulp coefficient perturbations, and at(w) returns the same value with no error. AllMargin PhaseCrossFreqs is [104.76 314.16] and Margin GM is 297.14 dB, against the true minimum crossing of 99.65 dB at w=2.259. Second repro: num [8.41798900940185e-14], 9-pole den [1 -8.99977808507088 35.99822556730129 -83.99379258894939 125.98759138433863 -125.9844969880358 83.9876037961689 -35.993805000779744 8.998230886657213 -0.9997789716302142], delay 3; it misses w=20.958 (|L|=1.10e-7), and Margin reports 261.5 dB. data.title: EDGE: ReduceUnobservable/ReduceAll return rotated model when nothing removed (pole flips)
data.body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13). Extend 4a73116 unrotated-model fix. Low severity.

[w13 #25 tf/review0] ReduceUnobservable (and ReduceAll when ncont<n) returns an orthogonally rotated model even when the observability stage removes nothing. On stiff nonnormal models this can flip ill-conditioned eigenvalues: one sweep case had n=6, ‖A‖=1.3e6, orig poles {-1.48,-1.99,-3.71,-4.23,...}, and the reduced poles {+0.257, -2.85±2.66i, ...} at order 6 = n. It exists on base too; base was lucky on that seed. The ReduceAll unrotated-model fix (commit 4a73116) could be extended to ReduceUnobservable/ReduceAll with nobs==ncont. Files: minimal.go Reduce. Severity: low, a precision-limit-adjacent cosmetic issue, since the I/O response is correct to 1e-14.

data.title: CORE: Zeros staircase rank decisions drop/garble zeros (non-square, scaled; platform-dependent)
data.body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13). Base equally wrong; bar is to beat base. Add exact-oracle count/value check to FuzzZeros (w13 #36).

[w13 #31 normszeros/SFXMAD SPWBDX] Zeros: unscaled and balanced staircase both garbage on a strongly diagonally scaled SISO with input-decoupling zero (in scope, unfixed; base also wrong). Repro: New(A,B,C,D) with n=4,m=p=1, A=[1.968381171286278 0 0 0; -3.3056869914010242e+10 0.2739524212751154 -7.452505416638818e+08 31022.31595250236; -0.0036934119373775447 -1.3381648221105064e-10 -0.12073917927091736 -1.9491487586739942e-05; 13231.64100776368 3.787172142112033e-07 -269842.69014969293 5.551312281470159], B=[0;44.52009700657428;2.665485955874114e-10;-8.261839357512965e-06], C=[4.527433297075258e+06 0.0006283026295836041 -2.1217336804057643e+07 1063.924795326897], D=0. Exact zeros (det P(s) in big.Rat plus 400-bit Durand-Kerner): 1.968381171286278 (the decoupling zero A[0][0]) and 1.9775309995995483±7.747629119246556i, all with entrywise sensitivity of about 1e-16. Base and branch both return wrong or dropped values (relative error 1 to 7.7). Zeros is on the staircase path with no D, and Newton refinement cannot add a zero the staircase loses. File: zeros.go (mimoZeros / zerosStaircase rank decisions).

[w13 #34 normszeros/review] Title: Zeros drops all three zeros of the 1463 non-square model on amd64 (base and branch both wrong). Repro: GOARCH=amd64, NewFromSlices(3,2,3, A,B,C,D from review id 1463, 0).Zeros() returns []. The exact zeros are -7.648048437606871, -21.744896691779353 and -2.4645885181395255e7. arm64 returns all three. Files: /Users/josephj/workspace/controlsys/.claude/worktrees/wf_96b80c0f-c1e-47/zeros.go (zerosStaircase / zerosStaircasePass rank decisions). Evidence: the unscaled staircase decides at rank margin 1.23, so the result flips with platform rounding. The balanced staircase returns an empty pencil at margin 562 on both platforms. Base 690c75a behaves the same way, so this is not a regression. A sturdier reduction for non-square models with a dependent [C D] row and nearly singular D would be needed, for example squaring the system down and checking each candidate with the backward-error test. Base also keeps the zeros over only about half of the α=2^-12..2^12 range.

[w13 #37 normszeros/review1] Pre-existing (base 690c75a): on the same non-square models, base Zeros is scale-fragile and sometimes wrong. Rescaling B·α, C/α (exactly zero-preserving) changes the zero count. For id 1463 base returns 0 zeros for α ≤ 2^-2 and 3 zeros for α ≥ 1, and for 1706 the count varies 0/1/2 across α. Base also gives spurious or garbled huge zeros: 1225 returns a real 3.26e7 where the exact pair is 2.98e5±4.40e6i, and in 1706 the huge zero is 1.7e-2 off. The fix bar for the blocking item is to beat base, not just match it. File: zeros.go zerosStaircase rank decisions against svlmax.

data.title: EDGE: Zeros eig(A-BD^-1C) O(1) wrong at cond(D)~1e16; hybrid fallback blocked by rank mismatch
PERF: Zeros Newton refinement 16-25x slower on stiff n=150; Dare work arrays regrown per call
data.body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13). Owner deferred perf. Zeros slowdown introduced by SFXMAD/SPWBDX (wave 13).

[w13 #35 normszeros/review0] Zeros slowdown on stiff, large models (introduced by this branch, zeros.go refineZeros/eigZeros/mimoZeros). Repro: A = T*J*T^-1 with J = diag(-10^(6*(i/(n-1)-0.5))) plus 0.3*randn superdiagonal, T = I + 0.3*randn/sqrt(n); B, C randn; m=p=1 or 3; D=0 or randn. sys.Zeros() time at n=150 is 25-30ms at 690c75a and 420-640ms on the branch (16-25x); n=80 is 7-12x and n=30 3-7x. Bode with a default grid on such models calls Zeros. Suggest a cap or batching for the Newton refinement (only zeros whose a-priori error estimate is actually large, or a refinement budget).

[w13 #41 riccati/BU6YAP] Dare speed: always using the extended pencil (Dgges) costs +53% at N10 and +38% at N50, with B/op up 53–121% because the work arrays are regrown on each call. NewRiccatiWorkspace sizes work as nn*50, but the Dgges/Dormqr query needs more. Pre-sizing ws.work from the Dgges query in NewRiccatiWorkspace would remove the extra allocations. File: riccati.go. Optional performance follow-up, not a correctness issue.

data.title: CORE: Dare/Care lack (Q,S,R) cost scaling: tiny ||X|| loses digits, huge cost ErrNoStabilizing
data.body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13). GEEI33 remainder. Check MATLAB idare scaling. Tighten mqRiccatiSchurRelErr after.

[w13 #40 riccati/BU6YAP] Dare/Care lack cost (Q,S,R) scaling, so accuracy is poor when ||X|| is much smaller than the pencil scale. Repro: FuzzRiccati corpus testdata/fuzz/FuzzRiccati/04679c87ed2ffeaf (kind=0xf1 vals=[75.83972937520639 6 3.6132640614817766 6.3 0.652072438895929 6 0 -847 483 -1 -75.3 -166.8 -10.714285714285714 -10 -1 -36], Q=CᵀC about 8e-12, S=CᵀD, R=DᵀD+1e-3 about 1.8e6, n=6, discrete). Dare's X (||X|| about 2.65e-11) differs from the converged fixed-point Riccati iteration by 2.4e-6 relative. Scaling (Q,S,R) by 1e5 and then X by 1e-5 gives 6.9e-9, and scaling by 1e11 gives 6.1e-9. On amd64 min eig(X) is -7.9e-18 (PSD loss of 3e-7 relative). The failure is the same on base and after the fix, so it is not related to near-zero eigenvalues. Files: riccati.go, matrix_equation_problem.go (scale). The FuzzRiccati residual and PSD tolerances are now widened by eps·h/(sep·||X||) in mateq_fuzz_test.go (mqRiccatiSchurRelErr); tighten them once cost scaling lands. Check MATLAB idare's scaling for parity.

[w13 #50 riccati/review] Dare errors (ErrNoStabilizing) on very unstable discrete plants with large cost, while the same problem with Q and R scaled to about 1 solves (it agrees with Hewer to 4e-6). Lower priority: an edge case (spectral radius about 200, |X| about 1e21), and unlike the Care cases the existing firstSigma rescue does not recover it. Repro, case 2512 of my sweep: A=[-152.29727095303136 -3.178908107484922 109.29141049541496; 65.62325786891606 -208.39758308585283 95.78001298506533; 59.741237972781015 84.85712783054723 -55.99748748513992], B=[-1.144344154554384; -0.24792791425090677; 0.035774271468863125], Q=[147525.89105437972 63506.942984963636 -101057.13616960809; 63506.942984963636 65140.03799109538 -65279.613963969714; -101057.13616960809 -65279.613963969714 92959.81631299868], R=1.4275139706597782e6. Dare(A,B,Q,R,nil) returns ErrNoStabilizing; with Q and R multiplied by 2^-16 it solves. Two more cases in the same 4000-case sweep (Q, R about 1e7 to 1e10, ||A|| about 30 to 150) fail the same way. Files: riccati.go (pencilSolution, firstSigma).

data.title: CORE: Dare ill-conditioned R: extended pencil loses digits; residualTerms Inf on mat.Condition
data.body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13). #42 regressed vs 690c75a via 3b4de00 (BU6YAP). Fix hint: whiten inputs with ws.rChol.

[w13 #42 riccati/GEEI33] Dare extended pencil (3b4de00) loses digits when R is badly conditioned (R = D'D + eps*I with m > p), and Eig disagrees with trace(A-BK). Repro: go test -run 'FuzzRiccati/illcond_r_dare_(m3|cross)' (counted skip 'R ill-conditioned, extended pencil loses digits (known followup)'; drop the illR guard in mateq_fuzz_test.go to see the failures). Files: riccati.go (generalizedStableSubspace input-column QR, pencil mu balancing), testdata/fuzz/FuzzRiccati/illcond_r_dare_m3 and illcond_r_dare_cross. Evidence (300-bit Newton oracle): illcond_r_dare_m3 (kind 0x55, n=2, m=3, cond(R)=5.6e9) X relative error 1.1e-8 at 690c75a, 3.4e-6 at 95e7e75, 1.9e-7 now, against a 1-ulp perturbation change of 1.3e-15. illcond_r_dare_cross (kind 0x27, S=C'D, cond(R)=1.4e9, ||X||=1.8e-19): 9.5e-8 at 690c75a, 1.0 at 95e7e75, 2e-3 now, against 6e-7; Eig is off trace(A-BK) by 6e-6. Fix hint: whiten the inputs with the Cholesky factor already in ws.rChol (Btilde = B*U^-1, Stilde = S*U^-1, Rtilde = I). This is an equivalence transform, so X and the eigenvalues are unchanged (idare semantics kept), K = U^-1*Ktilde, and mu becomes ||Btilde||.

[w13 #49 riccati/review] riccati.go residualTerms returns Inf whenever mat.Solve reports a mat.Condition error, which gonum raises even though the result it computed is usable. With an ill-conditioned R+BᵀXB, a saved pass that was scored Inf loses every keepBest comparison against a later pass. The behaviour predates this branch and is left unfixed; the fix is to ignore mat.Condition there.

data.title: EDGE: Dare Eig disagrees with eig(A-BK) 1e-4 with unit-circle pair and Q~1e-12
data.body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13). May be fuzz trace-check tolerance (no sep term) rather than solver.

[w13 #47 riccati/review] Dare: Eig disagrees with eig(A−BK) by 3.5e-4 and 8.8e-4 when A has an eigenvalue pair exactly on the unit circle (c2d of ±i) plus a repeated unstable eigenvalue and Q≈1e-12. Repro: FuzzRiccati corpus bytes kind 0x9b vals [376 -63 11 -2 0 0 0 -79 -48 -10 0.37 0 100 50 -20 -10], and kind 0x93 vals [0 97 0.5 -2 -37 120 0 55 0 -10 0.37 0 1 -10 44 -10]. The fuzz trace tolerance does not account for sep, so this may be a defect in the check rather than in the solver. Files: riccati.go, mateq_fuzz_test.go.

data.title: EDGE: Mixsyn errors 'gamma not achievable' on numerically singular square static G
data.body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13). Hidden by FuzzMixsyn gate syNumericallySingularD.

[w13 #44 riccati/IZKUS3] Mixsyn errors on a square, numerically singular static G when the slow-weight pole is not near z=1, continuous or discrete. Repro: G = NewGain(D, dt) with D=[95.76575281793012 30.239088825335227 -40.061662395521715; -128.5980865880245 -71.08545020314747 -2.349984258481528; 153.96097157258234 107.80290777082504 44.625135203013] (σ = 258, 63, 2.7e-13), W1 = ss(0.9048374180359595, 1, 9.468676905422027, 0.5, dt), W2 = 0.01. Mixsyn returns 'γ = 1.4e12 not achievable' for dt = 1, 0.1, 1e-2 and 1e-4, and for the continuous analog W1 = ss(-0.1, 1, 9.95, 0.5). K=0 already achieves γ = max|W1| = 100, so the error is wrong whether or not D is exactly singular. Evidence: hinfGeneralPlant.riccatis accepts γ = 101, 200, 1e3 and 1e5, so bisection succeeds but every controller build or check fails, most likely in the D22 = -D loop shift or wellPosedQ. Base 81b761d fails the same way. The FuzzMixsyn gate syNumericallySingularD hides it. Files: hinfsyn_general.go (synthesize, wellPosedQ, loopShiftIllPosed), hinfsyn.go.

data.title: CORE: Sigma small singular values from Gram eigenvalues lose accuracy (sqrt(eps)*sigma1)
data.body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13).

[w13 #55 fuzz/MOI6LA] [CORE-ish] Sigma loses accuracy on small singular values. complexSVDWorkspace takes them from eigenvalues of the Gram matrix G^H*G (frequency_svd.go: fillBlock, singularValues), so the absolute error is about sqrt(eps)*sigma1 instead of eps*sigma1. Repro: FuzzFreqResponse seed 7 (discrete, n=4, m=p=2, dt=0.1, pair at |z|=1 with zeta=1e-8) at w=3.16227766: sys.Sigma and FRD.Sigma give sigma2=3.1155e-6, exact 1.2382e-6 (fzSingularValues via gonum SVD), sigma1=224.9. The relative error is about eps*(sigma1/sigma2)^2, so it is fully wrong once sigma1/sigma2 > 1e8. MATLAB sigma uses svd. Fix: complex SVD (e.g. a Golub-Kahan step on the 2x2 case) instead of Gram eigenvalues.

data.title: EDGE: FRDFeedback m>p absolute pivot tol: false ErrAlgebraicLoop at ||KG||>1e15
data.body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13).

[w13 #56 fuzz/MOI6LA] [EDGE] FRDFeedback with more plant inputs than outputs solves the m x m system I - sign*K*G with an absolute pivot tolerance (cSolveInPlace). It loses accuracy at a relative error of about eps*||KG|| and returns a false ErrAlgebraicLoop once ||KG|| exceeds about 1e15, although (I+GK)^-1 G is well-conditioned. Repro: G = [[3c+ci, -2c+0.5ci]] (1x2), K = [[0.3],[0.2]], sign = -1. At c=1e14 the relative error is 4e-3; at c=1e15 it is 20%; at c>=1e16 it returns ErrAlgebraicLoop. The exact answer is G/(1+GK), about 4.63-1.71i. Files: frd.go FRDFeedback, frequency.go cSolveInPlace. Fix: solve the smaller p x p I - sign*G*K when p < m, or use a relative pivot test.

data.title: CORE: internal-delay FreqResponse wrong near open-loop poles moved by delay loop (evalFrLFTInto)
data.body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13). Fallback to frozen/closed-loop solve only on hard error; need ill-conditioning trigger. Distinct from HFKNLV.

[w13 #57 fuzz/MOI6LA] [EDGE] Internal-delay FreqResponse evaluates G11 + G12*Delta*(I - G22*Delta)^-1*G21 from the open-loop resolvent, so it loses about eps*cond(sI-A) relative accuracy where the delay loop moves a plant pole. The closed-loop condition is only about 25 there. Repro: FuzzFreqResponseInternalDelay seed 15 (seed 7 with Tau=2 samples: discrete, dt=0.1, pair at |z|=1 with zeta=1e-8, b2 = first column of B, c2[i] = 0.5*sin(i+0.9)) at w=3.16227766: relative error 1.5e-8 against an exact solve of the A + Delta*b2*c2^T pencil. Continuous case: seed 2 (zeta=10^-9.5, w=sqrt(10), tau=0.3) gives 4.4e-8 relative. The discrete absorbed-state fallback (evalFrLFTInto) only triggers when I - H22*Delta is ill-conditioned, not when H itself is near a pole. Fix: solve the closed-loop pencil sI - A - B2*Delta*(I - D22*Delta)^-1*C2 directly when H is ill-conditioned.

[w13 #65 fuzz/review] Additional evidence for the existing reviewer followup, 'internal-delay FreqResponse loses accuracy at open-loop plant poles that the delay loop moves'. Files: frequency.go:775 evalFrLFTInto (open-loop H, then G11 + G12·Δ·(I − G22Δ)⁻¹·G21) and frequency_pole.go:372 evalFrLFTFrozenInto. The accurate frozen path is reached only when bd.evalInto errors, which it does not do for a near-zero or near-unit-circle pole. In the discrete case the absorbedSolver refine gate did not trigger. Repro A, continuous integrator at DC: fzDecode(t, 0x3a, [-20 -99.9 41 -45 60.333333333333336 -45 -26.666666666666668 -13.45 42 -10 -4.3757142857142854 8.666666666666666 -10 -163 -10 -0.05228787452803376]) gives n=1, m=2, p=3, A=[1e-13], tau=0.887, b2=B[:,0], c2=[0.3438]. At ω=0, s.System(t, fzSysOpts{Delays:true, Internal:true}).FreqResponse returns entry [3] = -80736 against an exact -80681.65 (rel 6.7e-4). All six entries are off by 1e-4 to 6.7e-4 relative. The closed-loop point condition is 1 and the oracle bound is 7.5e-9 to 2.7e-7, against misses of 1e2 to 5e2. Repro B, discrete: fzDecode(t, 0x41, [-4 85 0 33 0 0 -32 0 -2 -2.5 0.037 -13 36 -13 -60 -0.2614393726401688]) gives n=2, dt=0.01, eig 1±1e-6i, tau=1 sample. At ω=1.0000000001e-4 the result is -360400.8+2.35930e6i against an exact -378293.08+2.39261e6i (rel 1.56e-2, cond 2.79e6, bound 0.535, miss 3.8e4). The adjacent ω=1e-4 is correct to 1.5e-11. Oracle: exact rational solve of (xI − A − Δ·b2·c2ᵀ)X = B in fzFRInternalOracle. Fastest repro: go test -run XXX -fuzz FuzzFreqResponseInternalDelay -fuzztime 60s . fails within about 1s. A 120s probe on the old code hid about 935 such misses at condOL=1, plus misses up to rel 0.3 at condOL ≥ 1e13.

[w13 #67 fuzz/review0] [EDGE] Internal-delay FreqResponse loses 7+ digits at an open-loop plant pole that the delay loop moves. This may already be filed by MOI6LA (its 'known:' skip reason); I could not confirm from the truncated summary. Files: frequency.go:775 evalFrLFTInto, frequency_pole.go:372 evalFrLFTFrozenInto. Mechanism: the code evaluates the open-loop H first and only falls back to the frozen closed-loop solve on a hard error, never when H is ill-conditioned. Repro 1 (continuous): run FuzzFreqResponseInternalDelay with the fzFRCheckKnown skip disabled on kind=0x72 vals=[-0.6786402423930551 13 -0.8522801975522336 11.64528661442717 -40 9.730159100767608 -5.7124287797345685 0.8515788906023601 -1.8699414019192915 -0.9009541575928393 0.6904845230869261 -1.8615858804687453 0.37193006986806204 -10 -10 -0.9291681166465303]. That model is n=3, m=2, p=3, with an undamped pole at ω=0.2095847879716648 and tau about 0.118. At ω=0.2095847881812496 the relative error is 3.47e-7 (|Δ|=1.18e-7, |h|=0.339) against the exact big.Rat closed-loop solve, whose point condition is 8.52 and whose first-order bound is 6.7e-13. Repro 2 (discrete, worse): kind=0xd7 vals=[-0.8603088727097932 4.928966109060965 -0.5305909486010396 13 -1.7603256926868887 13 5.5794598346733535 -0.5028651286615842 -1.6756909102435067 -9.522762649906602 -1.2934801749704727 -2.8222193382401946 0.1393351192955018 -10 -0.4596958443663803 0.02128779065627474]. That model is n=6, m=3, p=3, dt=0.0211, with pole pairs within 1e-5 of z=1. At ω=0.017364980811526754 the relative error is 1.27e-4 (|Δ|=1.68e-4, |h|=1.32) at closed-loop condition 1.43e4, with bound 2.6e-9. Both discrepancies are far above float64 rounding of the given coefficients. Suggested fix direction: switch to evalFrLFTFrozenInto when the open-loop solve is ill-conditioned (large H22 or a large residual), not only when it errors.

[w13 #68 fuzz/review1] [EDGE/CORE-ish] Internal-delay FreqResponse returns wrong values when the frequency point sits on a lightly damped open-loop pole but the closed loop is well conditioned. Repro: go test -run=FuzzFreqResponseInternalDelay with kind=0x41, vals=[-4 85 0 33 0 0 -32 0 -2 -2.5 0.037 -13 36 -13 -60 -0.2614393726401688]. This decodes to discrete dt=0.01, n=2, open-loop eig 1-5e-13 ± 1e-6i, internal delay tau=1 sample with b2=B and c2=0.5·sin(i-13), input delay 20, evaluated at ω=1.0000000001e-4. Library gives -360400.814+2359303.208i. The exact closed-loop value is -378293.080+2392607.289i, from a big.Rat solve of (zI−A−Δb2c2ᵀ)X=B times z^-20, which I re-derived independently with Python Fractions. That is a relative error of 1.6%, while the closed-loop condition is only 2.8e6. Cause: evalFrLFTInto (frequency.go:775-831) builds G11+G12Δ(1−G22Δ)⁻¹G21 from an open-loop solve with |G22|≈1.8e14. The bdSolver succeeds, so the frozen/closed-loop fallback is never taken, and the discrete refine gate xMax·(1+loopMax) > refineCondition·rhsMax does not fire. A plain complex128 LFT gives the same wrong value.

[w13 #69 fuzz/review2] [CORE] Discrete internal-delay FreqResponse returns a silently wrong finite value at a lightly damped open-loop pole. Repro: fzDecode(t, 0x41, [-3, 13, 0, 0, 77, 0, 0, 0, -2, -10, 0.37, -77, -10, -300, 72, -0.1307196863200844]) then s.System(t, fzSysOpts{Delays:true, Internal:true}). That gives n=2, m=p=1, dt=0.01, A=[0.9999999999499999 9.999999999777057e-06; -9.999999999727683e-06 0.9999999999499998], B=[-0.22547187812891345; -0.9990597137251606], C=[5.417961692372929e-07 -9.70531651649883e-07], D=0, and an internal delay of 1 sample with b2=B, c2=[-0.4997600792903656 -0.28305381844909017]. Call FreqResponse at w=0.001000000001 (the resonance times 1+1e-9). arm64 returns (0 - 1.944601535797119e-06i); amd64 returns (-2.235e-08 - 1.93715e-06i). The exact value is (-1.1938325831196937e-08 - 1.935222691114017e-06i): the real part is wrong by 100% (arm64) or about 87% (amd64), and |Δ|/|h| is 0.78% on arm64. Two independent references agree on the exact value. One is the exact big.Rat solve of the absorbed 3-state model [[A, b2],[c2ᵀ, 0]] at the library's z. The other is the library's own FreqResponse of that absorbed explicit model, which matches to 1e-15. The closed loop is well conditioned (cond about 3e5), so this is not a precision limit. The open-loop point is singular to working precision (cond 2.4e14), and evalFrLFTInto (frequency.go:775) keeps the H-then-LFT result. Neither the bd.evalInto error nor the discrete refineCondition check sends it to absorbedSolver or evalFrLFTFrozenInto. Files: frequency.go (evalFrLFTInto, absorbedSolver) and frequency_pole.go (evalFrLFTFrozenInto). FuzzFreqResponseInternalDelay finds it within 2000 execs.

data.title: CORE: TransferFunction collapses delay-absorbed shift chains (num=[0], junk coefs)
data.body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13). Causes TunePID unstable-certified designs (see TunePID certification task).

[w13 #58 fuzz/QNALQV] CORE: System.TransferFunction collapses on delay-absorbed shift chains. Repro: sys := NewFromSlices(1,1,1,{a},{-0.9667981925794609},{-0.8568887533689471},{57.7675665396686},1); sys.SetInputDelay({k}); m := sys.AbsorbDelay(AbsorbAll); m.TransferFunction(nil). The true G is (57.77z+0.83)/(z^k(z-a)). With a=3.72e-44: k=1,2 give the correct num [57.77 0.83]; k=3,5 add junk leading coefficients; k=20 gives num=[0] and den [1, -3e-33]. With a=1e-3, k=10 already gives num=[0]. File: transfer.go (newRowRealizationConverter, via rationalTransferFunction). Consequence: pidTuningIdealStable sees G≡0, so TunePID returns an unstable design (next item).

data.title: CORE: TunePIDFRD evidence misses gain crossings its own samples resolve near resonance
data.body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13).

[w13 #61 fuzz/QNALQV] CORE: TunePIDFRD evidence misses gain crossings that its own samples resolve near a resonance. Repro: s := fzDecode(t, 0xa0, [0,1.5,0.3,4,-0.5,0,6.5,0,-1,-2,0.4,0.3,-10,-10,-10,-10]) (ζ=0.01 mode at about 2 rad/s); build the FRD from 600 log-spaced samples of the exact response over [1e-3, 1e3]; call TunePIDFRD(PID, CrossoverFrequency 0.1623). GainCrossovers holds only wc, yet adjacent FRD samples straddle |L|=1 at about 1.95 and 2.0, inside FrequencyBand [1e-3, 1e3]. The same happens at ζ=1e-3 and ζ=0. Likely cause: an FRD plant has no modes, so pidTuningCrossingsOn's evidence grid is not refined where the data shows a resonance, and AchievedPhaseMargin is overstated. A related variant: an explicit wc at an interpolation notch, where the samples on both sides have |L|>1, misses the crossing paired with wc. Files: pid_tuning_frd.go, pid_tuning.go (pidTuningCrossingsOn).
