data.title: CORE: Nyquist RHPZerosCL undercounts delayed-loop windings once wc*tau >~ 12 (darg aliasing)
data.body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13). Stability verdict unaffected; count wrong.

[w13 #66 fuzz/review] Nyquist RHPZerosCL undercounts windings of delayed loops once wc*tau >~ 12. Repro: sys,_ := NewFromSlices(1,1,1,[]float64{-1},[]float64{1},[]float64{50},[]float64{0},0); sys.SetInputDelay([]float64{1}); r,_ := sys.Nyquist(nil,0) gives RHPZerosCL=12. True count is 16: a dense 4M-point winding of 1+L on [0,1e5] and fzQuasiRHP agree. k=100 gives 16 vs 32; k<=20 is correct. Files: nyquist.go continuousHalf / nyquistPath.piece. segment uses about 10 points per decade, and piece bisects only when |darg(1+L)| > pi/4. Because darg is taken mod 2pi, a delay rotation of more than pi per base step aliases while |L|>1. Second suspected mechanism, not isolated: for D!=0 loops the early return `if p.sys.HasDelay() && closure != 0 { return nil }` skips the tail beyond wHi=1e3*max(|p|,1/tau). The stability verdict is unaffected (the count stays >0); only the number is wrong. In the fuzz this is gated by the narrow skip 'known: Nyquist aliases delay windings...' (fzFRSeeds last seed).

Found in wave 11 (branch fix/wave11).

SLOWDOWN, large but tail-only: on the crowded-integrator sweep (den = s^m * tiny real roots 1e-10..1e-5, sometimes a tiny complex pair, plus one 1e-3..1 pole; 2000 cases, seed PCG(77,fam)), wall clock went from 42s on base to 1728s on the branch (41x). Per-case IsStable timing over 300 cases: 7 cases (2.3%) slow down by more than 2x, and the total goes from 1.09s to 99.4s. Worst cases: c1/0061 (num=[0.009773188260746423 0.04489604727967583 0.020323824184367914 0.025820219062960566 0.025797214642228176 0.006646947890672527 0.0211410669887515], den=[1 0.003649069685529213 2.4765632608475385e-08 1.738276564214012e-13 1.3318081161564088e-18 -1.5346094421104906e-24 0 0], tau=0.106793461122868, verdict U, matching the oracle) goes from 0.7ms to 26.9s. c1/0038 goes from 32ms to 34s and errors on both base and branch. c0/0474 (num=[6.147829022841792 10.216695150719099 7.832026243562451 3.0229141413956437 0.6108677798926465 0.060153027952126306 0.002148638203899052], den=[1 -0.46362065820370524 -8.844990464639967e-06 -5.1310852993591357e-11 -8.387818654264996e-17 0 0 0], tau=0.0034389605674428696): IsStable goes from 0.30s to 23.3s and DiskMargin from 0.68s to 22.9s.

Slowdown attribution: with 9e0e49a's margin_ddeval.go placed on base's delay_nyquist.go, c0/0474 still takes 21.6s. So the cause is the DOIFRS pivot test alone, not the formCluster order change or axisAt. The cost per solve is small (BenchmarkDDSISOSolve response 2661 to 2999 ns, noise 2594 to 2811 ns, about 1.1x). The cost is in how many solves run: the dd solve now succeeds where base failed early, so refine walks through the crowded band. The profile shows about 28% of the time in poleSpacing, which calls descriptorPolicy.poles and then Dgeev again on every evalWithPoleLimit call, and about 25% in ddSISOSolve. These two are the places to cut cost. The shipped tests are only mildly affected (TestDelayNyquistClusterSweep 85s to 96s).

Descriptor certifier reach collapses in the band between a crowded origin cluster and the next real pole. Repro: at 9e0e49a, set formCluster back to ascending k for dd, then run TestDelayNyquistTinyRealPolesDDCircles case 1 (den 1, 0.006386411776610228, 3.0129825054035514e-08, 1.2921688426134479e-17, 0, 0, 0; tau 0.025221635624798323). The dd pass verifies a k=4 cluster at g≈1.09e-7; the walk then returns refineBudget (2,097,152 points) at ω≈4.7107e-6 after about 15 s. Certified spans in [1e-7, 4.7e-6] average about 2e-12 wide. Files: delay_nyquist.go (refine, certifiedSpan), delay_nyquist_cert.go (descriptorCertifier kind 0/1 models). Descending k in the dd pass avoids it, but any walk that starts inside that band will hit the same budget wall.


Wave 12 reports folded in:

[w12 #22] No new defect. The certifier-reach collapse already filed in wave 11 (w11-fu.txt item: descriptor certifier reach collapses in the band between a crowded origin cluster and the next real pole; delay_nyquist.go refine/certifiedSpan, delay_nyquist_cert.go) is still present. Trying the outer dd radii first avoids it, but any walk that has to start inside that band still exhausts the 2M-point budget. New repro: c1/0277 (num=[11.804907045235103 47.69278444420078 78.93833711881778 56.554249325501495 20.364449939570378 4.073141801943374 0.4707595594277479 0.0310525592479381 0.0010784630364785225 1.5231794863841214e-05], den=[1 -0.030506554427827935 5.2038982663217025e-08 -8.555476402942147e-14 1.4908513010377137e-19 -4.276994673844071e-28 1.8994237953309433e-37 -2.30930559019089e-47 0 0 0], tau=0.012199028614811678). With formCluster's dd order set back to {0.5,0.25,0.75}, IsStable fails after about 50s; the S-model reach near ω≈3e-4 is about 1e-12.

[w12 #25] Pre-existing extreme slowness on crowded-integrator delay loops (both revisions): DiskMargin takes over 145s or does not finish in 150s. Repro c1/1225 (rand.NewPCG(20261019,1225) with the review generator) times out on both revisions. Explicit repro c1/1117: num=[-0.012235734044675426 -0.006311583925569351 0.02414059228419912 -0.008061845117263832 0.00512661893265594 0.010735185448027559 -0.0008198734917113229], den=[1 0.011355350040403025 -7.55495339499703e-08 8.009233485927711e-12 -4.209496182030594e-17 -1.9086774397679433e-23 9.940606728217147e-29 0], tau=0.0006115707778961484 (oracle 3 RHP roots): DiskMargin took 149.5s on base 2e4a07d, and IsStable also hit the 150s limit. Files: delay_nyquist.go (refine/clusterWinding), margin.go (DiskMargin).

[w12 #29] Pre-existing slow fail-closed case: num=[0.37252309338771605 0.4625825403441033 0.9274824381636989 0.8389534845815284 0.004072616333200653 -0.14458113372741474 4.1608923438942696e-06], den=[1 0.0077345812020016055 3.193020496185404e-08 8.971080898815777e-14 3.7045363670280857e-19 -6.605723732890916e-28 0 0], tau=0.001695591587321757 (double integrator, real poles 1.8e-9, -4.1e-6, -0.0077, pair at 3.4e-6i with Re +1.3e-11). Oracle gives 4 RHP roots. IsStable, DiskMargin and HinfNorm all error on both base and branch, taking about 255s for the three calls. It fails closed, but the error is slow.


Wave 13 reports folded in:

[w13 #5] Perf of the FreqResponse fallback path: review2 a PID (num {1.6478992314667082e-12}, den {1,-3.9988962961964294,5.996689296298131,-3.9966897039442033,0.998896703842506}, dt 0.01) took about 3 ms on base (returning an error) and now takes about 2.5 s to return a design. In the profile, 56% of CPU is poleSpacing -> descriptorPolicy.poles -> Eigen.Factorize, run on every unresolved sample, twice: once in sisoEval.at's gated solve (margin.go evalWithPoleLimitGated) and once in pidtunePlantPoint.at's evalWithPoleLimit. Caching the poles would fix most of it. Files: frequency_pole.go, margin.go (other track).

[w13 #53] Slow Nyquist walk around clusters of near-axis poles (performance, also on base 690c75a). In both triple-pair cases, the walk from the axis indentation evaluates about 1.4M-2M points over ω in [1e-11, 5e-7], far below the poles at 1.25e-5, before clusterWinding resolves the count with a 481-point walk. So IsStable, HinfNorm and DiskMargin each take about 50-60s on arm64 and roughly 2x that under amd64. Repro: case A in delay_nyquist_triple_test.go, time l.nyquist(0.5). Possible remedy: try clusterWinding before the full-budget walk when the axis poles are merged, or give the first walk a smaller budget. Files: delay_nyquist.go (refine/winding/clusterWinding).

Found in wave 10 (PR pending, branch fix/wave10).

Perf (CR7GLM, caused by AUOTFB): newPidtuneGate now runs on every automatic Pidtune call. It evaluates the plant about 3000 times (sens grid about 230 points/decade, cross grid 100/decade, no shared points, band floor*1e-3 to wc*1e3). Result: about 8x slower on BenchmarkPidtune_PI/PID/PIDF (93us to 760us, 25KB to 388KB/op) and +66% on the continuous-delay sweep. Options: share or interpolate the sens and cross plant samples, cheaper pole-residue evaluation of the SISO plant on the grids, or lazy top-down |S| scanning. Files: pidtune.go (newPidtuneGate, pidtuneGate.sensitivityOver, crossExcess). Repro: go run ./scripts/benchcmp -base 8cfed86 -candidate 027664e -bench Pidtune.

Pidtune slowdown on simple plants from 027664e (AUOTFB first-design gate). Repro: go run ./scripts/benchcmp -base 8cfed86 -candidate 027664e -bench Pidtune. Evidence, 8cfed86 to HEAD: Pidtune_PI 80 us to 711 us (+787%), PID +836%, PIDF +751%, PidtuneFastSampled/O2 42 us to 797 us (+1795%), O5 +429%, Delayed/PI +185%, Delayed/PD 1.0 ms to 15 ms (+1358%), Delayed/PIDF +142%; B/op 25 KB to 388 KB, allocs/op +42% to +60% (Delayed/PD +2190%, of which my commits recover 8.6%). The 027664e-vs-HEAD benchcmp shows my commits leave time unchanged, so this all comes from 027664e. Cause: every automatic first design now builds newPidtuneGate, which samples about 9+ decades ([floor*1e-3, wc*1e3]) even when the design then passes. Files: pidtune.go (Pidtune, run.design(wc, sign, auto), newPidtuneGate). Narrowing the band or building the gate lazily could change gate verdicts, so this is an owner decision; not fixed.

Pidtune small automatic calls still cost about 470us vs 77us on 8cfed86 (Pidtune_PI/PID/PIDF, FastSampled ~2.6x). Cause: AUOTFB gates every auto first design on the full back-off gate grid, [floor*1e-3, wc*1e3] at 1% steps (about 2100 plant solves, pidtune.go newPidtuneGate). Lowering it means building the first design's grid lazily or narrowing it, which changes verdicts on some plants; that needs an owner decision.

Perf: BenchmarkPidtune_Delayed/PD (0.3s-1/(s+1)^4, input delay 5, PD, wc=0) is 1.1-1.2ms on base and about 18-28ms now. The gated first design (|S| 7.6) fails, all 60 back-off steps run gate checks and fail, then the ungated first design is returned as the fallback. A faster failing gate path or an earlier stop (e.g. when |S| rises steadily as wc drops) would recover this. File: pidtune.go (Pidtune back-off loop).

Perf (minor, existing pattern): on the reflected-delay path, r.screened(wc) and checkPidtuneStability each call screen.at(wc, family), which builds pidTuningDelayStability state twice per step that reaches Nyquist. The same double call happens on the non-delay gated path (r.gated(pid, wc, r.screened(wc))). Files: pidtune.go (pidtuneRun.check), pid_tuning.go (pidStabilityScreen.at).

BenchmarkPidtune_BackoffFail/GateP is +7% (3.52 to 3.77 ms) after the crossover scan moved to the finer |S| grid (16add00). Repro: benchcmp -base b0e01b5 -candidate 9b2e8d4 -bench ^BenchmarkPidtune. Most of it is bisection and golden-section refinement calls into the memoized p.at during back-off steps that fail anyway.


Wave 13 reports folded in:

[w13 #60] CORE (perf): MaxEvaluations does not bound TunePID runtime on delayed lightly damped plants. Repro: s := fzDecode(t, 0x80, [0,3,0.3,4,0,0,6,0,-1,-3,0.8,-3.5,-10,52,-10,-10]) gives modes ζ=0.1 at 1 rad/s and ζ=0.01 at 2 rad/s, with a 19.95 s output delay. TunePID(PIDF, MaxEvaluations:512) takes 51 s and returns Unattainable. With damp=5 (ζ=1e-3) it takes 169 s. With a 3.16 s delay it takes 0.3 s. Pidtune on the same plant takes 4 ms and returns a design. Related: Pidtune takes about 50 s on fzDecode(0x80, [6,11,0.3,0.5,0,0,6,-7,-0.5,-30,0.2,0.5,38,-100,-10,-10]) (a ζ=1e-5 mode at 1e4 rad/s, 20 s input delay). The likely cost is the Nyquist screen (pidTuningDelayStability). The fuzz bodies skip these inputs (fzPidSystem and fzPidTuneSlow).

Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12).

[w12 #60 pidtune/review1] Crossover is still 3-5x off on discrete integrators that rounding scatters into a cluster of conjugate or comparable-distance poles (the integrator is not isolated), outside FI3ZIB's scope. Example from a seeded (z-1)·∏(z-e^(-a·dt)) sweep: nearest pole 2.07e-3 from z=1 with a second pole at the same distance (a conjugate pair); plantCrossoverFreq gives 0.1035 vs 0.0304 for half the slowest pole. Other examples: 0.50 vs 0.163 at ratio 1.22, and 0.245 vs 0.059 at ratio 1.66. These cases have no gain crossover and the same value on base. File: pidtune.go pidtuneIntegratingCrossover / pidtuneSlowestRoot. Designs stay stable.


Wave 13 reports folded in:

[w13 #10] Pidtune errors in every family when AllMargin's first gain crossing is at rounding level (pidtune.go plantCrossoverSource takes all.GainCrossFreqs[0] as wc). Repro on 690c75a: num [4.905554616319012e-13], den [1 -2.310228431318273 1.8436939371933398 -0.6052316064965124 0.07495077124036684 -0.0032273933261639186 4.2722707242222904e-05], dt 0.1, built with TransferFunc.StateSpace. AllMargin gives a gain crossing at 3.17e-11 rad/s, and P, I, PI, PD, PDF, PID and PIDF all return ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable at wc=3.17e-11. Neighbouring plants from the same generator (TestPidtuneRoundedZeroDCIntegrator, PCG(11,3)) whose crossing AllMargin misses get stable designs at wc of about 0.5 times the slowest pole; MATLAB pidtune returns a controller. This is also why sisoEval.at keeps its snapped +Inf (S2RNHI): with that value replaced, 88 of 300 sweep plants flip to errors.

[w13 #64] EDGE: Pidtune and TunePID return ErrInvalidArgument 'no gain crossover, bandwidth or nonzero pole to infer a crossover from' for biproper plants with |G|>1 at all frequencies whose integrator poles sit about 1e-8 off z=1, well above rounding. Repro: discrete Dt=0.1, A=[1.0000000116488188 1.8099675739185816e-08; -7.753540390871093e-09 0.9999999883511813], B=[0.6979798590772273 -0.5033119781891744], C=[1.4839794477710827e-06 -4.772606107217278e-07], D=520.8700127245612, Pidtune(PI, wc=0). The exact integrator takes the integrating path and gets a design. File: pidtune.go (plantCrossoverSource: integratingDCGain and pidtuneIntegratorCluster disagree).

Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12). Common root: staircase tolerances are absolute/normwise (tol*||A||, |[A;C_i]|) and balancedABC balances A alone, so tiny or inflated B/C cause dropped states and TF(k*sys) != k*TF(sys). Likely fix: joint balancing of [A B; C 0] as MATLAB does plus scale-relative rank tests. Previous patches regressed testdata/fuzz/FuzzDCGain/0adb1555e65760b9 on amd64/arm64 (see #30). Check MATLAB minreal on #35 before deciding.

[w12 #30 dcgain/E2AY73] TransferFunction drops controllable z=1 modes (transfer.go, balancedABC/convert). Repro: NewFromSlices(3,1,1, A=[1 0 -3.1622776601683795; 0 1 -3.1622776601683795; 0 0 eps], B=[-0.38211320287195655 0.7882242424655154 0.8038113259779769]', C=[-0.9291407314223547 0.6502534890410231 0.5087003937751763], D=0, dt=100). With eps in {1e-20, 1e-40, 1e-69}, TF den = [1 -eps] and MinimalOrder = 1. Exact: order 2, with a pole at z=1 of residue c1b1+c2b2+(c1+c2)a*b3/(1-eps) = 1.576. Evidence: Dgebal scales state 3 by about 1/eps, so B row 3 becomes about 1e20. controllabilityStaircase gives NCont=2 on the unbalanced model and 1 on the balanced one. With eps=1e-12 the balanced path keeps the order but the residue is off by 4e-4 relative. Two patches each regressed fuzz input testdata/fuzz/FuzzDCGain/0adb1555e65760b9 (||A|| about 1e43): falling back to the unbalanced staircase (broke amd64), and clamping the scaling by B/C (broke arm64). Likely needs joint balancing of [A B; C 0], as MATLAB does.

[w12 #35 dcgain/JBKTCQ] MinimalRealization drops a tiny-but-nonzero B as uncontrollable. Repro: r,_ := (&TransferFunc{Num:[][][]float64{{{-8.70643320022765e-16, 2.9186581655941266e-16, 1.3545850066477854e-16}}}, Den:[][]float64{{1, -5.609886783435264, 13.099973168748164, -16.29841103348229, 11.394314088807377, -4.243853507030152, 0.6578640663921657}}, Dt:0.01}).StateSpace(); r.Sys.MinimalRealization() gives order 0 (TransferFunction now gives order 6). Cause: same absolute staircase floor tol·‖A‖ (staircase.go:99) against ‖B‖ about 1e-15. Files: minimal.go, staircase.go; CtrbF/ObsvF (ctrbobsv.go) likely the same. I have not checked MATLAB minreal's behaviour on this model; it decides whether this is a bug.

[w12 #42 dcgain/review1] TransferFunction drops a well-defined first-order system when norm(A) is huge (pre-existing, base and branch). Repro: NewFromSlices(1,1,1, A=[-1e155], B=[1], C=[1], D=[0], 0).TransferFunction(nil) gives Num [[[0]]] / Den [[1]], instead of 1/(s+1e155) as MATLAB tf(ss) gives. DCGain is correct (1e-155). Same for A=-1e200, and for a 2x2 triangular A with entries ~1e150. Files: transfer.go rowRealizationConverter (staircase / numerator trimming relative to norm(A)).

Wave 13 attempt (branch fix/tf-wave13 commits 8c2ccf7 4a73116 aeac0be 2531f51) NOT merged; final review findings:

MinimalRealization / Reduce(ReduceAll) regressed from base-correct to non-minimal, keeping exactly unobservable states with unstable hidden eigenvalues (stable->unstable flip in the returned realization). Cause: scaleColumnsPow2 (staircase.go:106) scales each column of the first block toward ‖A‖. In Reduce's observability stage that block is Ccᵀ, taken from the controllability rotation. A column that is small because its large uncontrollable content was rotated out still carries noise at eps·‖C_full‖. Scaling that column up by about 2^9 lifts the noise above absFloor = n²eps‖Ac‖_F, which itself does not move, so in effect the test becomes relative per column rather than MATLAB's absolute default. The same mechanism applies to user CtrbF/ObsvF calls with a small, cancellation-derived column.
Repro (exact structure, no rotation, Ts=0.1, n=5,m=2,p=2): NewFromSlices(5,2,2, a=[0.8684323205674875 -0.6049616753433141 -0.817025610149589 0 0; 0 0.5112361371882209 -1.665579513685 0 0; 0 0.4426963353960824 2.2287867502570378 0 0; 1.450755586734131 0.5926180571361175 -1.003801815806515 -0.7392334214012152 2.598303245115053; 0.019516845706728403 0.7670269935617764 2.019276442042413 1.380736914734296 0.5174218017098235] (row-major), b=[0.7453432469816224 -0.1349637189736732; 0 0; 0 0; 0.2391746712711118 1.270569808451821; -1.6807270924517255 1.013393545638635], c=[0.10373234420450061 1.1189760895011407 -0.6387064209174134 0 0; 0.010176619760267125 -0.40735317004013655 0.15355429034927204 0 0], D=0, 0.1). Exact minimal order 1: states 1-2 have zero B rows and are never driven; states 3-4 have zero C columns and never feed states 0-2. Base 690c75a: MinimalRealization order 1, eig 0.868. Branch: order 3, eig {1.885, -2.106, 0.868}, two of them outside the unit circle. Response error is 4e-16, so only the order and stability are wrong. Same result on amd64. [w13 #23] Possible follow-up for the coordinator (a design gap, not a bug I found): TransferFunction has no structural (sminreal-style) pre-pass. When the rotation noise on a structurally zero subdiagonal is around 50-200·eps·‖A‖ (seen in models with diagonal scaling up to 10^±4, e.g. my sweep cases 5446 and 6438), no eps-scaled floor can drop it without also dropping real weak couplings. So structurally hidden states can still be kept and their poles land in the TF denominator. MATLAB-style structural elimination per output row (Sminreal already exists in sminreal.go) would remove them exactly. Left alone because it is outside this finding's scope.

[w13 #26] Reduce/CtrbF default tol is tighter than MATLAB. The default n²·eps·‖A‖_F is below MATLAB ctrbf's 10·n·‖A‖₁·eps (and minreal's documented sqrt(eps)) for small n. Repro: sweep-style plain model with exact structural hidden states, e.g. case 2320 (N=4, m=1, p=2, R=1): ReduceAll keeps 2 states because a noise singular value of 1.240e-15 is above the 1.226e-15 floor. Evidence: across 600 plain Gaussian models, ReduceAll over-counts 17 (2.8%) with the default and 6 with the MATLAB ctrbf tol, with no under-counts in any category. Files: staircase.go controllabilityStaircase, minimal.go Reduce. This is an owner/MATLAB-parity call, not strictly a pre-existing bug.

Branch HinfNorm 10322113722.95 at ω=9.1206258284e-4, while fzExactResponse at ω=9.1206258415e-4 gives 10322135171.8. Files: norms.go certifyPeak/candidatePeak. Conditioning is ~551, so this may be acceptable; filing is optional.

[w12 #77 fuzz/review] The norms.go change touches the library under-report the reviewer already filed (FuzzLinfNorm/FuzzHinfNorm, kind=0xc0 crasher). Climbing the sampled peak fixes the case where the true peak lies next to a grid sample. It does not fix the root cause: on stiff models (pole spread around 1e9), unstructured QZ in hamiltonianWS.hasImagEigs can still push genuine γ-crossings outside nearAxisTol=0.1. In norms.go hasImagEigs, the pencil eigenvalues at γ=4.8668e-5 for this model came out as (-5.0e-4+3.88e-3i)/0.9998, a ratio of 0.13. So a narrow peak between grid samples on a stiff model could still be under-reported. Possible fixes: balance the pencil (Dggbal 'B') before Dggev, or scale nearAxisTol to the eigenvalue condition. No concrete repro beyond the fixed crasher yet; the 5-minute fuzz runs found none.

Second instance: kind 0xc9 vals {0.6413769500533629, 3.225485305446771, -6.920211238942823, 5.194656803421655, 2.5649118927522707, 5.9960354875740425, 0.7321123327177131, 0, 0.8225408446783429, -8.084719954920434, -0.12421061853394999, -14.98391252021944, -10, -10, -10, -10} gives 10252.94430 vs exact 10252.94379 (+5e-8). Files: norms.go sigmaEvaluator / certifyPeak.

data.title: GEEI33 follow-up: unreviewed Care re-solve commits 1e4d9df bc621dc (branch fix/riccati-wave13 detached tip)
data.body:
In wave 13 the riccati track's last refix (1e4d9df, bc621dc: Care plain-Hamiltonian failure rescue by cost scaling, re-solve of an inaccurate plain-Care X at firstSigma) landed on a detached HEAD after the final review. The review passed 8e01b2f without them, so they were NOT merged in the wave 13 PR.
Review them and land them: cherry-pick bc621dc and its parent 1e4d9df onto main, run a seeded base-vs-branch Care sweep against the Newton oracle, and run the amd64 tests.

Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12). Common root: staircase tolerances are absolute/normwise (tol*||A||, |[A;C_i]|) and balancedABC balances A alone, so tiny or inflated B/C cause dropped states and TF(k*sys) != k*TF(sys). Likely fix: joint balancing of [A B; C 0] as MATLAB does plus scale-relative rank tests. Previous patches regressed testdata/fuzz/FuzzDCGain/0adb1555e65760b9 on amd64/arm64 (see #30). Check MATLAB minreal on #35 before deciding.

[w12 #30 dcgain/E2AY73] TransferFunction drops controllable z=1 modes (transfer.go, balancedABC/convert). Repro: NewFromSlices(3,1,1, A=[1 0 -3.1622776601683795; 0 1 -3.1622776601683795; 0 0 eps], B=[-0.38211320287195655 0.7882242424655154 0.8038113259779769]', C=[-0.9291407314223547 0.6502534890410231 0.5087003937751763], D=0, dt=100). With eps in {1e-20, 1e-40, 1e-69}, TF den = [1 -eps] and MinimalOrder = 1. Exact: order 2, with a pole at z=1 of residue c1b1+c2b2+(c1+c2)a*b3/(1-eps) = 1.576. Evidence: Dgebal scales state 3 by about 1/eps, so B row 3 becomes about 1e20. controllabilityStaircase gives NCont=2 on the unbalanced model and 1 on the balanced one. With eps=1e-12 the balanced path keeps the order but the residue is off by 4e-4 relative. Two patches each regressed fuzz input testdata/fuzz/FuzzDCGain/0adb1555e65760b9 (||A|| about 1e43): falling back to the unbalanced staircase (broke amd64), and clamping the scaling by B/C (broke arm64). Likely needs joint balancing of [A B; C 0], as MATLAB does.

[w12 #35 dcgain/JBKTCQ] MinimalRealization drops a tiny-but-nonzero B as uncontrollable. Repro: r,_ := (&TransferFunc{Num:[][][]float64{{{-8.70643320022765e-16, 2.9186581655941266e-16, 1.3545850066477854e-16}}}, Den:[][]float64{{1, -5.609886783435264, 13.099973168748164, -16.29841103348229, 11.394314088807377, -4.243853507030152, 0.6578640663921657}}, Dt:0.01}).StateSpace(); r.Sys.MinimalRealization() gives order 0 (TransferFunction now gives order 6). Cause: same absolute staircase floor tol·‖A‖ (staircase.go:99) against ‖B‖ about 1e-15. Files: minimal.go, staircase.go; CtrbF/ObsvF (ctrbobsv.go) likely the same. I have not checked MATLAB minreal's behaviour on this model; it decides whether this is a bug.

[w12 #42 dcgain/review1] TransferFunction drops a well-defined first-order system when norm(A) is huge (pre-existing, base and branch). Repro: NewFromSlices(1,1,1, A=[-1e155], B=[1], C=[1], D=[0], 0).TransferFunction(nil) gives Num [[[0]]] / Den [[1]], instead of 1/(s+1e155) as MATLAB tf(ss) gives. DCGain is correct (1e-155). Same for A=-1e200, and for a 2x2 triangular A with entries ~1e150. Files: transfer.go rowRealizationConverter (staircase / numerator trimming relative to norm(A)).

[w12 #72 fuzz/AULHZC] TransferFunction minimality depends on output scaling, so TF(k*sys) != k*TF(sys) at O(1). The row observability tolerance (ssToTFRow / ObservabilityTol, transfer.go:287) is relative to |[A; C_i]|. Repro: A=[-3.162277660168379e-14, 9.486832980505137e-14; -9.486832980505139e-14, -3.162277660168378e-14], B=[-0.9667981925794609; -0.01238866346289056], C=[856888.7533689471, 210795.79943077973], D=0, continuous. Result: MinimalOrder 1, and at x=9.32e-14+3.62e-14i tf = -6.14e18+1.78e18i against an exact -3.62e18+1.15e17i. Scaling C by 1e-6 gives order 2 and the correct value. FuzzSSToTF accepts this because its bound uses nu = max(|A|,|B|,|C_i|), a normwise backward-error model.

[w12 #73 fuzz/AULHZC] TransferFunction balances A alone with Dgebal (balancedABC, transfer.go:249, from the BLYSOP fix), which can inflate B or C by about 1e13; the staircase then drops states that matter. Repro: discrete Ts=1, n=4, A=[0.7214294796518126 -0.3045829930861377 -0.00041016443744005306 -4.0917982190015664e-18; -0.3045829930861377 0.12979857966165384 -0.0009701301233358639 1.7299845394387501e-18; -0.00041016443744002493 -0.0009701301233358758 0.0010844921094764262 2.026087561733075e-44; -8.123803525336596e-45 -1.9214602234118876e-44 -2.0260875617330751e-44 -2.319905867103475e-44], B=[-0.9667981925794609; -0.01238866346289056; 0.9601702866503661; 0.5260775173811046], C=[-8.568887533689471e-07 -2.1079579943077972e-07 9.931849187581927e-07 -4.3137684497061916e-07], D=0. The Dgebal scale is [1 1 1 1.14e-13]. TF order is 2 while MinimalRealization gives 3. At x=1.1613383804294024+0.06822811668058017i, tf = 2.72084e-6 against ss EvalFr = 2.72149e-6, a 2.4e-4 relative error in the dynamic part. FuzzSSToTF skips this case only when its check would fail and the Dgebal scaling ratio (max/min) exceeds 1e6 (reason 'Dgebal scaling of A alone inflates B or C').


Wave 13 attempt (branch fix/tf-wave13 commits 8c2ccf7 4a73116 aeac0be 2531f51) NOT merged; final review findings:

MinimalRealization / Reduce(ReduceAll) regressed from base-correct to non-minimal, keeping exactly unobservable states with unstable hidden eigenvalues (stable->unstable flip in the returned realization). Cause: scaleColumnsPow2 (staircase.go:106) scales each column of the first block toward ‖A‖. In Reduce's observability stage that block is Ccᵀ, taken from the controllability rotation. A column that is small because its large uncontrollable content was rotated out still carries noise at eps·‖C_full‖. Scaling that column up by about 2^9 lifts the noise above absFloor = n²eps‖Ac‖_F, which itself does not move, so in effect the test becomes relative per column rather than MATLAB's absolute default. The same mechanism applies to user CtrbF/ObsvF calls with a small, cancellation-derived column.
Repro (exact structure, no rotation, Ts=0.1, n=5,m=2,p=2): NewFromSlices(5,2,2, a=[0.8684323205674875 -0.6049616753433141 -0.817025610149589 0 0; 0 0.5112361371882209 -1.665579513685 0 0; 0 0.4426963353960824 2.2287867502570378 0 0; 1.450755586734131 0.5926180571361175 -1.003801815806515 -0.7392334214012152 2.598303245115053; 0.019516845706728403 0.7670269935617764 2.019276442042413 1.380736914734296 0.5174218017098235] (row-major), b=[0.7453432469816224 -0.1349637189736732; 0 0; 0 0; 0.2391746712711118 1.270569808451821; -1.6807270924517255 1.013393545638635], c=[0.10373234420450061 1.1189760895011407 -0.6387064209174134 0 0; 0.010176619760267125 -0.40735317004013655 0.15355429034927204 0 0], D=0, 0.1). Exact minimal order 1: states 1-2 have zero B rows and are never driven; states 3-4 have zero C columns and never feed states 0-2. Base 690c75a: MinimalRealization order 1, eig 0.868. Branch: order 3, eig {1.885, -2.106, 0.868}, two of them outside the unit circle. Response error is 4e-16, so only the order and stability are wrong. Same result on amd64. Reduce(ReduceUncontrollable) gives 3 (correct). Its Cc has singular values [0.104, 1.07e-16]: the noise SV is 65x below the branch's own absFloor of about 7e-15, yet ObsvF(RU) returns K=[2 1] at tol 0 and [1] at tol≥1e-14. Under MATLAB's absolute obsvf default (10·n·‖A‖₁·eps ≈ 3e-14) it would be rejected. Sweep: 2400 seeded Kalman-structured models (core plus uncontrollable and unobservable blocks, mostly orthogonally rotated) compared against the structural oracle. ReduceAll was base-correct and branch-wrong in 41 cases (6 of them plain O(1) rotated models, 2 exact unrotated). Reduced realization stable->unstable in 57 cases. The ObsvF/RO regression in case 1560 has the same cause. Same signature in cases 85/129/314/530: ObsvF(RU) K=[2 1] at tol 0, [1] at 1e-14. ## Decision (advisor, 2026-10-20): apply |S| <= 4 to every TunePID family; no 58.5° PM floor
Rationale: TunePID's own contract already accepts the margin at wc0 only when |S| <= 4. The robust = tau > 0 asymmetry, which skips the |S| check on undelayed plants, has no justification. The 58.5° floor is Pidtune policy; TunePID is the explicit-target tool, the same philosophy as V7UW3M (explicit wc ungated).
- (a) Read tuneAt first. If robust=true also triggers back-off or search, add only the |S| check.
- (b) On |S| failure, return the same error shape the delayed path returns today: PIDTuningError wrapping unattainable, with the |S| value.
- (c) In the sweep, a base design with |S| > 4 that becomes an error is an allowed flip. A base design with |S| <= 4 that flips is BLOCKING.
- Separate smell to investigate: the PD gets opposite-sign gains (Kp 0.5639, Kd -1.667e5) because gainSign becomes 0 once the integrator is recognised.
